1. //! Hybrid classical/post-quantum signatures
2. //!
3. //! All long-term signatures in SDIS use hybrid constructions that combine
4. //! Ed25519 (classical) and ML-DSA (post-quantum). Verification requires
5. //! BOTH signatures to be valid.
6. //!
7. //! # Security Model
8. //!
9. //! The hybrid construction provides defense-in-depth:
10. //! - If Ed25519 is broken (e.g., by quantum computers), ML-DSA provides security
11. //! - If ML-DSA has an undiscovered weakness, Ed25519 provides security
12. //! - An attacker must break BOTH algorithms to forge a signature
13. //!
14. //! # Size Considerations
15. //!
16. //! | Component | Size |
17. //! |-----------|------|
18. //! | Ed25519 signature | 64 bytes |
19. //! | ML-DSA signature | 3293 bytes |
20. //! | **Hybrid signature** | **~3.4 KB** |
21. //! | Ed25519 public key | 32 bytes |
22. //! | ML-DSA public key | 1952 bytes |
23. //! | **Hybrid public key** | **~2 KB** |
24. 
25. use ed25519_dalek::{Signature as Ed25519Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey};
26. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
27. use zeroize::{Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop};
28. 
29. use crate::ml_dsa::{MlDsaKeypair, MlDsaPublicKey, MlDsaSignature};
30. use crate::{CryptoError, Result};
31. 
32. /// Hybrid signature combining Ed25519 and ML-DSA
33. ///
34. /// Both signatures must verify for the hybrid signature to be valid.
35. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
36. pub struct HybridSignature {
37.     /// Classical Ed25519 signature (64 bytes)
38.     pub classical: Vec<u8>,
39.     /// Post-quantum ML-DSA signature (~3309 bytes)
40.     pub pq: Vec<u8>,
41. }
42. 
43. impl HybridSignature {
44.     /// Ed25519 signature size
45.     pub const CLASSICAL_SIZE: usize = 64;
46. 
47.     /// Create from component signatures
48.     pub fn new(classical: Ed25519Signature, pq: MlDsaSignature) -> Self {
49.         Self {
50.             classical: classical.to_bytes().to_vec(),
51.             pq: pq.as_bytes().to_vec(),
52.         }
53.     }
54. 
55.     /// Create from raw bytes
56.     pub fn from_bytes(classical: &[u8], pq: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
57.         if classical.len() != Self::CLASSICAL_SIZE {
58.             return Err(CryptoError::InvalidSignature(format!(
59.                 "Ed25519 signature must be {} bytes, got {}",
60.                 Self::CLASSICAL_SIZE,
61.                 classical.len()
62.             )));
63.         }
64. 
65.         // Validate pq signature format
66.         let _ = MlDsaSignature::from_bytes(pq)?;
67. 
68.         Ok(Self {
69.             classical: classical.to_vec(),
70.             pq: pq.to_vec(),
71.         })
72.     }
73. 
74.     /// Verify the hybrid signature
75.     ///
76.     /// Returns true only if BOTH classical and post-quantum signatures are valid.
77.     pub fn verify(&self, message: &[u8], public_key: &HybridPublicKey) -> bool {
78.         let classical_valid = self.verify_classical(message, &public_key.classical);
79.         let pq_valid = self.verify_pq(message, &public_key.pq);
80. 
81.         // BOTH must be valid
82.         classical_valid && pq_valid
83.     }
84. 
85.     /// Verify only the classical (Ed25519) signature
86.     pub fn verify_classical(&self, message: &[u8], public_key: &[u8]) -> bool {
87.         let pk_bytes: [u8; 32] = match public_key.try_into() {
88.             Ok(b) => b,
89.             Err(_) => return false,
90.         };
91. 
92.         let verifying_key = match VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&pk_bytes) {
93.             Ok(k) => k,
94.             Err(_) => return false,
95.         };
96. 
97.         let sig_bytes: [u8; 64] = match self.classical.as_slice().try_into() {
98.             Ok(b) => b,
99.             Err(_) => return false,
100.         };
101. 
102.         let signature = Ed25519Signature::from_bytes(&sig_bytes);
103. 
104.         verifying_key.verify(message, &signature).is_ok()
105.     }
106. 
107.     /// Verify only the post-quantum (ML-DSA) signature
108.     pub fn verify_pq(&self, message: &[u8], public_key: &MlDsaPublicKey) -> bool {
109.         let signature = match MlDsaSignature::from_bytes(&self.pq) {
110.             Ok(s) => s,
111.             Err(_) => return false,
112.         };
113. 
114.         MlDsaKeypair::verify(public_key, message, &signature)
115.     }
116. 
117.     /// Total size in bytes
118.     pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
119.         self.classical.len() + self.pq.len()
120.     }
121. 
122.     /// Serialize to bytes (classical || pq)
123.     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
124.         let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(self.size());
125.         bytes.extend_from_slice(&self.classical);
126.         bytes.extend_from_slice(&self.pq);
127.         bytes
128.     }
129. }
130. 
131. /// Hybrid public key combining Ed25519 and ML-DSA public keys
132. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
133. pub struct HybridPublicKey {
134.     /// Classical Ed25519 public key (32 bytes)
135.     pub classical: Vec<u8>,
136.     /// Post-quantum ML-DSA public key (~1952 bytes)
137.     pub pq: MlDsaPublicKey,
138. }
139. 
140. impl HybridPublicKey {
141.     /// Ed25519 public key size
142.     pub const CLASSICAL_SIZE: usize = 32;
143. 
144.     /// Create from component keys
145.     pub fn new(classical: VerifyingKey, pq: MlDsaPublicKey) -> Self {
146.         Self {
147.             classical: classical.as_bytes().to_vec(),
148.             pq,
149.         }
150.     }
151. 
152.     /// Create from raw bytes
153.     pub fn from_bytes(classical: &[u8], pq: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
154.         if classical.len() != Self::CLASSICAL_SIZE {
155.             return Err(CryptoError::InvalidKey(format!(
156.                 "Ed25519 public key must be {} bytes, got {}",
157.                 Self::CLASSICAL_SIZE,
158.                 classical.len()
159.             )));
160.         }
161. 
162.         // Validate classical key
163.         // SAFETY: We verified classical.len() == 32 above
164.         let classical_bytes: [u8; 32] = classical
165.             .try_into()
166.             .map_err(|_| CryptoError::InvalidKey("Classical key length mismatch".to_string()))?;
167.         let _ = VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&classical_bytes)
168.             .map_err(|e| CryptoError::InvalidKey(format!("Invalid Ed25519 public key: {e}")))?;
169. 
170.         let pq = MlDsaPublicKey::from_bytes(pq)?;
171. 
172.         Ok(Self {
173.             classical: classical.to_vec(),
174.             pq,
175.         })
176.     }
177. 
178.     /// Get classical public key as VerifyingKey
179.     pub fn classical_verifying_key(&self) -> Result<VerifyingKey> {
180.         let bytes: [u8; 32] = self
181.             .classical
182.             .as_slice()
183.             .try_into()
184.             .map_err(|_| CryptoError::InvalidKey("Invalid classical key length".to_string()))?;
185.         VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&bytes)
186.             .map_err(|e| CryptoError::InvalidKey(format!("Invalid Ed25519 public key: {e}")))
187.     }
188. 
189.     /// Total size in bytes
190.     pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
191.         self.classical.len() + self.pq.as_bytes().len()
192.     }
193. }
194. 
195. /// Hybrid keypair for signing
196. ///
197. /// Contains both classical (Ed25519) and post-quantum (ML-DSA) keypairs.
198. /// Secret keys are zeroized on drop for security.
199. #[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
200. pub struct HybridKeypair {
201.     /// Ed25519 signing key (zeroized on drop)
202.     #[zeroize(skip)]
203.     classical_signing: SigningKey,
204.     /// ML-DSA keypair
205.     #[zeroize(skip)]
206.     pq_keypair: MlDsaKeypair,
207. }
208. 
209. impl HybridKeypair {
210.     /// Generate a new hybrid keypair
211.     pub fn generate() -> Result<Self> {
212.         // Generate Ed25519 keypair
213.         let classical_signing = SigningKey::generate(&mut rand::rngs::OsRng);
214. 
215.         // Generate ML-DSA keypair
216.         let pq_keypair = MlDsaKeypair::generate()?;
217. 
218.         Ok(Self {
219.             classical_signing,
220.             pq_keypair,
221.         })
222.     }
223. 
224.     /// Create from seed bytes (deterministic generation)
225.     ///
226.     /// Both Ed25519 and ML-DSA keypairs are derived deterministically from the seed
227.     /// using HKDF. The same seed will always produce identical keypairs, enabling
228.     /// key recovery from a master seed.
229.     ///
230.     /// The seed must be at least 64 bytes:
231.     /// - First 32 bytes: Ed25519 seed (used directly)
232.     /// - Bytes 32-64: ML-DSA seed (passed to HKDF-based derivation)
233.     ///
234.     /// # Security
235.     ///
236.     /// The seed should be cryptographically random and stored securely.
237.     /// Anyone with the seed can regenerate all keypairs.
238.     pub fn from_seed(seed: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
239.         if seed.len() < 64 {
240.             return Err(CryptoError::InvalidKey(
241.                 "Seed must be at least 64 bytes".to_string(),
242.             ));
243.         }
244. 
245.         // Ed25519 from first 32 bytes (direct derivation)
246.         // SAFETY: We verified seed.len() >= 64 above
247.         let classical_seed: [u8; 32] = seed[..32]
248.             .try_into()
249.             .map_err(|_| CryptoError::InvalidKey("Seed slice conversion failed".to_string()))?;
250.         let classical_signing = SigningKey::from_bytes(&classical_seed);
251. 
252.         // ML-DSA from bytes 32-64 (deterministic via HKDF + ML-DSA seed)
253.         let pq_seed = &seed[32..64];
254.         let pq_keypair = MlDsaKeypair::from_seed(pq_seed)?;
255. 
256.         Ok(Self {
257.             classical_signing,
258.             pq_keypair,
259.         })
260.     }
261. 
262.     /// Sign a message with both algorithms
263.     ///
264.     /// # Errors
265.     ///
266.     /// Returns an error if ML-DSA signing fails (should not happen with valid keypair).
267.     pub fn sign(&self, message: &[u8]) -> Result<HybridSignature> {
268.         // Ed25519 signature
269.         let classical_sig = self.classical_signing.sign(message);
270. 
271.         // ML-DSA signature
272.         let pq_sig = self.pq_keypair.sign(message)?;
273. 
274.         Ok(HybridSignature::new(classical_sig, pq_sig))
275.     }
276. 
277.     /// Get the public key
278.     pub fn public_key(&self) -> HybridPublicKey {
279.         HybridPublicKey::new(
280.             self.classical_signing.verifying_key(),
281.             self.pq_keypair.public_key().clone(),
282.         )
283.     }
284. 
285.     /// Get the classical (Ed25519) verifying key
286.     pub fn classical_public(&self) -> VerifyingKey {
287.         self.classical_signing.verifying_key()
288.     }
289. 
290.     /// Get the post-quantum (ML-DSA) public key
291.     pub fn pq_public(&self) -> &MlDsaPublicKey {
292.         self.pq_keypair.public_key()
293.     }
294. 
295.     /// Sign with only Ed25519 (for ephemeral proofs)
296.     ///
297.     /// This is used for short-lived credentials where quantum resistance
298.     /// isn't necessary (e.g., 6-hour ephemeral QR proofs).
299.     pub fn sign_classical_only(&self, message: &[u8]) -> Ed25519Signature {
300.         self.classical_signing.sign(message)
301.     }
302. 
303.     /// Get the classical (Ed25519) secret key bytes
304.     ///
305.     /// WARNING: Handle with care - this exposes secret key material.
306.     /// Used for keystore serialization.
307.     pub fn classical_secret_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
308.         self.classical_signing.to_bytes()
309.     }
310. 
311.     /// Get the post-quantum (ML-DSA) secret key bytes
312.     ///
313.     /// WARNING: Handle with care - this exposes secret key material.
314.     /// Used for keystore serialization.
315.     pub fn pq_secret_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
316.         self.pq_keypair.secret_key_bytes()
317.     }
318. 
319.     /// Reconstruct a HybridKeypair from stored bytes
320.     ///
321.     /// Used when loading from keystore.
322.     pub fn from_bytes(
323.         classical_secret: &[u8; 32],
324.         classical_public: &[u8; 32],
325.         pq_secret: &[u8],
326.         pq_public: &[u8],
327.     ) -> Result<Self> {
328.         // Reconstruct Ed25519 signing key
329.         let classical_signing = SigningKey::from_bytes(classical_secret);
330. 
331.         // Verify public key matches
332.         let expected_public = classical_signing.verifying_key();
333.         if expected_public.as_bytes() != classical_public {
334.             return Err(CryptoError::InvalidKey(
335.                 "Classical public key doesn't match secret key".to_string(),
336.             ));
337.         }
338. 
339.         // Reconstruct ML-DSA keypair
340.         let pq_keypair = MlDsaKeypair::from_bytes(pq_secret, pq_public)?;
341. 
342.         Ok(Self {
343.             classical_signing,
344.             pq_keypair,
345.         })
346.     }
347. }
348.

350.     fn clone(&self) -> Self {
351.         Self {
352.             classical_signing: SigningKey::from_bytes(&self.classical_signing.to_bytes()),
353.             pq_keypair: self.pq_keypair.clone(),
354.         }
355.     }
356. }

1. //! ML-DSA (Module-Lattice Digital Signature Algorithm) wrapper
2. //!
3. //! This module wraps the pqcrypto-mldsa crate to provide a clean API
4. //! for ML-DSA signatures (NIST FIPS 204).
5. //!
6. //! We use ML-DSA-65 which provides:
7. //! - Security level: NIST Level 3 (~128-bit post-quantum security)
8. //! - Public key: 1952 bytes
9. //! - Signature: 3309 bytes
10. //! - Secret key: 4032 bytes
11. //!
12. //! ## Deterministic Key Generation
13. //!
14. //! This module supports deterministic key generation from a seed using HKDF
15. //! and ML-DSA's `from_seed` construction. This enables key recovery from a master seed.
16. //!
17. //! ```rust,ignore
18. //! use icn_crypto_pq::ml_dsa::MlDsaKeypair;
19. //!
20. //! let seed = [0u8; 32];
21. //! let keypair1 = MlDsaKeypair::from_seed(&seed)?;
22. //! let keypair2 = MlDsaKeypair::from_seed(&seed)?;
23. //!
24. //! // Same seed always produces identical keypairs
25. //! assert_eq!(keypair1.public_key().as_bytes(), keypair2.public_key().as_bytes());
26. //! ```

116. #[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
117. pub struct MlDsaKeypair {
118.     #[zeroize(skip)]
119.     public_key: MlDsaPublicKey,
120.     secret_key_bytes: Vec<u8>,
121. }
122. 
123. impl MlDsaKeypair {
124.     /// Secret key size in bytes
125.     pub const SECRET_KEY_SIZE: usize = 4032;
126. 
127.     /// Generate a new keypair with random keys
128.     pub fn generate() -> Result<Self> {
129.         let (pk, sk) = keypair();
130. 
131.         Ok(Self {
132.             public_key: MlDsaPublicKey {
133.                 bytes: pk.as_bytes().to_vec(),
134.             },
135.             secret_key_bytes: sk.as_bytes().to_vec(),
136.         })
137.     }
138. 
139.     /// Generate a keypair deterministically from a seed
140.     ///
141.     /// This uses HKDF-SHA3-256 to derive a 32-byte seed, then uses the
142.     /// pure-Rust ml-dsa crate for deterministic key generation.
143.     /// The same seed will always produce the same keypair.
144.     ///
145.     /// # Arguments
146.     ///
147.     /// * `seed` - At least 32 bytes of entropy (typically from a master seed)
148.     ///
149.     /// # Security
150.     ///
151.     /// The seed should be cryptographically random and kept secret.
152.     /// Recovery of the seed allows regeneration of the keypair.
153.     pub fn from_seed(seed: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
154.         if seed.len() < 32 {
155.             return Err(CryptoError::InvalidKey(
156.                 "ML-DSA seed must be at least 32 bytes".to_string(),
157.             ));
158.         }
159. 
160.         // Use HKDF to derive a 32-byte seed for the RNG
161.         let hk = Hkdf::<Sha3_256>::new(Some(ML_DSA_KEY_DERIVATION_DOMAIN), seed);
162.         let mut rng_seed = [0u8; 32];
163.         hk.expand(b"ml-dsa-65-keygen", &mut rng_seed)
164.             .map_err(|_| CryptoError::KeyDerivation("HKDF expansion failed".to_string()))?;
165. 
166.         let seed = Seed::from(rng_seed);
167. 
168.         // Generate keypair using the pure-Rust ml-dsa crate
169.         let kp = MlDsa65::from_seed(&seed);
170. 
171.         // Extract key bytes using encode() methods
172.         let signing_key = kp.signing_key();
173.         let verifying_key = kp.verifying_key();
174. 
175.         #[allow(deprecated)]
176.         let sk_encoded = signing_key.to_expanded();
177.         let pk_encoded = verifying_key.encode();
178. 
179.         Ok(Self {
180.             public_key: MlDsaPublicKey {
181.                 bytes: pk_encoded.as_slice().to_vec(),
182.             },
183.             secret_key_bytes: sk_encoded.as_slice().to_vec(),
184.         })
185.     }
186. 
187.     /// Create from existing key bytes
188.     pub fn from_bytes(secret_key: &[u8], public_key: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
189.         if secret_key.len() != Self::SECRET_KEY_SIZE {
190.             return Err(CryptoError::InvalidKey(format!(
191.                 "ML-DSA secret key must be {} bytes, got {}",
192.                 Self::SECRET_KEY_SIZE,
193.                 secret_key.len()
194.             )));
195.         }
196. 
197.         Ok(Self {
198.             public_key: MlDsaPublicKey::from_bytes(public_key)?,
199.             secret_key_bytes: secret_key.to_vec(),
200.         })
201.     }
202. 
203.     /// Get public key
204.     pub fn public_key(&self) -> &MlDsaPublicKey {
205.         &self.public_key
206.     }
207. 
208.     /// Get secret key bytes (use with caution)
209.     pub fn secret_key_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
210.         &self.secret_key_bytes
211.     }
212. 
213.     /// Sign a message
214.     pub fn sign(&self, message: &[u8]) -> Result<MlDsaSignature> {
215.         let sk = SecretKey::from_bytes(&self.secret_key_bytes)
216.             .map_err(|e| CryptoError::Signing(format!("Invalid secret key: {e:?}")))?;
217. 
218.         let sig = detached_sign(message, &sk);
219. 
220.         Ok(MlDsaSignature {
221.             bytes: sig.as_bytes().to_vec(),
222.         })
223.     }
224. 
225.     /// Verify a signature
226.     pub fn verify(public_key: &MlDsaPublicKey, message: &[u8], signature: &MlDsaSignature) -> bool {
227.         let pk = match public_key.to_pqcrypto() {
228.             Ok(pk) => pk,
229.             Err(_) => return false,
230.         };
231. 
232.         let sig = match signature.to_pqcrypto() {
233.             Ok(sig) => sig,
234.             Err(_) => return false,
235.         };
236. 
237.         verify_detached_signature(&sig, message, &pk).is_ok()
238.     }
239. }
240.

242.     fn clone(&self) -> Self {
243.         Self {
244.             public_key: self.public_key.clone(),
245.             secret_key_bytes: self.secret_key_bytes.clone(),
246.         }
247.     }
248. }

406.         let message = b"important document";

408. 
409.         // Later, recover the keypair from the same seed
410.         let recovered = MlDsaKeypair::from_seed(&seed).unwrap();
411. 
412.         // The recovered keypair should be able to:

416.             "Recovered keypair should verify original signatures"

418.

420.         let new_signature = recovered.sign(b"new message").unwrap();
421.         assert!(
422.             MlDsaKeypair::verify(original.public_key(), b"new message", &new_signature),
423.             "Original public key should verify recovered keypair signatures"
424.         );
425.     }

6. //! ICN Zero-Knowledge Proofs
7. //!
8. //! Zero-knowledge proof system for SDIS (Sovereign Digital Identity System).
9. //!
10. //! # Overview
11. //!
12. //! This crate provides:
13. //! - **Attribute proofs**: Prove properties without revealing data (age, citizenship, membership)
14. //! - **Non-revocation proofs**: Prove credential has not been revoked
15. //! - **Compound proofs**: Combine attribute + non-revocation
16. //! - **Accumulators**: RSA (legacy) and Merkle (PQ-safe) for revocation checking
17. //!
18. //! # Architecture
19. //!
20. //! ```text
21. //! ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
22. //! │                     ZKP System                                   │
23. //! ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
24. //! │                                                                  │
25. //! │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
26. //! │  │                    High-Level API                         │   │
27. //! │  │  ┌───────────────┐              ┌────────────────────┐   │   │
28. //! │  │  │   ZkProver    │              │    ZkVerifier      │   │   │
29. //! │  │  │ prove_age()   │              │   verify_age()     │   │   │
30. //! │  │  │ prove_cit()   │              │   verify_cit()     │   │   │
31. //! │  │  │ prove_mem()   │              │   verify_mem()     │   │   │
32. //! │  │  │ prove_nr()    │              │   verify_nr()      │   │   │
33. //! │  │  └───────┬───────┘              └─────────┬──────────┘   │   │
34. //! │  └──────────┼────────────────────────────────┼──────────────┘   │
35. //! │             │                                │                   │
36. //! │  ┌──────────▼────────────────────────────────▼──────────────┐   │
37. //! │  │                     Circuits                              │   │
38. //! │  │  ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌───────────┐  │   │
39. //! │  │  │  Age    │ │ Citizenship │ │Membership│ │NonRevoke  │  │   │
40. //! │  │  │ Circuit │ │   Circuit   │ │ Circuit  │ │ Circuit   │  │   │
41. //! │  │  └─────────┘ └─────────────┘ └──────────┘ └───────────┘  │   │
42. //! │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
43. //! │                                                                  │
44. //! │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
45. //! │  │                   Accumulator                             │   │
46. //! │  │                 (Revocation List)                         │   │
47. //! │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
48. //! └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
49. //! ```
50. //!
51. //! # Example Usage
52. //!
53. //! ```rust,ignore
54. //! use icn_zkp::{ZkProver, ZkVerifier, ProofContext, AgeAttestation};
55. //!
56. //! // Check proof capability first
57. //! let capability = icn_zkp::proof_capability();
58. //! if !capability.can_prove() {
59. //!     panic!("ZKP proving not available in this build");
60. //! }
61. //!
62. //! // Prover side
63. //! let prover = ZkProver::new();
64. //! let context = ProofContext::new(None);
65. //! let attestation = AgeAttestation {
66. //!     birthdate_days: 7300, // ~20 years ago
67. //!     signature: vec![0u8; 64],

361.     /// Rotate to a new KeyBundle
362.     ///
363.     /// Creates a new KeyBundle with incremented version and sets it as current.
364.     /// The old KeyBundle is retained for verification of old signatures.
365.     pub fn rotate_keybundle(&mut self, passphrase: &[u8]) -> Result<&KeyBundle> {
366.         let anchor = self
367.             .anchor
368.             .as_ref()
369.             .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("SDIS not initialized"))?
370.             .clone();
371. 
372.         let new_version = self.current_keybundle_version + 1;
373.         let new_keybundle = KeyBundle::generate(anchor, new_version)?;
374. 
375.         self.keybundles.push(new_keybundle);
376.         self.current_keybundle_version = new_version;
377. 
378.         // Save to disk
379.         self.save_v4(passphrase)?;
380. 
381.         info!("Rotated to KeyBundle v{}", new_version);
382. 
383.         // SAFETY: We just pushed to keybundles above, so last() is guaranteed Some
384.         #[allow(clippy::expect_used)]
385.         Ok(self
386.             .keybundles
387.             .last()
388.             .expect("keybundles cannot be empty after push"))
389.     }

391.     /// Upgrade identity to post-quantum security
392.     ///
393.     /// This adds ML-DSA (signing) and ML-KEM (encryption) keys to an existing
394.     /// Ed25519 identity. The DID remains unchanged.
395.     ///
396.     /// # Arguments
397.     /// * `passphrase` - Passphrase to encrypt the upgraded keystore
398.     ///
399.     /// # Returns
400.     /// The upgraded DID (unchanged from original)
401.     #[cfg(feature = "post-quantum")]
402.     pub fn upgrade_to_pq(&mut self, passphrase: &[u8]) -> Result<Did> {
403.         // Ensure keystore is unlocked
404.         let identity_bundle = self
405.             .identity_bundle
406.             .as_ref()
407.             .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Keystore must be unlocked to upgrade"))?;
408. 
409.         // Only software keys can be upgraded to PQ
410.         if identity_bundle.did_key().is_hardware_backed() {
411.             anyhow::bail!("Cannot upgrade hardware-backed keys to PQ in software");
412.         }
413. 
414.         // Reconstruct KeyPair to check PQ status
415.         let keypair = identity_bundle.keypair()?;
416. 
417.         // Check if already has PQ keys
418.         if keypair.has_pq_keys() {
419.             info!("Identity already has post-quantum keys");
420.             return Ok(identity_bundle.did().clone());
421.         }
422. 
423.         let did = identity_bundle.did().clone();
424.         info!("Upgrading identity {} to post-quantum security", did);
425. 
426.         // Generate ML-DSA keypair for signatures
427.         let pq_keypair = icn_crypto_pq::MlDsaKeypair::generate()
428.             .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Failed to generate ML-DSA keypair: {e}"))?;
429. 
430.         // Create upgraded KeyPair with PQ signing keys
431.         let (secret_bytes, public_bytes) = keypair.export_for_upgrade();
432.         let upgraded_keypair = KeyPair::from_bytes_with_pq(
433.             &secret_bytes,
434.             &public_bytes,
435.             pq_keypair.secret_key_bytes(),
436.             pq_keypair.public_key().as_bytes(),
437.         )?;
438. 
439.         // Convert upgraded KeyPair to DidKey.
440.         // PQ signing keys are stored alongside the bundle for persistence.
441.         let upgraded_did_key = DidKey::Software {
442.             secret_bytes: Zeroizing::new(upgraded_keypair.to_signing_key_bytes()),
443.             verifying_key: *upgraded_keypair.verifying_key(),
444.             did: upgraded_keypair.did().clone(),
445.         };
446. 
447.         // Generate ML-KEM keypair for hybrid encryption
448.         let kem_keypair = icn_crypto_pq::MlKemKeypair::generate()
449.             .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Failed to generate ML-KEM keypair: {e}"))?;
450. 
451.         // Create new IdentityBundle with upgraded keypair and KEM keys
452.         let upgraded_bundle = IdentityBundle::from_stored_with_pq(
453.             upgraded_did_key,
454.             identity_bundle.tls_cert().as_ref().to_vec(),
455.             Zeroizing::new(identity_bundle.tls_key_der_bytes().to_vec()),
456.             identity_bundle.binding_info().tls_binding_sig.clone(),
457.             identity_bundle.binding_info().created_at,
458.             Zeroizing::new(identity_bundle.x25519_secret_bytes().to_vec()),
459.             *identity_bundle.x25519_public_bytes(),
460.             Some(Zeroizing::new(pq_keypair.secret_key_bytes().to_vec())),
461.             Some(pq_keypair.public_key().as_bytes().to_vec()),
462.             Some(Zeroizing::new(kem_keypair.secret_key_bytes().to_vec())),
463.             Some(kem_keypair.public_key().as_bytes().to_vec()),
464.         )?;
465. 
466.         // Update in-memory state
467.         self.identity_bundle = Some(upgraded_bundle);
468. 
469.         // Save to disk
470.         self.save_v4(passphrase)?;
471. 
472.         info!(
473.             "Successfully upgraded identity {} to post-quantum security",
474.             did
475.         );
476. 
477.         Ok(did)
478.     }

567.     /// Encrypt and save v4 key material
568.     fn encrypt_and_save_v4(path: &Path, stored: &StoredKeyV4, passphrase: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {
569.         let json = Zeroizing::new(serde_json::to_vec(stored)?);
570. 
571.         let encryptor = age::Encryptor::with_user_passphrase(SecretString::new(
572.             String::from_utf8(passphrase.to_vec())
573.                 .context("Passphrase must be valid UTF-8")?
574.                 .into_boxed_str(),
575.         ));
576. 
577.         let mut encrypted = Vec::new();
578.         let mut writer = encryptor
579.             .wrap_output(&mut encrypted)
580.             .context("Failed to create age writer")?;
581. 
582.         std::io::copy(&mut json.as_slice(), &mut writer)
583.             .context("Failed to encrypt key material")?;
584. 
585.         writer
586.             .finish()
587.             .map(|_| ())
588.             .context("Failed to finalize encryption")?;
589. 
590.         std::fs::write(path, encrypted).context("Failed to write keystore file")?;
591. 
592.         Ok(())
593.     }
594. 
595.     /// Decrypt and load v4 key material
596.     fn decrypt_and_load_v4(path: &Path, passphrase: &[u8]) -> Result<StoredKeyV4> {
597.         // Read encrypted file
598.         let encrypted = std::fs::read(path).context("Failed to read keystore file")?;
599. 
600.         // Create age decryptor
601.         let decryptor = age::Decryptor::new(encrypted.as_slice())?;
602.         if !decryptor.is_scrypt() {
603.             anyhow::bail!("Unsupported age encryption type");
604.         }
605. 
606.         // Decrypt with scrypt identity
607.         let passphrase_str =
608.             String::from_utf8(passphrase.to_vec()).context("Passphrase must be valid UTF-8")?;
609.         let identity =
610.             age::scrypt::Identity::new(SecretString::new(passphrase_str.into_boxed_str()));
611. 
612.         let mut decrypted = Vec::new();
613.         let mut reader = decryptor
614.             .decrypt(std::iter::once(&identity as &dyn age::Identity))
615.             .context("Failed to decrypt (wrong passphrase?)")?;
616. 
617.         std::io::copy(&mut reader, &mut decrypted).context("Failed to read decrypted data")?;
618. 
619.         // Deserialize
620.         let stored: StoredKeyV4 =
621.             serde_json::from_slice(&decrypted).context("Failed to parse v4 key material")?;
622. 
623.         Ok(stored)
624.     }

633.     ///

643.     /// # fn example(keystore: &mut AgeKeyStore, passphrase: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
644.     /// keystore.update_did_document(

660.     pub fn update_did_document<F>(
661.         &mut self,

669.         // Ensure keystore is unlocked
670.         let identity_bundle = self

2. //!
3. //! A KeyBundle contains the cryptographic keys bound to an Anchor.
4. //! Unlike the Anchor which is permanent, KeyBundles can be rotated
5. //! while maintaining the same identity.
6. //!
7. //! # Key Components
8. //!
9. //! - **Hybrid Signature Keys**: Ed25519 + ML-DSA for quantum-resistant signatures
10. //! - **Encryption Key**: X25519 for key exchange
11. //! - **Version**: Monotonically increasing to track rotations
12. //!
13. //! # Rotation Protocol
14. //!
15. //! 1. Generate new KeyBundle with incremented version
16. //! 2. Sign rotation request with old KeyBundle
17. //! 3. Publish rotation event to gossip network

## SDIS Implementation Status Report

Based on comprehensive code analysis of icn-identity, icn-steward, icn-zkp, and icn-crypto-pq crates, here's the implementation status:

### ✅ **FULLY IMPLEMENTED**

1. **Anchor ID Computation** (`icn-identity/src/anchor.rs`)
   - ✅ H(VUI || genesis_random) correctly implemented
   - Uses SHA256 with domain separator "icn-anchor-v1"
   - Prevents rainbow table attacks via fresh randomness

2. **DID Format** (`icn-identity/src/anchor.rs:189-210`)
   - ✅ Format: `did:icn:\<base58btc-anchor-id\>`
   - Base58BTC encoding via multibase library
   - Proper conversion via `Did::from_anchor_id()`

3. **Post-Quantum Hybrid Signatures** (`icn-crypto-pq/src/hybrid.rs`)
   - ✅ Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 fully implemented
   - **Both signatures required to verify** (lines 77-82)
   - ML-DSA-65 per FIPS 204 (1952B public key, 3309B signature)
   - Deterministic key generation from seed for recovery

4. **Threshold PRF for VUI** (`icn-crypto-pq/src/shamir.rs` + `threshold.rs`)
   - ✅ k-of-n threshold scheme implemented
   - `PrfPartial::compute()` for steward evaluation
   - `combine_prf_partials()` client-side combination
   - Steward network coordination in `icn-steward/src/enrollment.rs`

5. **STARK-based ZK Proofs** (`icn-zkp/src/stark/`)
   - ✅ Real STARK proofs via winterfell library
   - ~96-bit security level
   - Circuits for: age, citizenship, membership, non-revocation
   - Feature-gated (`stark` feature) for binary size

### ⚠️ **PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED / GAPS**

1. **Age-Encrypted Keystore** (`icn-identity/src/keystore.rs:240-593`)
   - ✅ **Age encryption implemented** (lines 571-624)
   - ✅ Scrypt-based passphrase derivation
   - ✅ Zeroization via `Zeroizing\<T\>` for sensitive material
   - ⚠️ **GAP**: No explicit "age-based key rotation" policy
     - Keystores encrypt at rest but don't auto-rotate based on age
     - Manual rotation via `rotate_keybundle()` only

2. **Multi-Device Key Chaining** (`icn-identity/src/multi_device.rs`)
   - ✅ Multi-device support in DID Document v2
   - ✅ Device tracking with capabilities (Sign, AddDevice, RevokeDevice, etc.)
   - ⚠️ **GAP**: No cryptographic key chaining mechanism
     - Devices are listed but not linked via cryptographic derivation
     - No parent-child key hierarchy for secure delegation

### 🔴 **NOT FOUND / UNCLEAR**

1. **VUI Commitment Storage in Anchor**
   - ✅ VUI commitment is stored: `vui_commitment: [u8; 32]` (anchor.rs:60)
   - ⚠️ But recovery protocol documentation is missing

2. **Steward Network Attestations**
   - ✅ Structure exists: `VuiAttestation` with steward_did + signature
   - ❓ Consensus/validation logic for threshold attestation not found in search

3. **Key Recovery from Seed**
   - ✅ `HybridKeypair::from_seed()` enables full recovery (hybrid.rs:238)
   - ✅ Tested in comprehensive recovery scenario (tests lines 528-569)
   - ✅ ML-DSA also supports deterministic seed derivation

1. //! Core entity types for the ICN unified cooperative model
2. //!
3. //! This module defines the foundational types for representing entities at all scales:
4. //! - Individuals (backed by DIDs)
5. //! - Cooperatives (worker, consumer, multi-stakeholder)
6. //! - Communities (geographic, interest-based, or practice-based groups)
7. //! - Federations (cooperatives of cooperatives)
8. //!
9. //! The key insight is that membership is recursive: a cooperative's members
10. //! can themselves be cooperatives. Communities bridge individuals and cooperatives,
11. //! allowing diverse membership models.
12. 
13. use crate::error::{EntityError, Result};
14. use icn_identity::Did;
15. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
16. use std::collections::HashMap;
17. use std::fmt;
18. use std::str::FromStr;
19. 
20. // ============================================================================
21. // EntityId
22. // ============================================================================
23. 
24. /// Unique identifier for any entity (individual, cooperative, community, or federation)
25. ///
26. /// EntityId is designed to be compatible with DIDs:
27. /// - For individuals: wraps their DID directly
28. /// - For cooperatives: derived from cooperative creation ceremony
29. /// - For communities: derived from community formation
30. /// - For federations: derived from federation charter
31. ///
32. /// # Format
33. ///
34. /// `entity:icn:<type>:<identifier>`
35. ///
36. /// # Examples
37. ///
38. /// - `entity:icn:individual:z5TrA8...` (wraps DID)
39. /// - `entity:icn:cooperative:food-coop-2024`
40. /// - `entity:icn:community:neighborhood-2024`
41. /// - `entity:icn:federation:midwest-fed`
42. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
43. pub struct EntityId(String);
44. 
45. impl EntityId {
46.     /// Create an EntityId from an individual's DID
47.     ///
48.     /// This wraps the DID in the entity format, allowing individuals
49.     /// to participate in the entity system while maintaining their
50.     /// cryptographic identity.
51.     pub fn from_did(did: &Did) -> Self {
52.         let did_str = did.as_str();
53.         let identifier = did_str.strip_prefix("did:icn:").unwrap_or(did_str);
54.         EntityId(format!("entity:icn:individual:{identifier}"))
55.     }
56. 
57.     /// Create an EntityId for a cooperative
58.     ///
59.     /// The slug should be a URL-safe identifier for the cooperative.
60.     /// It will be validated for allowed characters.
61.     pub fn cooperative(slug: &str) -> Result<Self> {
62.         Self::validate_slug(slug)?;
63.         Ok(EntityId(format!("entity:icn:cooperative:{slug}")))
64.     }
65. 
66.     /// Create an EntityId for a federation
67.     ///
68.     /// The slug should be a URL-safe identifier for the federation.
69.     pub fn federation(slug: &str) -> Result<Self> {
70.         Self::validate_slug(slug)?;
71.         Ok(EntityId(format!("entity:icn:federation:{slug}")))
72.     }
73. 
74.     /// Create an EntityId for a community
75.     ///
76.     /// The slug should be a URL-safe identifier for the community.
77.     /// Communities can have both Individual and Cooperative members,
78.     /// and can join Federations.
79.     pub fn community(slug: &str) -> Result<Self> {
80.         Self::validate_slug(slug)?;
81.         Ok(EntityId(format!("entity:icn:community:{slug}")))
82.     }
83. 
84.     /// Validate a slug for use in EntityId
85.     ///
86.     /// Rules:
87.     /// - 4-64 characters (minimum 4 to avoid namespace collisions)
88.     /// - Lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens only
89.     /// - Must start with a letter
90.     /// - No consecutive hyphens
91.     fn validate_slug(slug: &str) -> Result<()> {
92.         if slug.len() < 4 {
93.             return Err(EntityError::InvalidFormat(
94.                 "Slug must be at least 4 characters".into(),
95.             ));
96.         }
97.         if slug.len() > 64 {
98.             return Err(EntityError::InvalidFormat(
99.                 "Slug cannot exceed 64 characters".into(),
100.             ));
```

1. # Vision: Institution-in-a-Box
2. 
3. > **"Every human group can run its own institution. On their hardware. With verifiable identity, consent, and auditability."**
4. 
5. You don’t “pivot” from what we have into the vision. You **route** it.
6. 
7. We are keeping the *core invariant* (sovereign nodes + trust-gated coordination) and deliberately growing the *interfaces* that make it feel like “the internet finally grew up.”
8. 
9. ## The Promise
10. 
11. > **"Spin up a community. Give it rules. Give it money flows. Give it governance. Make it interoperable. Make it accountable."**
12. 
13. That’s the north star.
14. 
15. ## 1. Institution Primitives (The Kernel)
16. 
17. We expose 4 “institution primitives” cleanly:
18. 
19. 1.  **Identity & Membership**: Who is in/out, what roles exist, verification, revocation.
20. 2.  **Rules & Governance**: Proposals, deliberation, voting, constitutional constraints.
21. 3.  **Economics**: Budgets, mutual credit, accounts, spending limits, audits.
22. 4.  **Interoperation**: Federation agreements for trade, sharing, and arbitration.
23. 
24. ## 2. The Product: Institution-in-a-Box
25. 
26. The first real product is a boring, powerful bundle: a **municipal operating system starter kit.**
27. 
28. *   **One-click “New Coop / New Community”**
29. *   Default charter templates
30. *   Membership onboarding
31. *   Treasury ledger
32. *   Proposal + vote loop
33. *   Dashboard: “What decisions exist, what money moved, who authorized it”
34. 
35. ## 3. The Compute Commons (The Consequence)
36. 
37. We don't pitch "a compute commons." We pitch **capability**. Compute is a paid-in-kind resource.
38. 
39. *   Communities contribute compute/storage/bandwidth.
40. *   They earn internal credit.
41. *   They spend it on shared services (search, hosting) or federation-wide projects.
42. 
43. Compute becomes the “mana meter” behind cooperation.
44. 
45. ## 4. Federation Agreements (The Bridge)
46. 
47. The **Federation Agreement** defines trust thresholds, dispute resolution, cross-ledger clearing, and data sharing between groups. This turns isolated islands into a **civilizational mesh**.
48. 
49. ## Roadmap: From Vision to Inevitability
50. 
51. 1.  **Stage A: Institutions** (Institution-in-a-Box, Charters, Treasury)
52. 2.  **Stage B: Federation** (Agreements, Cross-group Trust, Clearing)
53. 3.  **Stage C: Commons** (Resource Contribution, Shared Services)
54. 4.  **Stage D: Civilization Tools** (Municipal Governance, Public Infrastructure)
55. 
56. ## The Adoption Wedge
57. 
58. Our adoption wedge must deliver value *before* philosophy:
59. *   **Group purchasing**
60. *   **Mutual aid funds**
61. *   **Community grants**
62. *   **Shared services**
63. 
64. ## Governance Law: The Meaning Firewall
65. 
66. *   **Kernel** enforces *mechanisms* (identity, trust, audit).
67. *   **Apps** define *meaning* (what is a “member”, “vote”, “budget”).
68. 
69. ---
70. 
71. > **Turn what you have into the vision by productizing “institution primitives,” shipping Institution-in-a-Box, then scaling via Federation Agreements until the compute commons emerges as the resource layer behind cooperation.**
```

1. # Vision-to-Implementation Gap Analysis
2. 
3. **Document ID**: ICN-GAP-VISION-01
4. **Created**: 2025-11-28
5. **Purpose**: Map the ICN vision to implementation status and prioritize closing gaps
6. 
7. ---
8. 
9. ## Executive Summary
10. 
11. ICN is **substrate-complete** (~80% architecturally sound) but **integration-incomplete** (~50% functionally integrated). The core protocols work; they're not connected into the coherent experience the vision describes.
12. 
13. **Critical Finding**: The vision describes "a global cooperative operating layer" but several key pieces are either:
14. - Code exists but never wired into the daemon
15. - CLI commands are stubs that print "TODO"
16. - Security holes that would be unacceptable in production
17. 
18. ---
19. 
20. ## Vision Components Mapped to Implementation
21. 
22. ### 1. Identity You Own, Not Rent
23. 
24. **Vision**: "Device-level DIDs that you actually possess. Identity becomes portable, multi-device, cryptographically verifiable, independent of institutions."
25. 
26. **Implementation Status**:
27. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
28. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
29. | DID generation | ✅ | ✅ | Ed25519 keypairs, `did:icn:` format |
30. | Keystore (Age-encrypted) | ✅ | ✅ | v2.1 with TLS + X25519 |
31. | Multi-device DID Document | ✅ | ⚠️ | Code exists, IdentityActor commented out |
32. | Device add/revoke | ✅ | ❌ | CLI stubs: "TODO: Sign this event" |
33. | Social recovery | ✅ | ❌ | CLI stubs: "TODO: Publish to gossip" |
34. | Identity sync via gossip | ✅ | ❌ | `identity:updates` topic defined, not used |
35. 
36. **Gap**: Multi-device identity is CLI-local only. The IdentityActor that would sync across nodes is commented out in `supervisor.rs:315`.
37. 
38. **Files**:
39. - `icn-identity/src/did_document.rs` - DID Document v2 ✅
40. - `icn-identity/src/bundle.rs` - IdentityBundle ✅
41. - `icn-core/src/supervisor.rs:315` - IdentityActor COMMENTED OUT
42. - `bins/icnctl/src/main.rs:3070,3158` - device approve/revoke stubs
43. 
44. ---
45. 
46. ### 2. Web-of-Participation (Trust Graph)
47. 
48. **Vision**: "You trust people you've worked with. And you trust who they trust to the degree that makes sense. This creates a dynamic graph of actual participation."
49. 
50. **Implementation Status**:
51. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
52. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
53. | Trust graph storage | ✅ | ✅ | Sled-backed |
54. | Transitive trust computation | ✅ | ✅ | PageRank-style algorithm |
55. | Trust-gated rate limiting | ✅ | ✅ | 4 trust classes |
56. | Trust-gated gossip topics | ✅ | ✅ | AccessControl::TrustGated |
57. | Trust-gated compute | ✅ | ✅ | MIN_TRUST_SUBMIT/EXECUTE |
58. | Trust in policies | ✅ | ⚠️ | Direct trust only, not transitive |
59. 
60. **Gap**: Transitive trust computation works but is NOT used in access control policies. Only direct trust scores are checked.
61. 
62. **Files**:
63. - `icn-trust/src/graph.rs` - Trust graph ✅
64. - `icn-trust/src/compute.rs` - Transitive computation ✅
65. - `icn-net/src/rate_limit.rs` - Trust-based rate limiting ✅
66. 
67. ---
68. 
69. ### 3. Mutual Credit Economy
70. 
71. **Vision**: "No tokens to speculate on. No miners. No global blockchain. It models reciprocity: when you contribute value, you earn credit."
72. 
73. **Implementation Status**:
74. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
75. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
76. | Double-entry ledger | ✅ | ✅ | Merkle-DAG journal |
77. | Multi-currency | ✅ | ✅ | hours, USD, kWh, etc. |
78. | Dynamic credit limits | ✅ | ✅ | Trust + history based |
79. | New member protection | ✅ | ✅ | Progressive ramping |
80. | Dispute resolution | ✅ | ✅ | File, mediate, resolve |
81. | Cooperative treasury | ❌ | ❌ | No collective fund concept |
82. 
83. **Gap**: No treasury DID per cooperative. Payments are attributed to individuals, not coops. Communities can't hold collective funds.

87. - `icn-ledger/src/credit_policy.rs` - Dynamic limits ✅
88. - `icn-ledger/src/dispute.rs` - Dispute resolution ✅

90. ---
91. 
92. ### 4. Contracts as Computation (CCL)

117. ### 5. Gossip Instead of Gods

131. **Status**: ✅ **COMPLETE** - Gossip protocol is fully implemented and integrated.

139. 
140. ### 6. Distributed Compute as a Commons
141.

212. ## Security Issues
213. 
214. ### ~~CRITICAL: RPC Endpoint Has No Authentication~~ ✅ FIXED (2025-11-28)
215. 
216. **Location**: `icn-rpc/src/auth.rs` (NEW), `icn-rpc/src/server.rs`
217. 
218. **Resolution**: Full JWT authentication added to RPC server:
219. - `auth.challenge` / `auth.verify` endpoints for DID-based authentication
220. - Scope-based authorization for all methods (e.g., `compute:write`, `ledger:read`)
221. - Authenticated DID tracked for compute task submission (no more `"rpc:unknown"`)
222. - 6 new tests validating auth flow
223. 
224. **Usage**:
225. ```bash
226. # 1. Get challenge
227. curl -X POST http://localhost:5601 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"auth.challenge","params":{"did":"did:icn:..."},"id":1}'
228. 
229. # 2. Sign nonce and verify to get JWT
230. curl -X POST http://localhost:5601 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"auth.verify","params":{"did":"did:icn:...","signature":"...","scopes":["compute:write"]},"id":2}'
231. 
232. # 3. Use token for authenticated requests
233. curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST http://localhost:5601 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"compute.submit",...}'
234. ```
235.

## Summary: Treasury & Collective Funds Implementation Status

**The gap mentioned in the vision has been PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.** Treasury infrastructure exists but integration with cooperatives is incomplete.

### ✅ **What EXISTS** (in `icn-ledger/src/treasury.rs` and `icn-gateway/src/treasury_mgr.rs`):

1. **Treasury Account Structure** (lines 113-146):
   - `Treasury` struct with `treasury_did` (cooperative-owned account)
   - Support for `entity_id` (EntityId linking treasury to cooperative)
   - Multi-currency support (`currency` field)
   - Backward-compatible `coop_id` field

2. **Treasury Manager** (lines 209-259):
   - Persistent storage via `TreasuryManager`
   - Budget tracking (`TreasuryBudget`)
   - Spending rules with approval thresholds
   - Velocity limits for spending rate control
   - Labor shares and cooperative bonds (Razeto integration)
   - Complete audit trail for all operations

3. **API Endpoints** (via `icn-gateway/src/api/treasury.rs`):
   - Balance queries
   - Budget management
   - Spending rule configuration
   - Audit trail pagination

4. **Governance Integration**:
   - Spending rules trigger governance approval
   - Proposal system for large withdrawals
   - Approval types: SimpleMajority, etc.

### ❌ **What's MISSING** (per `docs/internal/status/vision-implementation-gap.md` line 81-82):

**From the Gap Analysis (lines 81-82):**
\> **Gap**: No treasury DID per cooperative. Payments are attributed to individuals, not coops. Communities can't hold collective funds.

Critical missing pieces:
1. **Treasury-to-Cooperative Wiring**: While `Treasury` struct has `entity_id` support (modern), the cooperative actor in `icn-coop/src/actor.rs` doesn't create or manage treasuries during cooperative formation
2. **Collective Payment Routing**: Ledger entries still route to individual DIDs, not cooperative treasury DIDs
3. **Federation Treasury**: No support for federation-level treasuries
4. **Treasury Initialization**: No ceremonial creation of treasury DIDs during cooperative creation

### 📊 **The Reality**:

- **Code exists**: Complete treasury system in `icn-ledger` with 3 submodules (approvals, audit, budgets)
- **Tests exist**: `icn-gateway/tests/treasury_custody_test.rs`, `icn-core/tests/treasury_integration.rs`
- **API exists**: Full HTTP endpoints via `icn-gateway`
- **NOT WIRED**: Cooperatives don't create treasuries, ledger doesn't route collective payments to them

**What users can't do today** (Vision-Implementation Gap, line 321):
\> Lock funds in cooperative treasury

**Tier 3 Implementation Priority** (line 295-298):
```
7. **Cooperative Treasury**
   - Treasury DID per cooperative  ← Missing
   - Governance-approved spending  ← Partial
   - Collective fund accounting    ← Missing
```

The infrastructure is 80% ready; the missing 20% is integrating it with the cooperative lifecycle actor to auto-create treasuries and route payments appropriately.

1. //! Fuel estimation for CCL contracts
2. //!
3. //! Provides static analysis of contract rules to estimate fuel consumption
4. //! before execution. This helps clients set appropriate fuel limits.
5. 
6. use crate::ast::{Contract, Expr, Rule, Stmt};

8. 
9. /// Fuel cost constants for estimation (matches interpreter defaults)
10. const FUEL_STMT: u64 = 1;
11. const FUEL_EXPR: u64 = 1;
12. const FUEL_CALL: u64 = 10;
13. const FUEL_LOOP_ITERATION: u64 = 5;
14. const MAX_LOOP_ITERATIONS: u64 = 1000;
15. 
16. /// Fuel estimator for CCL contracts
17. ///
18. /// Performs static analysis of contract rules to estimate fuel consumption.
19. ///
20. /// # Example
21. ///
22. /// ```
23. /// use icn_ccl::{Contract, FuelEstimator};
24. ///
25. /// let contract = Contract::new("Test".to_string());
26. /// let estimator = FuelEstimator::new(&contract);
27. ///
28. /// if let Some(estimate) = estimator.estimate_rule("my_rule") {
29. ///     println!("Recommended fuel: {}", estimate.recommended());
30. /// }
31. /// ```

33.     contract: &'a Contract,
34. }
35. 
36. impl<'a> FuelEstimator<'a> {
37.     /// Create a new fuel estimator for a contract
38.     pub fn new(contract: &'a Contract) -> Self {
39.         Self { contract }
40.     }
41. 
42.     /// Estimate fuel for a specific rule
43.     ///
44.     /// Returns None if the rule doesn't exist.
45.     pub fn estimate_rule(&self, rule_name: &str) -> Option<FuelEstimate> {
46.         let rule = self.contract.get_rule(rule_name)?;
47.         Some(self.estimate_rule_internal(rule))
48.     }
49. 
50.     /// Estimate fuel for all rules in the contract
51.     pub fn estimate_all_rules(&self) -> Vec<(String, FuelEstimate)> {
52.         self.contract
53.             .rules
54.             .iter()
55.             .map(|rule| (rule.name.clone(), self.estimate_rule_internal(rule)))
56.             .collect()
57.     }
58. 
59.     fn estimate_rule_internal(&self, rule: &Rule) -> FuelEstimate {
60.         let mut estimate = FuelEstimate::zero();
61. 
62.         // Estimate require conditions
63.         for require in &rule.requires {
64.             estimate = estimate.then(self.estimate_expr(require));
65.         }
66. 
67.         // Estimate body statements
68.         for stmt in &rule.body {
69.             estimate = estimate.then(self.estimate_stmt(stmt));
70.         }
71. 
72.         estimate
73.     }
74.

78.

6. //!
7. //! This crate implements a domain-specific language (DSL) for expressing cooperative
8. //! agreements with built-in safety features:
9. //!
10. //! - **Deterministic execution**: Same inputs always produce same outputs
11. //! - **Capability-based security**: Explicit permissions for ledger access
12. //! - **Fuel metering**: Bounded execution prevents infinite loops
13. //! - **Not Turing-complete**: Safe subset of operations
14. //!
15. //! ## Example: TimeBank Contract
16. //!
17. //! ```rust

19. //! use icn_identity::KeyPair;

1. //! Contract runtime that integrates interpreter with ledger
2. 
3. use crate::ast::Contract;
4. use crate::interpreter::Interpreter;
5. use crate::types::{ContractState, ExecutionContext, ExecutionResult, LedgerOperation};
6. use anyhow::{Context as _, Result};
7. use icn_ledger::{entry::JournalEntryBuilder, ContentHash, Ledger};
8. use std::collections::HashMap;
9. use std::sync::Arc;
10. use tokio::sync::RwLock;
11. use tracing::{debug, info};
12. 
13. /// Contract runtime manages contract execution and ledger integration
14. pub struct ContractRuntime {
15.     /// Ledger instance
16.     ledger: Arc<RwLock<Ledger>>,
17. 
18.     /// Installed contracts (code_hash -> Contract)
19.     contracts: HashMap<ContentHash, Contract>,
20. 
21.     /// Contract installations (code_hash -> Installation metadata)
22.     installations: HashMap<ContentHash, crate::types::ContractInstallation>,
23. 
24.     /// Contract states (code_hash -> State)
25.     states: HashMap<ContentHash, ContractState>,
26. }
27. 
28. impl ContractRuntime {
29.     /// Create a new contract runtime
30.     pub fn new(ledger: Arc<RwLock<Ledger>>) -> Self {
31.         ContractRuntime {
32.             ledger,
33.             contracts: HashMap::new(),
34.             installations: HashMap::new(),
35.             states: HashMap::new(),
36.         }
37.     }
38. 
39.     /// Install a contract with installation metadata
40.     pub fn install_contract_with_metadata(
41.         &mut self,
42.         code_hash: ContentHash,
43.         contract: Contract,
44.         installation: crate::types::ContractInstallation,
45.     ) -> Result<()> {
46.         info!("Installing contract: {} ({})", contract.name, code_hash);
47. 
48.         // Validate contract structure before installation
49.         contract.validate().context("Contract validation failed")?;
50. 
51.         // Initialize state with state variables
52.         let mut state = ContractState::new();
53.         for state_var in &contract.state_vars {
54.             state.set(state_var.name.clone(), state_var.initial_value.clone());
55.         }
56. 
57.         self.contracts.insert(code_hash.clone(), contract);
58.         self.installations.insert(code_hash.clone(), installation);
59.         self.states.insert(code_hash, state);
60. 
61.         Ok(())
62.     }
63. 
64.     /// Install a contract (deprecated - use install_contract_with_metadata)
65.     pub fn install_contract(&mut self, code_hash: ContentHash, contract: Contract) -> Result<()> {
66.         // Create a basic installation for backward compatibility
67.         // SAFETY: KeyPair::generate() only fails if system entropy is exhausted
68.         #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
69.         let installation = crate::types::ContractInstallation {
70.             code_hash: code_hash.clone(),
71.             installed_by: contract.participants.first().cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| {
72.                 // Fallback to a dummy DID
73.                 use icn_identity::KeyPair;
74.                 KeyPair::generate().unwrap().did().clone()
75.             }),
76.             capabilities: vec![
77.                 // Grant all capabilities for backward compatibility
78.                 crate::types::Capability::WriteLedger {
79.                     accounts: contract.participants.clone(),
80.                 },
81.                 crate::types::Capability::ReadLedger {
82.                     accounts: contract.participants.clone(),
83.                 },
84.             ],
85.             participants: contract.participants.clone(),
86.             signatures: vec![],
87.             installed_at: icn_time::current_timestamp_secs(),
88.             min_caller_trust: None,
89.         };
90. 
91.         self.install_contract_with_metadata(code_hash, contract, installation)
92.     }

500.     fn eval_binop(&self, op: BinOp, left: Value, right: Value) -> Result<Value> {
501.         use BinOp::*;
502.         use Value::*;
503. 
504.         match (op, &left, &right) {
505.             // Integer arithmetic
506.             (Add, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Int(a + b)),
507.             (Sub, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Int(a - b)),
508.             (Mul, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Int(a * b)),
509.             (Div, Int(a), Int(b)) => {
510.                 if *b == 0 {
511.                     return Err(CclError::DivisionByZero {
512.                         span: Span::unknown(),
513.                     });
514.                 }
515.                 Ok(Int(a / b))
516.             }
517.             (Mod, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Int(a % b)),
518. 
519.             // String concatenation
520.             (Add, String(a), String(b)) => Ok(String(format!("{a}{b}"))),
521. 
522.             // Comparisons
523.             (Eq, a, b) => Ok(Bool(a == b)),
524.             (Ne, a, b) => Ok(Bool(a != b)),
525.             (Lt, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Bool(a < b)),
526.             (Le, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Bool(a <= b)),
527.             (Gt, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Bool(a > b)),
528.             (Ge, Int(a), Int(b)) => Ok(Bool(a >= b)),
529. 
530.             // Logical
531.             (And, a, b) => Ok(Bool(a.is_truthy() && b.is_truthy())),
532.             (Or, a, b) => Ok(Bool(a.is_truthy() || b.is_truthy())),
533. 
534.             _ => Err(CclError::InvalidBinaryOp {
535.                 span: Span::unknown(),
536.                 op: format!("{op:?}"),
537.                 left_type: left.type_name().to_string(),
538.                 right_type: right.type_name().to_string(),
539.             }),
540.         }
541.     }
542. 
543.     /// Evaluate unary operation
544.     fn eval_unop(&self, op: UnOp, val: Value) -> Result<Value> {
545.         match (op, &val) {
546.             (UnOp::Not, v) => Ok(Value::Bool(!v.is_truthy())),
547.             (UnOp::Neg, Value::Int(i)) => Ok(Value::Int(-i)),
548.             _ => Err(CclError::InvalidUnaryOp {
549.                 span: Span::unknown(),
550.                 op: format!("{op:?}"),
551.                 operand_type: val.type_name().to_string(),
552.             }),
553.         }
554.     }
555. 
556.     /// Evaluate built-in function call
557.     fn eval_call(&mut self, name: &str, args: Vec<Value>) -> Result<Value> {
558.         match name {
559.             "len" => {
560.                 if args.len() != 1 {
561.                     return Err(CclError::ArgumentCount {
562.                         span: Span::unknown(),
563.                         name: "len".to_string(),
564.                         expected: 1,
565.                         actual: args.len(),
566.                     });
567.                 }
568.                 match &args[0] {
569.                     Value::List(list) => Ok(Value::Int(list.len() as i64)),
570.                     Value::Set(set) => Ok(Value::Int(set.len() as i64)),
571.                     Value::String(s) => Ok(Value::Int(s.len() as i64)),
572.                     _ => Err(CclError::ArgumentType {
573.                         span: Span::unknown(),
574.                         name: "len".to_string(),
575.                         expected: "list, set, or string",
576.                         actual: args[0].type_name().to_string(),
577.                     }),
578.                 }
579.             }
580. 
581.             "abs" => {
582.                 if args.len() != 1 {
583.                     return Err(CclError::ArgumentCount {
584.                         span: Span::unknown(),
585.                         name: "abs".to_string(),
586.                         expected: 1,
587.                         actual: args.len(),
588.                     });
589.                 }
590.                 match &args[0] {
591.                     Value::Int(i) => Ok(Value::Int(i.abs())),
592.                     _ => Err(CclError::ArgumentType {
593.                         span: Span::unknown(),
594.                         name: "abs".to_string(),
595.                         expected: "integer",
596.                         actual: args[0].type_name().to_string(),
597.                     }),
598.                 }
599.             }
600.
```

1. # Vision-to-Implementation Gap Analysis
2. 
3. **Document ID**: ICN-GAP-VISION-01
4. **Created**: 2025-11-28
5. **Purpose**: Map the ICN vision to implementation status and prioritize closing gaps
6. 
7. ---
8. 
9. ## Executive Summary
10. 
11. ICN is **substrate-complete** (~80% architecturally sound) but **integration-incomplete** (~50% functionally integrated). The core protocols work; they're not connected into the coherent experience the vision describes.
12. 
13. **Critical Finding**: The vision describes "a global cooperative operating layer" but several key pieces are either:
14. - Code exists but never wired into the daemon
15. - CLI commands are stubs that print "TODO"
16. - Security holes that would be unacceptable in production
17. 
18. ---
19. 
20. ## Vision Components Mapped to Implementation
21. 
22. ### 1. Identity You Own, Not Rent
23. 
24. **Vision**: "Device-level DIDs that you actually possess. Identity becomes portable, multi-device, cryptographically verifiable, independent of institutions."
25. 
26. **Implementation Status**:
27. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
28. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
29. | DID generation | ✅ | ✅ | Ed25519 keypairs, `did:icn:` format |
30. | Keystore (Age-encrypted) | ✅ | ✅ | v2.1 with TLS + X25519 |
31. | Multi-device DID Document | ✅ | ⚠️ | Code exists, IdentityActor commented out |
32. | Device add/revoke | ✅ | ❌ | CLI stubs: "TODO: Sign this event" |
33. | Social recovery | ✅ | ❌ | CLI stubs: "TODO: Publish to gossip" |
34. | Identity sync via gossip | ✅ | ❌ | `identity:updates` topic defined, not used |
35. 
36. **Gap**: Multi-device identity is CLI-local only. The IdentityActor that would sync across nodes is commented out in `supervisor.rs:315`.
37. 
38. **Files**:
39. - `icn-identity/src/did_document.rs` - DID Document v2 ✅
40. - `icn-identity/src/bundle.rs` - IdentityBundle ✅
41. - `icn-core/src/supervisor.rs:315` - IdentityActor COMMENTED OUT
42. - `bins/icnctl/src/main.rs:3070,3158` - device approve/revoke stubs
43. 
44. ---
45. 
46. ### 2. Web-of-Participation (Trust Graph)
47. 
48. **Vision**: "You trust people you've worked with. And you trust who they trust to the degree that makes sense. This creates a dynamic graph of actual participation."
49. 
50. **Implementation Status**:
51. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
52. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
53. | Trust graph storage | ✅ | ✅ | Sled-backed |
54. | Transitive trust computation | ✅ | ✅ | PageRank-style algorithm |
55. | Trust-gated rate limiting | ✅ | ✅ | 4 trust classes |
56. | Trust-gated gossip topics | ✅ | ✅ | AccessControl::TrustGated |
57. | Trust-gated compute | ✅ | ✅ | MIN_TRUST_SUBMIT/EXECUTE |
58. | Trust in policies | ✅ | ⚠️ | Direct trust only, not transitive |
59. 
60. **Gap**: Transitive trust computation works but is NOT used in access control policies. Only direct trust scores are checked.
61. 
62. **Files**:
63. - `icn-trust/src/graph.rs` - Trust graph ✅
64. - `icn-trust/src/compute.rs` - Transitive computation ✅
65. - `icn-net/src/rate_limit.rs` - Trust-based rate limiting ✅
66. 
67. ---
68. 
69. ### 3. Mutual Credit Economy
70. 
71. **Vision**: "No tokens to speculate on. No miners. No global blockchain. It models reciprocity: when you contribute value, you earn credit."
72. 
73. **Implementation Status**:
74. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
75. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
76. | Double-entry ledger | ✅ | ✅ | Merkle-DAG journal |
77. | Multi-currency | ✅ | ✅ | hours, USD, kWh, etc. |
78. | Dynamic credit limits | ✅ | ✅ | Trust + history based |
79. | New member protection | ✅ | ✅ | Progressive ramping |
80. | Dispute resolution | ✅ | ✅ | File, mediate, resolve |
81. | Cooperative treasury | ❌ | ❌ | No collective fund concept |
82. 
83. **Gap**: No treasury DID per cooperative. Payments are attributed to individuals, not coops. Communities can't hold collective funds.
84. 
85. **Files**:
86. - `icn-ledger/src/ledger.rs` - Core ledger ✅
87. - `icn-ledger/src/credit_policy.rs` - Dynamic limits ✅
88. - `icn-ledger/src/dispute.rs` - Dispute resolution ✅
89. 
90. ---
91. 
92. ### 4. Contracts as Computation (CCL)
93. 
94. **Vision**: "A tiny deterministic VM that executes agreements as code: membership rules, cooperative bylaws, cost-sharing, approvals, contributions."
95. 
96. **Implementation Status**:
97. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
98. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
99. | CCL AST & parser | ✅ | ✅ | Contract, Rule, Stmt, Expr |
100. | Interpreter | ✅ | ✅ | Fuel-metered execution |
101. | Capability system | ✅ | ✅ | ReadLedger, WriteLedger, ReadTrust |
102. | Compute execution | ✅ | ✅ | LocalExecutor runs CCL |
103. | Contract registry | ✅ | ⚠️ | Code exists, needs supervisor wiring |
104. | CclRef task code | ✅ | ⚠️ | TaskCode::CclRef variant ready |
105. | Gossip deployment | ❌ | ❌ | Registry sync not yet implemented |
106. 
107. **Progress (2025-11-28)**: Contract registry implemented with persistent storage and in-memory caching. Deploy once, invoke by hash pattern ready. Executor handles CclRef variant.
108.

111. - `icn-ccl/src/interpreter.rs` - Execution ✅
112. - `icn-ccl/src/registry.rs` - ContractRegistry ✅ NEW
113. - `icn-compute/src/types.rs` - TaskCode::CclRef ✅

140. ### 6. Distributed Compute as a Commons
141.

144. **Implementation Status**:
145. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |

167. ### 7. Democratic Federation
168. 
169. **Vision**: "Communities choose whom to federate with. Trust determines bandwidth, permissions, and cooperation. No central server; no company to appease."
170. 
171. **Implementation Status**:

214. ### ~~CRITICAL: RPC Endpoint Has No Authentication~~ ✅ FIXED (2025-11-28)

218. **Resolution**: Full JWT authentication added to RPC server:

225. ```bash
226. # 1. Get challenge
227. curl -X POST http://localhost:5601 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"auth.challenge","params":{"did":"did:icn:..."},"id":1}'
228. 
229. # 2. Sign nonce and verify to get JWT
230. curl -X POST http://localhost:5601 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"auth.verify","params":{"did":"did:icn:...","signature":"...","scopes":["compute:write"]},"id":2}'
231. 
232. # 3. Use token for authenticated requests
233. curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST http://localhost:5601 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"compute.submit",...}'
234. ```

1. //! Authorization Primitive
2. //!
3. //! Provides object-capability tokens and policy oracle interface.
4. //!
5. //! # Design
6. //!
7. //! - Capabilities are bearer tokens, not RBAC roles
8. //! - Policy decisions come from apps via PolicyOracle
9. //! - Kernel enforces decisions without understanding them
10. //!
11. //! # The Policy Oracle Pattern
12. //!
13. //! The kernel calls `PolicyOracle::evaluate()` to get authorization
14. //! decisions. Apps (like the trust app) implement this trait to
15. //! provide domain-specific logic. The kernel then enforces the
16. //! decision without understanding why it was made.
17. //!
18. //! # The Meaning Firewall
19. //!
20. //! The kernel does NOT understand:
21. //! - Trust classes or scores
22. //! - Governance weights
23. //! - Credit multipliers
24. //! - Membership status
25. //!
26. //! It only understands:
27. //! - Allow with constraints
28. //! - Deny with reason
29. //!
30. //! Apps set constraint values. Kernel enforces them blindly.
31. //!
32. //! # Non-Goals
33. //!
34. //! - Role hierarchies (use capabilities instead)
35. //! - Trust scores (trust app implements these via PolicyOracle)
36. //! - Predefined capability taxonomies (apps define their own)
37. //! - Any policy logic (just enforcement)
38. 
39. use crate::types::{CapabilityId, Did, LogicalTimestamp};
40. use async_trait::async_trait;
41. use ordered_float::OrderedFloat;
42. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
43. use std::collections::HashMap;
44. use std::hash::Hash;
45. use std::time::Duration;
46. 
47. // ============================================================================
48. // Policy Decision Types
49. // ============================================================================
50. 
51. /// Result of a policy evaluation.
52. ///
53. /// The kernel enforces these decisions WITHOUT understanding their semantic origin.
54. /// Apps (trust, governance, ledger) populate ConstraintSet via PolicyOracle.
55. #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
56. pub enum PolicyDecision {
57.     /// Request is allowed, optionally with constraints
58.     Allow {
59.         /// Constraints the kernel will enforce
60.         constraints: ConstraintSet,
61.     },
62.     /// Request is denied
63.     Deny {
64.         /// Error describing why the request was denied
65.         reason: PolicyError,
66.     },
67. }
68. 
69. impl PolicyDecision {
70.     /// Create an Allow decision with no constraints.
71.     pub fn allow() -> Self {
72.         Self::Allow {
73.             constraints: ConstraintSet::default(),
74.         }
75.     }
76. 
77.     /// Create an Allow decision with constraints.
78.     pub fn allow_with(constraints: ConstraintSet) -> Self {
79.         Self::Allow { constraints }
80.     }
81. 
82.     /// Create a Deny decision.
83.     pub fn deny(reason: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
84.         Self::Deny {
85.             reason: PolicyError::Denied(reason.into()),
86.         }
87.     }
88. 
89.     /// Create a Deny decision with a PolicyError.
90.     pub fn deny_error(reason: PolicyError) -> Self {
91.         Self::Deny { reason }
92.     }
93. 
94.     /// Check if this decision allows the request.
95.     pub fn is_allowed(&self) -> bool {
96.         matches!(self, Self::Allow { .. })
97.     }
98. 
99.     /// Get constraints if allowed, None if denied.
100.     pub fn constraints(&self) -> Option<&ConstraintSet> {
101.         match self {
102.             Self::Allow { constraints } => Some(constraints),
103.             Self::Deny { .. } => None,
104.         }
105.     }
106. }
107. 
108. /// Error returned when a policy denies a request.
109. #[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
110. pub enum PolicyError {
111.     /// Generic denial with reason
112.     Denied(String),
113.     /// Actor not recognized
114.     UnknownActor,
115.     /// Resource not found
116.     ResourceNotFound,
117.     /// Insufficient privilege
118.     InsufficientPrivilege,
119.     /// Rate limit exceeded
120.     RateLimitExceeded,
121.     /// Capability expired
122.     CapabilityExpired,
123.     /// Capability revoked
124.     CapabilityRevoked,
125. }
126. 
127. impl std::fmt::Display for PolicyError {
128.     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
129.         match self {
130.             Self::Denied(reason) => write!(f, "Denied: {reason}"),
131.             Self::UnknownActor => write!(f, "Unknown actor"),
132.             Self::ResourceNotFound => write!(f, "Resource not found"),
133.             Self::InsufficientPrivilege => write!(f, "Insufficient privilege"),
134.             Self::RateLimitExceeded => write!(f, "Rate limit exceeded"),
135.             Self::CapabilityExpired => write!(f, "Capability expired"),
136.             Self::CapabilityRevoked => write!(f, "Capability revoked"),
137.         }
138.     }
139. }
140. 
141. impl std::error::Error for PolicyError {}
142. 
143. // ============================================================================
144. // Constraint Types
145. // ============================================================================
146. 
147. /// Kernel-enforced constraints.
148. ///
149. /// The kernel does NOT know WHY these values exist.
150. /// Apps (trust, governance, ledger) set them via PolicyOracle.

1. //! Meaning Firewall Validation Tests
2. //!
3. //! These tests verify that the kernel/app separation architecture is maintained.
4. //! The "meaning firewall" ensures kernel crates only deal with mechanical constraints
5. //! (e.g., `min_votes = 67`) and never domain-specific concepts (e.g., "supermajority").
6. //!
7. //! # Architecture Rule
8. //!
9. //! Kernel crates should only use types from icn-kernel-api:
10. //! - PolicyRequest, PolicyDecision, ConstraintSet
11. //! - Domain, ActionKind
12. //!
13. //! They should NOT use domain-specific types:
14. //! - TrustGraph, TrustClass, TrustScore (from icn-trust)
15. //! - GovernanceRules, DecisionType (from icn-governance)
16. //! - MembershipCriteria (from icn-entity/coop/community)
17. //!
18. //! # Strict Mode
19. //!
20. //! These tests run in CI and **fail on regressions**. The known violation counts
21. //! are pinned to exact values — adding new violations will break the build.
22. //! Reducing violations requires updating the pinned counts downward.
23. 
24. use std::path::PathBuf;
25. 
26. /// Core kernel crates that must not depend on domain crates.
27. const KERNEL_CRATES: &[&str] = &["icn-net", "icn-gateway", "icn-gossip", "icn-ledger"];
28. 
29. /// Domain-specific crates that kernel must not depend on directly.
30. const DOMAIN_CRATES: &[&str] = &["icn-trust", "icn-governance"];
31. 
32. /// Forbidden import patterns in kernel crates.
33. /// Used as reference for what constitutes a Meaning Firewall violation.
34. /// The strict_*_import_violations tests use `use icn_*::` patterns directly;
35. /// bare type names here are too broad for automated scanning (appear in docs).

58. fn get_workspace_root() -> PathBuf {
59.     let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
60.     manifest_dir
61.         .parent()
62.         .expect("Could not find crates directory")
63.         .to_path_buf()
64. }
65. 
66. fn read_cargo_toml(crate_name: &str) -> Option<String> {
67.     let path = get_workspace_root().join(crate_name).join("Cargo.toml");
68.     std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()
69. }
70. 
71. fn list_rust_files(crate_name: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
72.     let src_path = get_workspace_root().join(crate_name).join("src");
73.     let mut files = Vec::new();
74. 
75.     fn collect_rs_files(dir: &std::path::Path, files: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
76.         if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
77.             for entry in entries.flatten() {
78.                 let path = entry.path();
79.                 if path.is_dir() {
80.                     collect_rs_files(&path, files);
81.                 } else if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == "rs") {
82.                     files.push(path);
83.                 }
84.             }
85.         }
86.     }
87. 
88.     collect_rs_files(&src_path, &mut files);
89.     files
90. }
91. 
92. /// Check if a Cargo.toml contains a dependency on a specific crate.
93. fn has_dependency(cargo_toml: &str, dep_name: &str) -> bool {
94.     cargo_toml.contains(&format!("{dep_name} ="))
95.         || cargo_toml.contains(&format!("{dep_name}="))
96.         || cargo_toml.contains(&format!("{dep_name}.workspace"))
97.         || cargo_toml.contains(&format!("[dependencies.{dep_name}]"))
98.         || cargo_toml.contains(&format!("[dev-dependencies.{dep_name}]"))
99.         || cargo_toml.contains(&format!("[build-dependencies.{dep_name}]"))
100. }

1. //! Centralized trust policy engine
2. //!
3. //! This module provides a unified interface for all trust-based access decisions
4. //! across ICN subsystems. It combines trust class computation with capability-based
5. //! access control to determine what operations a peer is allowed to perform.
6. //!
7. //! # Architecture
8. //!
9. //! - **PolicySource trait**: Abstraction for policy lookup
10. //! - **TrustPolicy struct**: Per-peer policy combining limits + capabilities
11. //! - **Capability enum**: Fine-grained permissions for operations
12. //! - **TrustScoreProvider trait**: Abstraction for trust score computation
13. //! - **DefaultPolicySource**: Implementation using any `TrustScoreProvider`
14. 
15. use icn_identity::Did;
16. use icn_kernel_api::TrustClass;
17. use std::collections::HashMap;
18. use std::sync::Arc;
19. 
20. /// Trait for looking up trust policies
21. ///
22. /// This abstraction allows for different policy sources:
23. /// - DefaultPolicySource: Uses a TrustScoreProvider
24. /// - StaticPolicySource: Fixed policies for testing
25. /// - RemotePolicySource: Fetch policies from remote server
26. #[async_trait::async_trait]
27. pub trait PolicySource: Send + Sync {
28.     /// Get the trust policy for a DID
29.     async fn policy_for(&self, did: &Did) -> TrustPolicy;
30. }
31. 
32. /// Trust-based policy for a peer
33. ///
34. /// Combines resource limits with capability-based permissions.
35. #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
36. pub struct TrustPolicy {
37.     /// Trust class of the peer
38.     pub class: TrustClass,
39. 
40.     /// Maximum messages per second from this peer
41.     pub max_messages_per_second: u32,
42. 
43.     /// Maximum concurrent QUIC streams
44.     pub max_streams: u32,
45. 
46.     /// Allowed gossip topics (empty = all public topics allowed)
47.     pub allowed_topics: Vec<String>,
48. 
49.     /// Allowed capabilities
50.     pub allowed_capabilities: Vec<Capability>,
51. 
52.     /// Per-capability rate limiting quotas
53.     ///
54.     /// Provides granular control over expensive operations.
55.     /// If a capability is not in this map, the default is no quota (unlimited).
56.     pub capability_quotas: HashMap<Capability, CapabilityQuota>,
57. }
58. 
59. impl TrustPolicy {
60.     /// Check if peer can access a specific topic
61.     pub fn can_access_topic(&self, topic: &str) -> bool {
62.         // Empty list means all public topics are allowed
63.         self.allowed_topics.is_empty() || self.allowed_topics.contains(&topic.to_string())
64.     }
65. 
66.     /// Check if peer has a specific capability
67.     pub fn has_capability(&self, cap: &Capability) -> bool {
68.         self.allowed_capabilities.contains(cap)
69.     }
70. 
71.     /// Get the rate limiting quota for a specific capability
72.     ///
73.     /// Returns `None` if the capability is not allowed, or if no quota is set
74.     /// (meaning unlimited for that capability).
75.     pub fn quota_for(&self, cap: &Capability) -> Option<&CapabilityQuota> {
76.         if !self.has_capability(cap) {
77.             return None;
78.         }
79.         self.capability_quotas.get(cap)
80.     }
