212.     /// Apply a delta to the balances
213.     ///
214.     /// Uses checked arithmetic to prevent overflow. Returns error if
215.     /// the calculation would overflow.
216.     pub fn apply_delta(&mut self, delta: &AccountDelta) -> Result<(), crate::LedgerError> {
217.         if delta.account_id != self.account_id {
218.             return Ok(()); // Delta is for a different account
219.         }
220. 
221.         let current = self.get(&delta.currency);
222.         let change = delta.net_change()?;
223.         let new_balance = current.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| {
224.             crate::LedgerError::ArithmeticOverflow(format!(
225.                 "overflow in apply_delta: {} + {} for account {} currency {}",
226.                 current, change, self.account_id, delta.currency
227.             ))
228.         })?;
229.         self.balances.insert(delta.currency.clone(), new_balance);
230.         Ok(())
231.     }
232. }

435. /// Configuration for witness requirements on a ledger
436. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
437. pub struct WitnessConfig {
438.     /// Default policy for all entries
439.     pub default_policy: WitnessPolicy,
440. 
441.     /// Value threshold above which witnesses are required
442.     /// If None, policy applies to all entries regardless of value
443.     pub threshold: Option<u64>,

445.     /// Grace period (in seconds) to collect witness signatures.
446.     /// After this time, unsigned entries may be rejected.
447.     ///
448.     /// This is validated in `Ledger::validate_witness_signatures()` which
449.     /// rejects signatures older than this timeout.
450.     pub collection_timeout_secs: u64,
451. 
452.     /// Minimum trust score required for witnesses (optional).
453.     /// When set, witnesses must have at least this trust score with
454.     /// all parties involved in the transaction (author and counterparties).
455.     ///
456.     /// This integrates with ICN's trust graph to prevent collusion with
457.     /// unknown/untrusted entities. Trust scores are computed using the
458.     /// combined score from all three trust dimensions (social, economic, technical).
459.     ///
460.     /// Example values:
461.     /// - 0.1 = Known trust class (minimal requirement)
462.     /// - 0.4 = Partner trust class (recommended for high-value transfers)
463.     /// - 0.7 = Federated trust class (maximum security)
464.     ///
465.     /// If None, trust validation is skipped (backward compatible behavior).
466.     pub min_witness_trust: Option<f64>,
467. }

470.     fn default() -> Self {

474.             collection_timeout_secs: 300, // 5 minutes default

476.         }
477.     }

504.     /// Create config requiring counterparty signature with minimum trust score
505.     ///

507.     ///
508.     /// Panics if `min_trust` is not in the valid range [0.0, 1.0] or is NaN.
509.     pub fn counterparty_with_trust(threshold: u64, min_trust: f64) -> Self {
510.         assert!(
511.             (0.0..=1.0).contains(&min_trust) && !min_trust.is_nan(),
512.             "min_trust must be in range [0.0, 1.0], got {}",
513.             min_trust
514.         );
515.         WitnessConfig {
516.             default_policy: WitnessPolicy::Counterparty,
517.             threshold: Some(threshold),
518.             collection_timeout_secs: 300,
519.             min_witness_trust: Some(min_trust),
520.         }
521.     }

524.     ///

526.     ///
527.     /// Panics if `min_trust` is not in the valid range [0.0, 1.0] or is NaN.
528.     pub fn quorum_with_trust(required: u32, witnesses: Vec<Did>, min_trust: f64) -> Self {
529.         assert!(
530.             (0.0..=1.0).contains(&min_trust) && !min_trust.is_nan(),
531.             "min_trust must be in range [0.0, 1.0], got {}",
532.             min_trust
533.         );
534.         WitnessConfig {
535.             default_policy: WitnessPolicy::Quorum {
536.                 required,
537.                 witnesses,
538.             },
539.             threshold: None,
540.             collection_timeout_secs: 300,
541.             min_witness_trust: Some(min_trust),
542.         }

545.     /// Determine the effective policy for a given entry value
546.     pub fn effective_policy(&self, entry_value: u64) -> &WitnessPolicy {
547.         match self.threshold {
548.             Some(thresh) if entry_value < thresh => &WitnessPolicy::None,
549.             _ => &self.default_policy,
550.         }
551.     }

556. pub struct WitnessSignature {

559.

566.     /// - Rejects future timestamps (beyond 5s clock skew tolerance)
567.     /// - Rejects expired signatures (older than `WitnessConfig::collection_timeout_secs`)
568.     pub signed_at: u64,
569. }

582. /// A journal entry with attached witness signatures
583. ///
584. /// This wraps a JournalEntry with the required witness signatures
585. /// based on the ledger's WitnessPolicy. The entry hash is signed
586. /// by witnesses, not the full entry content.
587. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
588. pub struct WitnessedEntry {
589.     /// The underlying journal entry
590.     pub entry: JournalEntry,
591. 
592.     /// Witness signatures collected for this entry
593.     pub witness_signatures: Vec<WitnessSignature>,
594. 
595.     /// The policy that was applied when collecting signatures
596.     pub policy_applied: WitnessPolicy,
597. }
598. 
599. impl WitnessedEntry {
600.     /// Create a new witnessed entry with no signatures yet
601.     pub fn new(entry: JournalEntry, policy: WitnessPolicy) -> Self {
602.         WitnessedEntry {
603.             entry,
604.             witness_signatures: Vec::new(),
605.             policy_applied: policy,
606.         }
607.     }
608. 
609.     /// Add a witness signature
610.     pub fn add_signature(&mut self, sig: WitnessSignature) {
611.         self.witness_signatures.push(sig);
612.     }
613. 
614.     /// Check if the entry has sufficient signatures for the applied policy
615.     ///
616.     /// Note: This only checks that the policy requirements are met structurally.
617.     /// Cryptographic signature validation must be performed separately by the caller.
618.     pub fn has_sufficient_signatures(&self) -> bool {
619.         match &self.policy_applied {
620.             WitnessPolicy::None => true,
621.             WitnessPolicy::Counterparty => {
622.                 // Require at least one witness who is a non-author counterparty
623.                 let counterparties: std::collections::HashSet<_> = self
624.                     .entry
625.                     .accounts
626.                     .iter()
627.                     .map(|d| &d.account_id)
628.                     .filter(|id| **id != self.entry.author)
629.                     .collect();
630.                 self.witness_signatures
631.                     .iter()
632.                     .any(|s| counterparties.contains(&s.witness))
633.             }
634.             WitnessPolicy::Quorum {
635.                 required,
636.                 witnesses,
637.             } => {
638.                 // Only count signatures from authorized witnesses (unique DIDs)
639.                 let allowed_witnesses: std::collections::HashSet<_> = witnesses.iter().collect();
640.                 let signed_authorized: std::collections::HashSet<_> = self
641.                     .witness_signatures
642.                     .iter()
643.                     .map(|s| &s.witness)
644.                     .filter(|w| allowed_witnesses.contains(w))
645.                     .collect();
646.                 signed_authorized.len() >= *required as usize
647.             }
648.             WitnessPolicy::AllParties => {
649.                 // Each non-author account must have signed as a witness
650.                 let unique_accounts: std::collections::HashSet<_> = self
651.                     .entry
652.                     .accounts
653.                     .iter()
654.                     .map(|d| &d.account_id)
655.                     .filter(|id| **id != self.entry.author)
656.                     .collect();
657.                 let signed_witnesses: std::collections::HashSet<_> =
658.                     self.witness_signatures.iter().map(|s| &s.witness).collect();
659.                 unique_accounts.iter().all(|a| signed_witnesses.contains(a))
660.             }
661.         }
662.     }
663. 
664.     /// Get the entry hash that witnesses should sign
665.     pub fn entry_hash(&self) -> Option<&ContentHash> {
666.         self.entry.id.as_ref()
667.     }
668. 
669.     /// Count unique witnesses who have signed
670.     pub fn unique_witness_count(&self) -> usize {
671.         let witnesses: std::collections::HashSet<_> =
672.             self.witness_signatures.iter().map(|s| &s.witness).collect();
673.         witnesses.len()
674.     }
675. }
676.

18.     /// Create a new builder with the given author
19.     pub fn new(author: Did) -> Self {

36.     pub fn debit(mut self, account_id: Did, currency: String, amount: i64) -> Self {

38.             .push(AccountDelta::debit(account_id, currency, amount));
39.         self
40.     }
41. 
42.     /// Add a credit to an account
43.     pub fn credit(mut self, account_id: Did, currency: String, amount: i64) -> Self {

45.             .push(AccountDelta::credit(account_id, currency, amount));
46.         self

52.         self
53.     }
54.

56.     pub fn add_parent(mut self, parent: ContentHash) -> Self {
57.         self.parents.push(parent);
58.         self
59.     }
60. 
61.     /// Set a nonce for replay protection.
62.     ///
63.     /// When set, the nonce is included in the content hash, ensuring
64.     /// entries with identical content produce distinct hashes. Use this
65.     /// for commons credit entries where the nonce is the `receipt_id`.
66.     pub fn nonce(mut self, nonce: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
67.         self.nonce = Some(nonce);
68.         self
69.     }
70. 
71.     /// Build and validate the journal entry
72.     pub fn build(self) -> Result<JournalEntry> {
73.         // Validate double-entry invariant: Σ debits == Σ credits per currency
74.         validate_double_entry(&self.accounts)?;
75. 
76.         // Validate that amounts are positive
77.         validate_positive_amounts(&self.accounts)?;
78. 
79.         // Get current timestamp in milliseconds (security-critical: reject if clock is invalid)
80.         let timestamp = icn_time::try_current_timestamp_millis()
81.             .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Cannot create journal entry: {e}"))?;
82. 
83.         let mut entry = JournalEntry {
84.             id: None,
85.             timestamp,
86.             author: self.author,
87.             contract_ref: self.contract_ref,
88.             accounts: self.accounts,
89.             parents: self.parents,
90.             signature: None, // Will be set by caller
91.             nonce: self.nonce,
92.         };
93. 
94.         // Compute the content hash
95.         entry.compute_hash()?;
96. 
97.         Ok(entry)
98.     }
99. }
100. 
101. /// Validate double-entry bookkeeping invariant
102. /// For each currency, the sum of debits must equal the sum of credits
103. fn validate_double_entry(accounts: &[AccountDelta]) -> Result<()> {
104.     // Group by currency and sum debits/credits
105.     let mut currency_totals: HashMap<String, (i64, i64)> = HashMap::new();
106. 
107.     for delta in accounts {
108.         let (total_debits, total_credits) = currency_totals
109.             .entry(delta.currency.clone())
110.             .or_insert((0, 0));
111. 
112.         *total_debits += delta.debit.unwrap_or(0);
113.         *total_credits += delta.credit.unwrap_or(0);
114.     }
115. 
116.     // Check that debits == credits for each currency
117.     for (currency, (debits, credits)) in currency_totals.iter() {
118.         if debits != credits {
119.             bail!(
120.                 "Double-entry invariant violated for currency '{currency}': debits={debits}, credits={credits}"
121.             );
122.         }
123.     }
124. 
125.     Ok(())
126. }
127. 
128. /// Validate that all amounts are positive
129. fn validate_positive_amounts(accounts: &[AccountDelta]) -> Result<()> {
130.     for delta in accounts {
131.         if let Some(debit) = delta.debit {
132.             if debit < 0 {
133.                 bail!(
134.                     "Negative debit amount not allowed: {} for account {}",
135.                     debit,
136.                     delta.account_id
137.                 );
138.             }
139.         }
140. 
141.         if let Some(credit) = delta.credit {
142.             if credit < 0 {
143.                 bail!(
144.                     "Negative credit amount not allowed: {} for account {}",
145.                     credit,
146.                     delta.account_id
147.                 );
148.             }
149.         }
150.     }

1. //! Use-based resource access model
2. //!
3. //! This module implements a use-based access model for resources that prevents
4. //! rent-seeking and speculation by requiring active use rather than passive ownership.
5. //!
6. //! # Core Concepts
7. //!
8. //! - **UseAccess**: Time-limited, renewable access rights with accumulation limits
9. //! - **Stewardship**: Access tied to duties and responsibilities
10. //! - **Anti-Speculation**: Rules preventing rent-seeking and profit from access transfers
11. //! - **Witness Signatures**: Optional cryptographic attestation for handoff procedures
12. //!
13. //! # Witness Signatures for Handoff Procedures
14. //!
15. //! For high-value resources, `HandoffProcedure` supports optional witness requirements:
16. //!
17. //! ```rust,ignore
18. //! use icn_ledger::use_access::{AccessModel, ResourceAccess, StewardshipDuty, UsageEvent};
19. //! use icn_entity::EntityId;
20. //!
21. //! // Create stewardship with witness-verified handoff
22. //! let witness1 = "did:icn:witness1".to_string();
23. //! let witness2 = "did:icn:witness2".to_string();
24. //!
25. //! let access = ResourceAccess::new(
26. //!     "high-value-equipment".to_string(),
27. //!     EntityId::individual_from_did(steward_did.clone()),
28. //!     AccessModel::Stewardship {
29. //!         duties: vec![StewardshipDuty::HandoffProcedure {
30. //!             steps: vec![
31. //!                 "Document current state".to_string(),
32. //!                 "Transfer credentials".to_string(),
33. //!             ],
34. //!             witnesses: Some(vec![witness1.clone(), witness2.clone()]),
35. //!             min_witness_signatures: Some(2),  // Require both witnesses
36. //!         }],
37. //!         review_period_seconds: 90 * 24 * 3600,
38. //!     },
39. //! );
40. //!
41. //! // Complete handoff step with witness attestation
42. //! let step_event = UsageEvent::handoff_step(timestamp, "Documented state", 0)
43. //!     .with_witness(witness1.clone())
44. //!     .with_witness(witness2.clone());
45. //! access.record_usage_event(step_event)?;
46. //!
47. //! // Validate handoff completion before transfer
48. //! access.validate_handoff_completion()?;
49. //! ```
50. //!
51. //! **Backward Compatibility**: When `witnesses` is `None`, no witness validation is performed,
52. //! maintaining existing behavior for community-context resources.
53. //!
54. //! # Example
55. //!
56. //! ```rust,ignore
57. //! use icn_ledger::use_access::{AccessModel, ResourceAccess};
58. //! use icn_entity::EntityId;
59. //!
60. //! // Create use-based access
61. //! let access = ResourceAccess::new(
62. //!     "tool-shed-001".to_string(),
63. //!     EntityId::individual_from_did(alice_did.clone()),
64. //!     AccessModel::UseAccess {
65. //!         duration_seconds: 7 * 24 * 3600, // 1 week
66. //!         renewable: true,
67. //!         max_accumulated: 4, // Max 4 weeks total
68. //!     },
69. //! );
70. //!
71. //! // Record usage
72. //! access.record_usage(current_time, "Used for repairs")?;
73. //!
74. //! // Check if idle
75. //! if access.is_idle(current_time, 48 * 3600) {
76. //!     // Revoke due to non-use
77. //! }
78. //! ```
79.

85. /// Errors related to resource access
86. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Error, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
87. pub enum AccessError {
88.     /// Access has expired
89.     #[error("Access expired at {0}")]
90.     Expired(u64),
91. 
92.     /// Access is not renewable
93.     #[error("Access is not renewable")]
94.     NotRenewable,
95. 
96.     /// Maximum accumulated duration reached
97.     #[error("Maximum accumulated access reached: {0} renewals")]
98.     MaxAccumulatedReached(u32),
99. 
100.     /// Stewardship duty not fulfilled
101.     #[error("Stewardship duty not fulfilled: {0}")]
102.     DutyUnfulfilled(String),

1. //! Labor shares and cooperative bonds for Razeto integration
2. //!
3. //! This module implements Razeto's Cooperative Share Exchange concepts:
4. //! - Labor shares representing accumulated value from worker contributions
5. //! - Cooperative bonds as debt securities for inter-coop financing
6. //! - Surplus allocation for periodic distribution to shareholders

## Gap Analysis: Economic Primitives Foundation (35-40% Coverage)

**Good news: The ICN ledger already has significant foundational structures for typed assets**, though they're not yet unified into a cohesive asset type system. Here's what exists:

### **Existing Asset-Related Structures:**

1. **Core Entry System** (`types.rs`, `entry.rs`)
   - `JournalEntry`: Double-entry ledger with `AccountDelta` (debit/credit tracking)
   - `Currency`: Mutual credit or issuer-backed definitions with decimals
   - **Gap**: No asset type classification (durable, consumable, perishable, service)

2. **Resource Access Model** (`use_access.rs`) ⭐ **Strongest Foundation**
   - `ResourceAccess`: Time-limited, renewable use-based access
   - `AccessModel::UseAccess`: Duration, renewability, accumulation caps
   - `AccessModel::Stewardship`: Duties, handoff procedures with witness attestation
   - `AntiSpeculationRules`: Prevents rent-seeking transfers
   - **Maps to**: Durable goods (equipment) + Service (maintenance obligations)
   - **Missing**: Perishable/consumable lifecycle tracking

3. **Labor Shares** (`labor_shares.rs`) ⭐ **Strong Foundation**
   - `LaborShare`: Earned through contribution, not purchased (anti-speculation)
   - `ShareStatus`: Active, Redeeming, Redeemed (lifecycle)
   - `ShareEvent`: Audit trail (Created → LaborContributed → SurplusAllocated → FullyRedeemed)
   - **Maps to**: Economic value representation (hybrid equity/credit)
   - **Missing**: Transformation tracking (when labor becomes surplus)

4. **Treasury & Budget System** (`treasury/`)
   - `TreasuryBudget`: Purpose-bound allocation with spending tracking
   - Budget periods, status lifecycle, thresholds
   - **Maps to**: Allocation/consumption of resources
   - **Missing**: Asset class boundaries

5. **Dispute & Quarantine** (`types.rs`)
   - `DisputeStatus` & `DisputeOutcome`: Settlement, WriteOff
   - `QuarantinedEntry`: Reasons (InvariantViolation, CharterViolation)
   - **Maps to**: Conflict resolution for asset claims
   - **Missing**: Asset-specific dispute types

6. **Witness Attestation** (`types.rs`) ⭐
   - `WitnessPolicy`: Counterparty, Quorum, AllParties
   - `WitnessedEntry`: Signature collection and validation
   - **Maps to**: Claim verification infrastructure
   - **Missing**: Asset-specific witness requirements

### **What's Missing for Typed Assets (35% → 60%+):**

| Dimension | Current | Needed |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| **Asset Classification** | String currencies | Enum: Durable/Consumable/Perishable/Service |
| **Lifecycle States** | Basic statuses | Acquisition → Use → Transformation → Disposal |
| **Transformation Tracking** | Labor hours only | Resource inputs/outputs (e.g., tools → labor → output) |
| **Claim Structures** | Debits/Credits | Asset-backed claims with custody/lien support |
| **Degradation** | None | Perishability tracking, depreciation schedules |
| **Custody Rules** | None | Asset-specific access policies (e.g., tool checkout, seasonal storage) |

### **Immediate Foundation to Build On:**

1. **Extend `Currency` → `AssetType` enum**
   ```rust
   pub enum AssetType {
       Durable { depreciation_years: u32, serial_number: Option\<String\> },
       Consumable { unit: String, expiry: Option\<u64\> },
       Perishable { shelf_life_seconds: u64, temperature_requirements: Option\<String\> },
       Service { hours_per_unit: f64, skill_level: String },
   }
   ```

2. **Link `ResourceAccess` + `LaborShare` + `JournalEntry`**
   - ResourceAccess already supports handoff with witnesses
   - LaborShare tracks contributions → surplus allocation (transformation)
   - JournalEntry provides immutable audit trail

3. **Enhance `UseAccessModel` for consumables**
   - Add `consumed_units` tracking
   - Tie to `Treasury::spent_amount` for ledger consistency

4. **Leverage existing structures**:
   - Witness attestation → custody claims
   - Dispute resolution → asset recovery
   - Labor events → transformation audit trail

**The 35-40% gap exists not from missing data structures, but from lack of unified asset semantics across these modules.** The building blocks are there; they need orchestration.

1. # Vision-to-Implementation Gap Analysis
2. 
3. **Document ID**: ICN-GAP-VISION-01
4. **Created**: 2025-11-28
5. **Purpose**: Map the ICN vision to implementation status and prioritize closing gaps
6. 
7. ---
8. 
9. ## Executive Summary
10. 
11. ICN is **substrate-complete** (~80% architecturally sound) but **integration-incomplete** (~50% functionally integrated). The core protocols work; they're not connected into the coherent experience the vision describes.
12. 
13. **Critical Finding**: The vision describes "a global cooperative operating layer" but several key pieces are either:
14. - Code exists but never wired into the daemon
15. - CLI commands are stubs that print "TODO"
16. - Security holes that would be unacceptable in production
17. 
18. ---
19. 
20. ## Vision Components Mapped to Implementation
21. 
22. ### 1. Identity You Own, Not Rent
23. 
24. **Vision**: "Device-level DIDs that you actually possess. Identity becomes portable, multi-device, cryptographically verifiable, independent of institutions."
25. 
26. **Implementation Status**:
27. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
28. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
29. | DID generation | ✅ | ✅ | Ed25519 keypairs, `did:icn:` format |
30. | Keystore (Age-encrypted) | ✅ | ✅ | v2.1 with TLS + X25519 |
31. | Multi-device DID Document | ✅ | ⚠️ | Code exists, IdentityActor commented out |
32. | Device add/revoke | ✅ | ❌ | CLI stubs: "TODO: Sign this event" |
33. | Social recovery | ✅ | ❌ | CLI stubs: "TODO: Publish to gossip" |
34. | Identity sync via gossip | ✅ | ❌ | `identity:updates` topic defined, not used |
35. 
36. **Gap**: Multi-device identity is CLI-local only. The IdentityActor that would sync across nodes is commented out in `supervisor.rs:315`.
37. 
38. **Files**:
39. - `icn-identity/src/did_document.rs` - DID Document v2 ✅
40. - `icn-identity/src/bundle.rs` - IdentityBundle ✅
41. - `icn-core/src/supervisor.rs:315` - IdentityActor COMMENTED OUT
42. - `bins/icnctl/src/main.rs:3070,3158` - device approve/revoke stubs
43. 
44. ---
45. 
46. ### 2. Web-of-Participation (Trust Graph)
47. 
48. **Vision**: "You trust people you've worked with. And you trust who they trust to the degree that makes sense. This creates a dynamic graph of actual participation."
49. 
50. **Implementation Status**:
51. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
52. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
53. | Trust graph storage | ✅ | ✅ | Sled-backed |
54. | Transitive trust computation | ✅ | ✅ | PageRank-style algorithm |
55. | Trust-gated rate limiting | ✅ | ✅ | 4 trust classes |
56. | Trust-gated gossip topics | ✅ | ✅ | AccessControl::TrustGated |
57. | Trust-gated compute | ✅ | ✅ | MIN_TRUST_SUBMIT/EXECUTE |
58. | Trust in policies | ✅ | ⚠️ | Direct trust only, not transitive |
59. 
60. **Gap**: Transitive trust computation works but is NOT used in access control policies. Only direct trust scores are checked.
61. 
62. **Files**:
63. - `icn-trust/src/graph.rs` - Trust graph ✅
64. - `icn-trust/src/compute.rs` - Transitive computation ✅
65. - `icn-net/src/rate_limit.rs` - Trust-based rate limiting ✅
66. 
67. ---
68. 
69. ### 3. Mutual Credit Economy
70. 
71. **Vision**: "No tokens to speculate on. No miners. No global blockchain. It models reciprocity: when you contribute value, you earn credit."
72. 
73. **Implementation Status**:
74. | Component | Code | Integrated | Notes |
75. |-----------|------|------------|-------|
76. | Double-entry ledger | ✅ | ✅ | Merkle-DAG journal |
77. | Multi-currency | ✅ | ✅ | hours, USD, kWh, etc. |
78. | Dynamic credit limits | ✅ | ✅ | Trust + history based |
79. | New member protection | ✅ | ✅ | Progressive ramping |
80. | Dispute resolution | ✅ | ✅ | File, mediate, resolve |
81. | Cooperative treasury | ❌ | ❌ | No collective fund concept |
82. 
83. **Gap**: No treasury DID per cooperative. Payments are attributed to individuals, not coops. Communities can't hold collective funds.
84. 
85. **Files**:
86. - `icn-ledger/src/ledger.rs` - Core ledger ✅
87. - `icn-ledger/src/credit_policy.rs` - Dynamic limits ✅
88. - `icn-ledger/src/dispute.rs` - Dispute resolution ✅
89. 
90. ---
91. 
92. ### 4. Contracts as Computation (CCL)

1. # ICN Roadmap
2. 
3. **Last Updated**: 2026-01-31
4. **Current Focus**: Phase 3 State Generalization + Kernel Crate Cleanup
5. **Target**: Clean kernel with pluggable first-party and third-party apps
6. 
7. ---
8. 
9. ## Strategic Context
10. 
11. ICN is infrastructure for a **parallel political economy** — enabling cooperatives, communities, and federations to deliver better material outcomes than traditional capitalist and captured democratic systems.
12. 
13. **Core Vision**: ICN is not just infrastructure *for* cooperatives — it is **cooperative infrastructure that governs itself democratically**. The protocols are adjustable by the organizations using them.
14. 
15. ### Architecture Reset (2026-01-26)
16. 
17. The previous roadmap (Phases 19-35) has been superseded by the **Kernel/App Separation** initiative. This architectural reset:
18. 
19. 1. **Separates kernel from apps** - Kernel provides 8 generic primitives; apps implement domain logic
20. 2. **Establishes the "Meaning Firewall"** - Kernel never understands domain semantics
21. 3. **Enables third-party apps** - Same APIs as first-party apps
22. 4. **Simplifies the codebase** - From 27 tightly-coupled crates to ~12 kernel crates + apps
23. 
24. **See**: [KERNEL_APP_SEPARATION.md](../KERNEL_APP_SEPARATION.md) for full architectural documentation.

93. ## The Meaning Firewall
94. 
95. The core architectural principle driving this work:
96. 
97. ```
98. CCL Document (constitution / bylaws / treaty)
99.          ↓
100. App Interpreter (Governance / Membership / Ledger / Federation)
101.          ↓
102. PolicyDecision { constraints }
103.          ↓
104. Kernel enforces constraints mechanically
105. ```
106. 
107. **Example**: The kernel never sees "constitutional amendment" or "supermajority" — only:
108. - `min_votes = 67`
109. - `quorum_required = 50`
110. - `deadline = 1706000000`
111. 
112. This ensures:
113. 1. Apps can implement any governance model
114. 2. Kernel remains simple and auditable
115. 3. Third-party apps have equal capabilities
116.

149. ### 8 Kernel Primitives
150. 
151. | Primitive | Purpose |

153. | Identity | DID management, key operations |
154. | Authorization | Capability-based access control via PolicyOracle |
155. | State | Persistent storage (KV, Log, Blob) |
156. | Compute | Event/request routing (Reducer/Service split) |

158. | Time | Clocks, timers |
159. | Coordination | Consensus, CRDTs |

163. 
164. ## CCL: Constitutional Layer
165. 
166. CCL (Cooperative Contract Language) is the declarative layer for expressing:
167. - Entity constitutions and bylaws
168. - Governance rules and voting procedures
169. - Economic policies (surplus allocation, credit limits)
170. - Federation agreements
171. 
172. **Schema v0 complete** (PR #855):
173. - `entity.rs` - Cooperatives, communities, federations, membership
174. - `governance.rs` - Bodies, decisions, delegation
175. - `economics.rs` - Capital, surplus, credit
176. - `agreement.rs` - Federation agreements, boundary protocols
177. 
178. **Key Insight**: Federation agreements use **binary boundary outcomes**:
179. 
180. ```yaml
181. boundary_outcome:
182.   type: binary  # approved | rejected
183. ```
184. 
185. Federation A uses consensus. Federation B uses majority vote. The agreement doesn't care — it only asks "Did each party approve?"
186. 
187. **Internal process is sovereign. Boundary outcomes are interoperable.**
188.

1. # Trust Computation Algorithm Unification
2. 
3. **Date:** 2026-02-01  
4. **Issue:** #902 - Unify trust computation algorithm between TrustGraph and TrustPolicyOracle  
5. **PR:** [pending]
6. 
7. ## Summary
8. 
9. Successfully unified the trust computation algorithm between standalone mode (TrustManager/TrustPolicyOracle) and actor-backed mode (TrustGraph) by extracting a shared computation function to eliminate divergence.
10. 
11. ## Problem Statement
12. 
13. Two different implementations computed trust scores:
14. 
15. | Mode | Location | Implementation |
16. |------|----------|----------------|
17. | Standalone | `compute_trust_from_edges_map()` in `trust_mgr.rs` | Manual iteration and averaging |
18. | Actor-backed | `TrustGraph::compute_trust_score_weighted()` | Manual iteration and averaging |
19. 
20. While both used the same algorithm (70% direct, 30% transitive for legacy weights), the implementations were duplicated. This could lead to:
21. - Subtle divergence over time if implementations are updated independently
22. - Confusion when debugging trust score differences
23. - Extra maintenance burden
24. 
25. The divergence was documented as intentional (lines 1035-1051 in `trust_mgr.rs`), but the recommendation was to unify (Option B).
26. 
27. ## Solution
28. 
29. ### Implementation Approach
30. 
31. **Option B: Extract Shared Function**
32. 
33. Created `icn-trust/src/computation.rs` with a single parameterized function:
34. 
35. ```rust
36. pub fn compute_trust_score<I>(
37.     direct_score: f64,
38.     intermediates: I,
39.     weights: ScoringWeights,
40. ) -> f64
41. where
42.     I: Iterator<Item = (f64, f64)>,
43. ```
44. 
45. This function:
46. 1. Takes direct trust score (0.0 if no edge)
47. 2. Takes iterator of (intermediate_trust, indirect_trust) pairs
48. 3. Takes configurable weights (direct/transitive)
49. 4. Returns combined score in [0.0, 1.0]
50. 
51. ### Changes Made
52. 
53. **New Module:**
54. - `icn-trust/src/computation.rs` (203 lines)
55.   - Core algorithm implementation
56.   - 9 comprehensive unit tests
57.   - Full documentation with examples
58. 
59. **Refactored:**
60. 
61. 1. **TrustGraph** (`icn-trust/src/lib.rs`):
62.    ```rust
63.    // Before: Manual loop computing transitive_sum/count
64.    // After: Build iterator and delegate to shared function
65.    let intermediates: Vec<_> = own_edges
66.        .into_iter()
67.        .filter(|edge| edge.target != *target)
68.        .filter_map(|intermediate_edge| {
69.            self.get_edge(&intermediate_edge.target, target)
70.                .ok()
71.                .flatten()
72.                .map(|indirect_edge| {
73.                    (intermediate_edge.score.value(), indirect_edge.score.value())
74.                })
75.        })
76.        .collect();
77.    
78.    let final_score = crate::computation::compute_trust_score(
79.        direct_score,
80.        intermediates.iter().copied(),
81.        weights,
82.    );
83.    ```
84. 
85. 2. **TrustManager** (`icn-gateway/src/trust_mgr.rs`):
86.    - `compute_trust_from_edges_map()`: Now uses shared function
87.    - `compute_trust_score_local()`: Now uses shared function
88.    - `compute_trust_score_local_async()`: Now uses shared function
89.    - Removed unused `DIRECT_TRUST_WEIGHT` and `TRANSITIVE_TRUST_WEIGHT` constants
90. 
91. **Tests:**
92. - Added `test_algorithm_consistency_standalone_vs_actor_backed()` in gateway
93. - Validates identical scores across all three scenarios:
94.   1. Direct trust only
95.   2. Single intermediary
96.   3. Multiple intermediaries (averaging)
97. 
98. **Documentation:**
99. - Updated `ARCHITECTURE.md` Section 2.2
100. - Documented v2 unified algorithm
101. - Added implementation location and consistency guarantee
102. 
103. ## Verification
104. 
105. ### Test Results
106. 
107. ```bash
108. # Trust crate tests
109. cargo test -p icn-trust --lib
110. # Result: ok. 160 passed; 0 failed
111. 
112. # Gateway crate tests  
113. cargo test -p icn-gateway --lib
114. # Result: ok. 438 passed; 0 failed
115. 
116. # Consistency test
117. cargo test -p icn-gateway --lib test_algorithm_consistency
118. # Result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
119. 
120. # Full workspace build
121. cargo build
122. # Result: Finished `dev` profile
123. ```
124. 
125. ### Algorithm Validation
126. 
127. The consistency test validates that for identical trust graph configurations:
128. 
129. ```rust
130. // Scenario: Alice trusts Bob (0.9), Bob trusts Carol (0.7)
131. let score_standalone = standalone.compute_trust_score(&alice, &carol);
132. let score_actor = graph.compute_trust_score(&carol).unwrap();
133. 
134. assert!((score_standalone - score_actor).abs() < 0.0001);
135. // Both: 0.0 * 0.7 + (0.9 * 0.7) * 0.3 = 0.189
136. ```
137. 
138. All scenarios pass with epsilon < 0.0001, confirming perfect consistency.
139. 
140. ## Benefits
141. 
142. 1. **Single Source of Truth**: One algorithm, guaranteed consistency
143. 2. **Easier Maintenance**: Changes to algorithm propagate everywhere
144. 3. **Better Testing**: Can validate algorithm in isolation
145. 4. **Production Confidence**: Dev/test behavior matches production
146. 5. **Flexible Weighting**: Easy to adjust weights per trust graph type
147. 
148. ## Design Decisions
149. 
150. ### Why Iterator Pattern?
151. 
152. The shared function accepts `Iterator<Item = (f64, f64)>` rather than `Vec`:
153. 
154. ```rust
155. pub fn compute_trust_score<I>(
156.     direct_score: f64,
157.     intermediates: I,  // Iterator, not Vec
158.     weights: ScoringWeights,
159. ) -> f64
160. where
161.     I: Iterator<Item = (f64, f64)>,
162. ```
163. 
164. **Rationale:**
165. - More flexible: Callers can use lazy iterators or collected vectors
166. - No allocation penalty: Can compute on-the-fly without Vec allocation
167. - Composable: Easy to chain filters and maps
168. 
169. **Trade-off:**
170. - Async code must collect to Vec first (can't await in iterator)
171. - This is fine: async version already iterates sequentially anyway
172. 
173. ### Why Collect in TrustGraph?
174. 
175. TrustGraph collects intermediates to Vec before calling shared function:
176. 
177. ```rust
178. let intermediates: Vec<_> = own_edges.into_iter()...collect();
179. let final_score = crate::computation::compute_trust_score(
180.     direct_score,
181.     intermediates.iter().copied(),
182.     weights,
183. );
184. ```
185. 
186. **Rationale:**
187. - Enables debug logging of transitive_score separately
188. - No performance penalty (same iteration count)
189. - Makes debugging easier (can inspect intermediates)
190. 
191. ## Performance Impact
192. 
193. ### Before vs After
194. 
195. **Before:** Manual loop in each location
196. - TrustGraph: Iterate edges, accumulate sum/count
197. - TrustManager: Iterate edges, accumulate sum/count
198. 
199. **After:** Delegate to shared function
200. - Builds iterator/vector of pairs
201. - Passes to shared function
202. - Shared function accumulates sum/count
203. 
204. **Net Impact:** Neutral
205. - Same algorithmic complexity: O(n) where n = number of outgoing edges
206. - Same number of edge lookups
207. - Minimal overhead from iterator abstraction (likely optimized away)
208. 
209. **Verified:** All existing benchmarks would show no regression (if we had them).
210. 
211. ## Future Work
212. 
213. ### Potential Enhancements
214. 
215. 1. **Multi-hop Transitive Trust**
216.    - Current: 1-hop only (A → B → C)
217.    - Future: Configurable max hops with decay factor
218.    - Would require different algorithm, but easy to add new function
219. 
220. 2. **Path Quality Weighting**
221.    - Current: Simple average of all paths
222.    - Future: Weight by path quality (shorter paths = higher weight)
223.    - Can be added to shared function without breaking changes
224. 
225. 3. **Caching at Computation Layer**
226.    - Current: Caching at TrustGraph layer only
227.    - Future: Cache in shared function with invalidation strategy
228.    - Would benefit all callers
229. 
230. 4. **Performance Benchmarks**
231.    - Add criterion benchmarks for `compute_trust_score()`
232.    - Validate that iteration pattern has no overhead
233.    - Track performance over time
234. 
235. ## References
236. 
237. - Issue #902: "Unify trust computation algorithm"
238. - `icn-trust/src/computation.rs` - Implementation
239. - `icn-gateway/src/trust_mgr.rs` - Gateway integration
240. - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` Section 2.2 - Algorithm documentation
241. 
242. ## Lessons Learned
243. 
244. 1. **Extract Early**: Algorithm duplication caught early prevented divergence
245. 2. **Test First**: Consistency test validated unification before merging
246. 3. **Document Why**: Comments about intentional differences helped understand problem
247. 4. **Iterator Pattern**: Generic iterators provide flexibility without cost
248. 
249. ---
250. 
251. **Status:** ✅ Complete  
252. **Test Coverage:** 100% (9 unit tests + 1 integration test)  
253. **Documentation:** Updated  
254. **Performance:** Verified (no regression)
255.
````

10. ## Executive Summary
11.

30.

33. - **Location**: `icn/crates/icn-rpc/src/server.rs`

35. - **Fix**: Add `icn_rpc_*` metrics module, instrument all handlers

38. ### 2. ~~Compute API Missing from OpenAPI Specification~~ ✅ FIXED
39. 
40. **Impact**: Developers cannot consume compute endpoints
41. 
42. - **Location**: `docs/api/openapi.yaml`
43. - **Issue**: Compute endpoints (submit, status, cancel) not documented
44. - **Fix**: Add `/v1/compute/*` endpoints to OpenAPI spec

1. # ICN Roadmap
2. 
3. **Last Updated**: 2026-01-31
4. **Current Focus**: Phase 3 State Generalization + Kernel Crate Cleanup
5. **Target**: Clean kernel with pluggable first-party and third-party apps
6. 
7. ---
8. 
9. ## Strategic Context
10. 
11. ICN is infrastructure for a **parallel political economy** — enabling cooperatives, communities, and federations to deliver better material outcomes than traditional capitalist and captured democratic systems.
12. 
13. **Core Vision**: ICN is not just infrastructure *for* cooperatives — it is **cooperative infrastructure that governs itself democratically**. The protocols are adjustable by the organizations using them.
14. 
15. ### Architecture Reset (2026-01-26)
16. 
17. The previous roadmap (Phases 19-35) has been superseded by the **Kernel/App Separation** initiative. This architectural reset:
18. 
19. 1. **Separates kernel from apps** - Kernel provides 8 generic primitives; apps implement domain logic
20. 2. **Establishes the "Meaning Firewall"** - Kernel never understands domain semantics
21. 3. **Enables third-party apps** - Same APIs as first-party apps
22. 4. **Simplifies the codebase** - From 27 tightly-coupled crates to ~12 kernel crates + apps
23. 
24. **See**: [KERNEL_APP_SEPARATION.md](../KERNEL_APP_SEPARATION.md) for full architectural documentation.

87. - ~~[#916](https://github.com/InterCooperative-Network/icn/issues/916): Enable strict Meaning Firewall CI~~ ✅ PR #974

89. - [#918](https://github.com/InterCooperative-Network/icn/issues/918): Move supervisor init_*.rs to app crates

91. ---
92. 
93. ## The Meaning Firewall
94. 
95. The core architectural principle driving this work:
96. 
97. ```
98. CCL Document (constitution / bylaws / treaty)
99.          ↓
100. App Interpreter (Governance / Membership / Ledger / Federation)
101.          ↓
102. PolicyDecision { constraints }
103.          ↓
104. Kernel enforces constraints mechanically
105. ```
106. 
107. **Example**: The kernel never sees "constitutional amendment" or "supermajority" — only:
108. - `min_votes = 67`
109. - `quorum_required = 50`
110. - `deadline = 1706000000`
111. 
112. This ensures:
113. 1. Apps can implement any governance model
114. 2. Kernel remains simple and auditable
115. 3. Third-party apps have equal capabilities
116. 
117. ---
118. 
119. ## Target Architecture
120. 
121. ### Kernel Crates (~12)
122. 
123. ```
124. icn-kernel-api/   # Trait definitions (PolicyOracle, primitives)
125. icn-identity/     # DID + keystore
126. icn-store/        # Generic storage (KV, Log, Blob)
127. icn-protocol/     # Gossip + networking
128. icn-core/         # Runtime + supervisor + app management
129. icn-services/     # API surfaces (RPC, Gateway)
130. icn-security/     # Security primitives
131. icn-crypto/       # Cryptography
132. icn-obs/          # Observability
133. icn-encoding/     # Serialization
134. icn-time/         # Time primitives
135. icn-testkit/      # Test utilities
136. ```
137. 
138. ### First-Party Apps
139. 
140. ```
141. apps/
142.   trust/          # Trust graph, attestations, PolicyOracle
143.   ledger/         # Mutual credit, escrow, budgets
144.   governance/     # Proposals, voting, CCL-driven rules
145.   membership/     # Entity management, membership classes
146.   echo/           # Test app (implemented)
147. ```
148. 
149. ### 8 Kernel Primitives
150.

1. # ICN Development Plan 2026
2. 
3. **Created**: 2026-01-08
4. **Target**: Pilot deployment with a real cooperative
5. **Author**: Development planning based on comprehensive code review
6. 
7. ---
8. 
9. ## Revised Assessment
10. 
11. The code review identified "4,618 unwraps" as a critical issue. **This was misleading.**
12. 
13. Actual breakdown:
14. | Location | Count | % |
15. |----------|-------|---|
16. | Test code | 4,323 | 97.6% |
17. | Production code | 107 | 2.4% |
18. 
19. **The codebase is in much better shape than initially assessed.**
20. 
21. ### Real Issues (Corrected)
22. 
23. | Issue | Severity | Blocking Pilot? |
24. |-------|----------|-----------------|
25. | 107 production unwraps | LOW | No - mostly infallible ops |
26. | `block_in_place` in trust_mgr | LOW | No - correct Tokio pattern |
27. | Low test coverage (icn-coop, icn-core) | MEDIUM | No - but risky to change |
28. | No NAT traversal | HIGH | **Yes** - LAN only currently |
29. | No backup validation | HIGH | **Yes** - data loss risk |
30. | Empty icn-testkit | LOW | No - nice to have |
31. | 6 ignored integration tests | MEDIUM | No - known async issue |
32. 
33. ### Actual Pilot Blockers
34. 
35. 1. **Network**: ICN only works on LAN (mDNS). Need NAT traversal for internet.
36. 2. **Operations**: No validated backup/restore. Unacceptable for real data.
37. 3. **Documentation**: No runbooks for cooperative administrators.
38. 4. **Onboarding**: No setup guide for new cooperatives.
39. 
40. ---
41. 
42. ## Goal
43. 
44. Deploy ICN with a **real cooperative** for a 3-month pilot, with:
45. - Mutual credit ledger tracking real transactions
46. - Governance proposals for real decisions
47. - Trust relationships between real members
48. - Ability to operate over the internet (not just LAN)
49. 
50. ---
51. 
52. ## Critical Path
53. 
54. ```
55. M1: Operations Foundation (3 weeks)
56.          ↓
57. M2: Network Connectivity (4 weeks)
58.          ↓
59. M3: Documentation & Onboarding (2 weeks)
60.          ↓
61. M4: Pilot Deployment (ongoing)
62. ```
63. 
64. **Total to pilot-ready: ~9 weeks**
65. 
66. ---

159. | Coordination | Consensus, CRDTs |
160. | Naming | Name resolution, discovery |
161. 
162. ---
163. 
164. ## CCL: Constitutional Layer
165. 
166. CCL (Cooperative Contract Language) is the declarative layer for expressing:
167. - Entity constitutions and bylaws
168. - Governance rules and voting procedures
169. - Economic policies (surplus allocation, credit limits)
170. - Federation agreements
171. 
172. **Schema v0 complete** (PR #855):
173. - `entity.rs` - Cooperatives, communities, federations, membership
174. - `governance.rs` - Bodies, decisions, delegation
175. - `economics.rs` - Capital, surplus, credit
176. - `agreement.rs` - Federation agreements, boundary protocols
177. 
178. **Key Insight**: Federation agreements use **binary boundary outcomes**:
179. 
180. ```yaml
181. boundary_outcome:
182.   type: binary  # approved | rejected
183. ```
184. 
185. Federation A uses consensus. Federation B uses majority vote. The agreement doesn't care — it only asks "Did each party approve?"
186. 
187. **Internal process is sovereign. Boundary outcomes are interoperable.**
188. 
189. ---
190.

198. | 5: Membership Consolidation | 4-5 days | ⏳ Planned |
199. | 6: Crate Consolidation | 3-4 days | ⏳ Planned |
200. | 7: Naming Primitive | 2-3 days (service discovery foundation exists) | ⏳ Planned |
201. 
202. **Total remaining: ~16-20 days of focused work** (Phase 2 complete)
203.

<sub>⏱️ 16m 57s</sub>

### 👤 User

[[PLAN]] You’re very close to having a “complete loop” spec: identity → standing → governance → allocations → workloads → receipts → audit → future constraints. The doc already nails the philosophical and constitutional spine. What’s missing (or under-specified) is the operational substrate that makes that loop unavoidable in practice: nodes, cells, workload placement, execution verification, storage/replication, and “apps as civic infrastructure.”

Below is feedback focused on the compute/node/cell layers and how they interact with governance + economics, plus concrete gaps to fill.

What’s strong already

Nodes as civic organs is the right frame. It makes it clear the “state machine” is not a metaphor.

Scope-aware execution is the correct scaling primitive (cell → org → federation → commons).

Apps/services as governed software is the missing link most “decentralized governance” projects never bridge.

The doc reads like a system that could run society. Now it needs a few missing “plumbing” clauses so it reads like a system that must run the parts it claims.

The missing compute concepts to add
1) A Workload Manifest schema (the “constitution for execution”)

Right now “workloads are scoped” is conceptually clear, but you need the exact shape of the declaration. Add a section defining a workload manifest with at least:

Scope ceiling: max_scope = cell|org|fed|commons

Data locality requirements: “must execute where dataset X resides” / “may not leave cell”

Capabilities required (your existing model): ReadLedger, WriteLedger, ReadTrust, etc.

Resource envelope: CPU time, memory, storage I/O, network egress

Determinism contract: deterministic vs best-effort (and what outputs are considered canonical)

Privacy class: public / member / need-to-know (ties directly to your audit tiers)

Verification policy: re-exec quorum, witness set, or attestation requirements

Without this, scope-aware compute is a principle, not an interface.

2) Execution Receipts need to be first-class like Decision/Allocation Receipts

You mention execution receipts, but they don’t yet have “named artifact parity” with governance and economics. Define the canonical fields:

workload_id, version_hash, inputs_hash, policy_hash

scope_executed_at, executor_node(s), witness_node(s)

resource_spent (fuel + compute units)

outputs_hash + pointers to artifacts (logs, proof, result objects)

verification_result (passed/failed/disputed) + dispute pointer

settlement_hook (what ledger event this triggers, if any)

This is how “governance is a deployment pipeline” becomes cryptographically tight.

3) Deterministic vs non-deterministic workloads (split the universe)

You already defend determinism at the “receipt hash” level. Great. Now codify:

Class A: Canonical workloads (must be deterministic; outputs become constraints/ledger state)

governance tallying, budget computation, settlement/netting, eligibility evaluation

Class B: Advisory workloads (can be probabilistic; outputs are suggestions, not state)

forecasting demand, routing optimization, recommendations, anomaly detection

Then state: only Class A outputs can mutate canonical state. Everything else can inform proposals, not enact them.

4) A real sandbox model for apps (capability gating isn’t the whole story)

CCL safety + capabilities is necessary, but you also need operational isolation:

Execution environment: WASM sandbox? native module ABI? container boundary?

Filesystem/network rules: default deny, explicit allow by capability

Secrets handling: how an org stores secrets without turning nodes into opaque admin boxes

Upgrade rules: canary, rollback, mandatory re-approval when capability set changes

This is where your “cooperative AWS” either becomes real or becomes “we trust the admins.”

5) Storage is implied but not specified (and storage is governance)

You describe gossip and ledgers, but “apps/services” will need durable state beyond the ledger:

State types

canonical: ledger, governance receipts, trust edges

service state: calendars, inventory, case management, schedules

blobs: documents, media, backups, datasets

Placement rules

cell-local encrypted stores for sensitive state

federation mirrors for cross-entity interoperability

commons for public indices and shared libraries

Replication + recovery

snapshot cadence, quorum durability targets, disaster recovery semantics

If you don’t specify storage, someone will “just use S3,” and the whole point collapses.

6) Cell formation + governance boundary needs one more sentence: “cells are operated by one entity”

You said it in your message to me, but it should be explicit in the doc:

A cell is a LAN federation of nodes under one operator entity (a co-op, community, federation, or an individual).

Cross-entity clustering belongs at federation scope, not “mixed-operator cell scope.”

Otherwise readers will assume “any 3 nodes on a LAN can form a cell,” which is a trust boundary disaster.

7) Individual node ownership mode (power users, devs, personal use)

You want: “identity is mobile-first, but individuals can coordinate nodes.” Spell it out as a supported topology:

Wallet = root identity

Personal node(s) = optional operator footprint

caching/verifying receipts

running personal services (vault, comms, client gateway)

contributing compute to commons under personal policy

acting as a dev/test node for org apps without granting org custody

This matters because it’s how you bridge from “movement infrastructure” to “daily life infra.”

8) Commons compute isn’t just “spare cycles,” it’s a governed pool with admission + abuse rules

You hint at it, but it needs explicit governance/econ coupling:

Who can submit to commons? Based on standing + trust + credit ceilings

How is priority determined? Charter-defined scheduler policy (UBS-first, emergency-first, etc.)

How is abuse handled? Misbehavior detector → quarantine → ban, plus economic penalties

How is compensation settled? Mutual credit entries tied to execution receipts

Otherwise commons compute becomes the soft underbelly where attackers and freeloaders live.

How everything should interact (tight end-to-end narrative)

Here’s the clean interaction model that matches your intent (and patches the missing glue):

Identity & Standing

Individual wallet presents membership/standing proofs to an entity’s node/cell.

Node issues a short-lived capability envelope scoped to that entity + scope.

Governance produces “policy deltas”

Proposal lifecycle runs in-scope.

Outcome produces a Decision Receipt.

The Governance Oracle compiles that into a policy delta (capabilities, ceilings, scheduler rules, budget authorities).

Economics binds policy to scarcity

Ledger Oracle applies budget authorities and credit ceilings.

Allocation decisions produce Allocation Receipts tied to deliverables/claims.

Workloads make the decision real

Decision/Allocation receipts trigger workload manifests.

Scheduler places workloads at the lowest compliant scope:

cell for local civic operations

org for multi-site internal services

federation for cross-entity clearing/markets/disputes

commons for shared indices + burst capacity + constitutional services

Execution produces accountable reality

Workload runs in sandbox with declared capabilities + fuel.

Produces Execution Receipt + artifact hashes.

Verification policy runs (re-exec, witnesses, or attestations).

Receipts close the loop

Execution receipts settle ledger entries (payments, credits, service claims).

Audit tier controls visibility.

Receipts become future constraints (fraud penalties, trust changes, policy updates).

That’s the “democratic voice becomes operational” story you want: the voice doesn’t end at a vote. It ends at an execution receipt.

One accuracy nit you should lock down (PQC sizes)

You cite ML-DSA-65 signature size (~3,293 bytes). That’s consistent with NIST’s ML-DSA draft tables: ML-DSA signature sizes are 2420 / 3293 / 4595 bytes across parameter sets.
(This is good news: your numbers look right, and citing NIST’s table makes the doc feel grounded.)

Suggested additions to the document outline (minimal but surgical)

Add these subsections (you can keep them short and still “feel complete”):

Workload Manifests & Placement Rules

99. impl ComputeTask {
100.     /// Compute the task hash
101.     pub fn hash(&self) -> TaskHash {
102.         let bytes = icn_encoding::encode(self).unwrap_or_default();
103.         *blake3::hash(&bytes).as_bytes()
104.     }
105. 
106.     /// Validate task parameters
107.     pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), crate::error::ComputeError> {
108.         // Validate task ID
109.         if self.id.is_empty() {
110.             return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(
111.                 "Task ID cannot be empty".into(),
112.             ));
113.         }
114.         if self.id.len() > 256 {
115.             return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
116.                 "Task ID too long: {} bytes (max 256)",
117.                 self.id.len()
118.             )));
119.         }
120. 
121.         // Validate submitter DID format
122.         if !self.submitter.starts_with("did:icn:") {
123.             return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
124.                 "Invalid submitter DID format: {}",
125.                 self.submitter
126.             )));
127.         }
128. 
129.         // Validate fuel limit
130.         const MIN_FUEL: u64 = 100;
131.         const MAX_FUEL: u64 = 10_000_000; // 10M operations max
132.         if self.fuel_limit.0 < MIN_FUEL {
133.             return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
134.                 "Fuel limit too low: {} (min {})",
135.                 self.fuel_limit.0, MIN_FUEL
136.             )));
137.         }
138.         if self.fuel_limit.0 > MAX_FUEL {
139.             return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
140.                 "Fuel limit too high: {} (max {})",
141.                 self.fuel_limit.0, MAX_FUEL
142.             )));
143.         }
144. 
145.         // Validate task code
146.         match &self.code {
147.             TaskCode::Ccl(source) => {
148.                 if source.is_empty() {
149.                     return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(
150.                         "CCL source cannot be empty".into(),
151.                     ));
152.                 }
153.                 if source.len() > 1_000_000 {
154.                     return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
155.                         "CCL source too large: {} bytes (max 1MB)",
156.                         source.len()
157.                     )));
158.                 }
159.             }
160.             TaskCode::WasmInline(bytes) => {
161.                 if bytes.is_empty() {
162.                     return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(
163.                         "WASM bytes cannot be empty".into(),
164.                     ));
165.                 }
166.                 if bytes.len() > 5_000_000 {
167.                     return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
168.                         "WASM module too large: {} bytes (max 5MB)",
169.                         bytes.len()
170.                     )));
171.                 }
172.             }
173.             TaskCode::WasmRef(_) => {
174.                 // Hash is always valid by type
175.             }
176.             TaskCode::CclRef { rule, .. } => {
177.                 // Hash is always valid by type, but rule name must be non-empty
178.                 if rule.is_empty() {
179.                     return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(
180.                         "Rule name cannot be empty".into(),
181.                     ));
182.                 }
183.                 if rule.len() > 256 {
184.                     return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
185.                         "Rule name too long: {} chars (max 256)",
186.                         rule.len()
187.                     )));
188.                 }
189.             }
190.         }
191. 
192.         // Validate input size
193.         const MAX_INPUT_SIZE: usize = 1_000_000; // 1MB max
194.         if self.inputs.len() > MAX_INPUT_SIZE {
195.             return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
196.                 "Input too large: {} bytes (max 1MB)",
197.                 self.inputs.len()
198.             )));
199.         }
200. 
201.         // Validate deadline is in the future if provided
202.         if let Some(deadline) = self.deadline {
203.             let now = icn_time::current_timestamp_millis();
204. 
205.             if deadline <= now {
206.                 return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::DeadlineExceeded);
207.             }
208.         }
209. 
210.         // Validate payment rate if provided
211.         if let Some(rate) = self.payment_rate {
212.             const MAX_RATE: u64 = 1_000_000; // 1M credits per 1000 fuel max
213.             if rate > MAX_RATE {
214.                 return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(format!(
215.                     "Payment rate too high: {rate} (max {MAX_RATE})"
216.                 )));
217.             }
218.         }
219. 
220.         // Validate capabilities
221.         if self.required_capabilities.is_empty() {
222.             return Err(crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidCode(
223.                 "At least one capability required".into(),
224.             ));
225.         }
226. 
227.         Ok(())
228.     }
229. }

240.     CclRef {

252. /// Result of task execution
253. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
254. pub struct ComputeResult {
255.     /// Hash of the executed task
256.     pub task_hash: TaskHash,
257.     /// Task ID for correlation
258.     pub task_id: TaskId,
259.     /// DID of executor
260.     pub executor: String,
261.     /// Execution outcome
262.     pub outcome: ExecutionOutcome,
263.     /// Fuel consumed
264.     pub fuel_used: u64,
265.     /// Execution duration (millis)
266.     pub duration_ms: u64,
267.     /// Timestamp
268.     pub completed_at: u64,
269.     /// Ed25519 signature over result
270.     pub signature: Vec<u8>,
271. }
272. 
273. impl ComputeResult {
274.     /// Compute canonical hash for signing (deterministic serialization)
275.     pub fn signing_payload(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
276.         let mut payload = Vec::new();
277.         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.task_hash);
278.         payload.extend_from_slice(self.task_id.as_bytes());
279.         payload.extend_from_slice(self.executor.as_bytes());
280. 
281.         // Outcome hash
282.         match &self.outcome {
283.             ExecutionOutcome::Success(data) => {
284.                 payload.push(0);
285.                 payload.extend_from_slice(data);
286.             }
287.             ExecutionOutcome::Failed(msg) => {
288.                 payload.push(1);
289.                 payload.extend_from_slice(msg.as_bytes());
290.             }
291.             ExecutionOutcome::OutOfFuel => {
292.                 payload.push(2);
293.             }
294.             ExecutionOutcome::Timeout => {
295.                 payload.push(3);
296.             }
297.         }
298. 
299.         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.fuel_used.to_le_bytes());
300.         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.duration_ms.to_le_bytes());
301.         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.completed_at.to_le_bytes());
302. 
303.         payload
304.     }
305. 
306.     /// Sign the result with Ed25519
307.     pub fn sign(&mut self, signing_key: &ed25519_dalek::SigningKey) {
308.         let payload = self.signing_payload();
309.         let signature = signing_key.sign(&payload);
310.         self.signature = signature.to_bytes().to_vec();
311.     }
312. 
313.     /// Verify the signature
314.     pub fn verify_signature(
315.         &self,
316.         executor_did: &icn_identity::Did,
317.     ) -> Result<(), crate::error::ComputeError> {
318.         use ed25519_dalek::Verifier;
319. 
320.         // Extract public key from DID
321.         let verifying_key = executor_did.to_verifying_key().map_err(|e| {
322.             crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidSignature(format!(
323.                 "Cannot extract public key from DID: {e}"
324.             ))
325.         })?;
326. 
327.         let signature =
328.             ed25519_dalek::Signature::from_bytes(self.signature.as_slice().try_into().map_err(
329.                 |_| crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidSignature("Invalid signature length".into()),
330.             )?);
331. 
332.         let payload = self.signing_payload();
333.         verifying_key.verify(&payload, &signature).map_err(|e| {
334.             crate::error::ComputeError::InvalidSignature(format!(
335.                 "Signature verification failed: {e}"
336.             ))
337.         })?;
338. 
339.         Ok(())
340.     }
341. }

1. //! Compute Primitive
2. //!
3. //! Provides WASM execution with metering, scheduling, and resource quotas.
4. //!
5. //! # Design
6. //!
7. //! Two execution modes:
8. //! - **Deterministic**: No I/O, no wall clock, same input → same output.
9. //!   Used for reducers, validators, governance tallying.
10. //! - **Service**: Capability-gated I/O, long-running processes.
11. //!   Used for indexers, bridges, WebSocket handlers.
12. //!
13. //! # ABIs
14. //!
15. //! - `icn_abi_v1`: Deterministic compute
16. //! - `icn_service_abi_v1`: Service compute
17. //!
18. //! ABIs are versioned and stable (like syscalls).
19. //!
20. //! # Non-Goals
21. //!
22. //! - Domain-specific libraries (apps bundle their own)
23. //! - Privileged execution for "official" apps
24. //! - Any interpretation of what code does
25. 
26. use crate::types::{Duration, JobId, LogId, LogicalTimestamp, ServiceId};
27. 
28. /// WASM module ready for execution.
29. #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
30. pub struct WasmModule {
31.     /// Module name
32.     pub name: String,
33.     /// Compiled WASM bytecode
34.     pub bytecode: Vec<u8>,
35.     /// ABI version this module uses
36.     pub abi_version: AbiVersion,
37. }
38. 
39. /// Supported ABI versions.
40. #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
41. pub enum AbiVersion {
42.     /// Deterministic compute ABI (v1)
43.     DeterministicV1,
44.     /// Service compute ABI (v1)
45.     ServiceV1,
46. }
47. 
48. /// Result of deterministic execution.
49. #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
50. pub struct ExecutionResult {
51.     /// Output bytes
52.     pub output: Vec<u8>,
53.     /// Fuel consumed
54.     pub fuel_consumed: u64,
55.     /// Execution time (for metrics, not determinism)
56.     pub execution_time_us: u64,
57. }
58. 
59. /// Service configuration.
60. #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
61. pub struct ServiceConfig {
62.     /// Service name
63.     pub name: String,
64.     /// Environment variables
65.     pub env: std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
66.     /// Capabilities granted to this service
67.     pub capabilities: Vec<String>,
68. }
69. 
70. /// Resource quota for execution.
71. #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
72. pub struct ResourceQuota {
73.     /// Maximum fuel (compute units) per execution
74.     pub max_fuel: u64,
75.     /// Maximum memory in bytes
76.     pub max_memory: u64,
77.     /// Maximum execution time
78.     pub max_duration: Duration,
79.     /// Maximum storage writes per execution
80.     pub max_storage_writes: u32,
81. }
82.

91.     }

171.     },
172. }

174. /// Compute engine for WASM execution.
175. pub trait ComputeEngine: Send + Sync {
176.     /// Execute a deterministic computation.
177.     ///
178.     /// The module must use `icn_abi_v1` (deterministic).
179.     /// Same input always produces same output.
180.     fn execute_deterministic(
181.         &self,
182.         module: &WasmModule,
183.         input: &[u8],
184.         fuel: u64,
185.     ) -> Result<ExecutionResult, ComputeError>;
186. 
187.     /// Start a long-running service.
188.     ///
189.     /// The module must use `icn_service_abi_v1`.
190.     fn start_service(
191.         &self,
192.         module: &WasmModule,
193.         config: ServiceConfig,
194.         quota: ResourceQuota,
195.     ) -> Result<ServiceId, ComputeError>;
196. 
197.     /// Stop a running service.
198.     fn stop_service(&self, id: &ServiceId) -> Result<(), ComputeError>;
199. 
200.     /// Get service status.
201.     fn service_status(&self, id: &ServiceId) -> Result<ServiceStatus, ComputeError>;
202. 
203.     /// List running services.
204.     fn list_services(&self) -> Result<Vec<ServiceId>, ComputeError>;
205. 
206.     /// Schedule a job for later execution.
207.     fn schedule(&self, job: Job, trigger: Trigger) -> Result<JobId, ComputeError>;
208. 
209.     /// Cancel a scheduled job.
210.     fn cancel(&self, job_id: &JobId) -> Result<(), ComputeError>;
211. 
212.     /// Get job status.
213.     fn job_status(&self, job_id: &JobId) -> Result<JobStatus, ComputeError>;
214. 
215.     /// List scheduled jobs.
216.     fn list_jobs(&self) -> Result<Vec<JobId>, ComputeError>;
217. }

1. //! Scheduler primitives for intelligent task placement.
2. //!
3. //! This module extends the Phase 15 compute layer with resource-aware scheduling.
4. //! It introduces resource profiles, capacity tracking, and placement scoring.
5. //!
6. //! # Design Philosophy
7. //!
8. //! - **Incremental**: Builds on existing task submission/claiming protocol
9. //! - **Backward Compatible**: Works alongside legacy claiming logic
10. //! - **Trust-Governed**: Trust scores remain primary scheduling input
11. //! - **Gossip-Based**: No centralized scheduler, distributed negotiation
12. //!
13. //! # Evolution Stages
14. //!
15. //! - **Phase 16A** (this module): Resource profiles and capacity matching
16. //! - **Phase 16B**: Placement scoring and deliberation windows
17. //! - **Phase 16C**: Locality awareness and topology integration
18. //! - **Phase 16D**: Actor state and migration
19. //! - **Phase 16E**: Cooperative scheduling policies
20. 
21. use icn_kernel_api::{CellId, ScopeLevel};
22. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
23. use std::collections::HashMap;
24. use std::time::Duration;
25. 
26. /// Resource requirements for a compute task or actor.
27. ///
28. /// This replaces vague "capabilities" with concrete resource needs.
29. /// All fields are optional to support incremental adoption.
30. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
31. pub struct ResourceProfile {
32.     /// CPU cores required (e.g., 0.5 = half a core, 2.0 = two cores)
33.     pub cpu_cores: Option<f64>,
34. 
35.     /// Memory required in megabytes

461.             .and_then(|content| {

465.                     .split_whitespace()
466.                     .next()

468.             })
469.             .map(|load_avg| {

472.             })
473.             .unwrap_or(total_cores) // Fallback: assume all cores available
474.     }

1. //! Result quorum verification for high-value compute tasks.
2. //!
3. //! This module implements multi-executor verification to prevent incorrect
4. //! or malicious results from single executors on valuable computations.
5. //!
6. //! # Task Value Classification
7. //!
8. //! Tasks are classified by estimated value:
9. //! - **Low**: Single executor sufficient
10. //! - **Medium**: 2-executor verification
11. //! - **High**: 3+ executor quorum
12. //!
13. //! # Verification Flow
14. //!
15. //! 1. Task submitted with `verification_config`
16. //! 2. Scheduler assigns multiple executors based on value
17. //! 3. Results collected from all executors
18. //! 4. Quorum determines canonical result
19. //! 5. Divergent results escalate to dispute
20. //!
21. //! # Configuration
22. //!
23. //! ```toml
24. //! [compute.verification]
25. //! low_value_threshold = 100      # Below: single executor
26. //! medium_value_threshold = 1000  # Below: 2 executors
27. //! high_value_quorum = 3          # Above medium: 3+ executors
28. //! consensus_threshold = 0.67     # 2/3 majority for consensus
29. //! ```
30.

40. pub enum TaskValue {
41.     /// Low value - single executor sufficient
42.     #[default]
43.     Low,
44.     /// Medium value - 2-executor verification
45.     Medium,
46.     /// High value - 3+ executor quorum
47.     High,
48.     /// Critical value - maximum verification
49.     Critical,
50. }
51. 
52. impl TaskValue {
53.     /// Get the required executor count for this value level
54.     pub fn required_executors(&self) -> usize {
55.         match self {
56.             TaskValue::Low => 1,
57.             TaskValue::Medium => 2,
58.             TaskValue::High => 3,
59.             TaskValue::Critical => 5,
60.         }
61.     }
62. 
63.     /// Classify a task based on its estimated value in credits
64.     pub fn from_credits(credits: u64, config: &VerificationConfig) -> Self {
65.         if credits < config.low_value_threshold {
66.             TaskValue::Low
67.         } else if credits < config.medium_value_threshold {
68.             TaskValue::Medium
69.         } else if credits < config.high_value_threshold {
70.             TaskValue::High
71.         } else {
72.             TaskValue::Critical
73.         }
74.     }
75. }

653. impl Default for CapacityBudget {
654.     fn default() -> Self {
655.         Self {
656.             local_reserve: 0.30,
657.             cell_share: 0.25,

664. 
665. impl CapacityBudget {
666.     /// Get the capacity fraction for a given scope level.
667.     ///
668.     /// Returns the fraction of total node capacity available to tasks
669.     /// at the specified scope.
670.     pub fn fraction_for(&self, scope: ScopeLevel) -> f64 {
671.         match scope {
672.             ScopeLevel::Local => self.local_reserve,
673.             ScopeLevel::Cell => self.cell_share,
674.             ScopeLevel::Org => self.org_share,
675.             ScopeLevel::Federation => self.federation_share,
676.             ScopeLevel::Commons => self.commons_share,
677.         }
678.     }
679. 
680.     /// Get the cumulative capacity available at a given scope and below.
681.     ///
682.     /// Tasks at a wider scope can use capacity from all narrower scopes
683.     /// that haven't been consumed. This returns the maximum fraction
684.     /// available if the scope widened from Local up to the given level.
685.     pub fn cumulative_fraction_up_to(&self, scope: ScopeLevel) -> f64 {
686.         let mut total = self.local_reserve;
687.         if scope >= ScopeLevel::Cell {
688.             total += self.cell_share;
689.         }
690.         if scope >= ScopeLevel::Org {
691.             total += self.org_share;
692.         }
693.         if scope >= ScopeLevel::Federation {
694.             total += self.federation_share;
695.         }
696.         if scope >= ScopeLevel::Commons {
697.             total += self.commons_share;
698.         }
699.         total
700.     }
701. 
702.     /// Validate that fractions are individually valid and sum to ≤ 1.0.
703.     pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
704.         let fractions = [
705.             self.local_reserve,
706.             self.cell_share,
707.             self.org_share,
708.             self.federation_share,
709.             self.commons_share,
710.         ];
711. 
712.         for &f in &fractions {
713.             if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&f) {
714.                 return Err("Each fraction must be in [0.0, 1.0]");
715.             }
716.         }
717. 
718.         let sum: f64 = fractions.iter().sum();
719.         if sum > 1.0 + Self::FLOAT_TOLERANCE {
720.             return Err("Fractions must sum to at most 1.0");
721.         }
722. 
723.         Ok(())
724.     }
725. 
726.     /// Practical tolerance for floating-point comparisons.
727.     ///
728.     /// Using `f64::EPSILON` (~2.2e-16) is too tight when fractions are
729.     /// adjusted over many rounds; accumulated rounding can exceed it.
730.     /// 1e-9 is well above rounding noise but invisible at the 0.01 scale
731.     /// of our smallest meaningful fraction.
732.     const FLOAT_TOLERANCE: f64 = 1e-9;
733. 
734.     /// Minimum fraction per scope during demand adjustment.
735.     ///
736.     /// Prevents complete starvation of any scope, ensuring every scope
737.     /// retains at least minimal capacity for burst traffic.
738.     ///
739.     /// **Security**: Without this bound, an attacker could submit sustained
740.     /// high-demand tasks in one scope to drive other scopes' budgets to zero
741.     /// via the demand feedback loop, effectively denying service to those scopes.
742.     const MIN_SCOPE_FRACTION: f64 = 0.01;
743. 
744.     /// Maximum fraction per scope during demand adjustment.
745.     ///
746.     /// Prevents any single scope from monopolizing capacity, leaving
747.     /// headroom for other scopes even under sustained high demand.
748.     ///
749.     /// **Security**: Without this bound, a single dominant scope could absorb
750.     /// nearly all capacity, leaving other scopes unable to schedule tasks
751.     /// even when legitimate demand arises.
752.     const MAX_SCOPE_FRACTION: f64 = 0.80;
753. 
754.     /// Adjust budget based on observed demand.
755.     ///
756.     /// Takes utilization ratios (0.0-1.0) per scope and shifts unused
757.     /// capacity toward scopes with higher demand. The adjustment is
758.     /// conservative (moves at most `learning_rate` fraction per call).
759.     ///
760.     /// # Arguments
761.     /// * `utilization` - Map of scope → utilization ratio (0.0 = idle, 1.0 = saturated).
762.     ///   Scopes absent from the map are left unchanged (only scopes with data
763.     ///   participate in the rebalancing).
764.     /// * `learning_rate` - Maximum fraction to shift per adjustment (clamped to 0.0..0.1)
765.     ///

1. //! Scope and Cell primitives for multi-scale cooperative computing.
2. //!
3. //! This module defines `ScopeLevel` and `CellId` — kernel primitives that
4. //! enable spatial awareness without introducing domain semantics.
5. //!
6. //! # Design
7. //!
8. //! The kernel knows that `Federation` is "wider" than `Org`, but it does NOT
9. //! know what an organization *is*. That interpretation stays in apps,
10. //! consistent with the Meaning Firewall.
11. //!
12. //! See `docs/architecture/CELLS_AND_SCOPES.md` for the full specification.
13. 
14. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
15. 
16. // ============================================================================
17. // ScopeLevel
18. // ============================================================================
19. 
20. /// Scope level for operations, data, and services.
21. ///
22. /// Defines how far an operation should reach in the network hierarchy.
23. /// The kernel uses this for routing, replication, and capacity allocation
24. /// without interpreting the domain semantics of each level.
25. ///
26. /// # Ordering
27. ///
28. /// `ScopeLevel` implements `Ord`: `Local < Cell < Org < Federation < Commons`.
29. /// This ordering is used for hierarchical fallback in placement and discovery.
30. ///
31. /// # Examples
32. ///
33. /// ```
34. /// use icn_kernel_api::scope::ScopeLevel;
35. ///
36. /// assert!(ScopeLevel::Cell < ScopeLevel::Org);
37. /// assert!(ScopeLevel::Org.includes(ScopeLevel::Cell));
38. /// assert_eq!(ScopeLevel::Cell.widen(), Some(ScopeLevel::Org));
39. /// assert_eq!(ScopeLevel::Commons.widen(), None);
40. /// ```
41. #[derive(
42.     Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize,
43. )]
44. #[repr(u8)]
45. pub enum ScopeLevel {
46.     /// This node only — no network involvement.
47.     ///
48.     /// This is the default scope level. Defaulting to the narrowest scope
49.     /// prevents accidental data or request leakage to wider audiences.
50.     #[default]
51.     Local = 0,
52.     /// Nodes within the same cell (HA cluster).
53.     Cell = 1,
54.     /// Cells within the same organization.
55.     Org = 2,
56.     /// Organizations within the same federation.
57.     Federation = 3,
58.     /// All reachable nodes (public commons).
59.     Commons = 4,
60. }
61. 
62. impl ScopeLevel {
63.     /// All scope levels in ascending order.
64.     pub const ALL: [ScopeLevel; 5] = [
65.         ScopeLevel::Local,
66.         ScopeLevel::Cell,
67.         ScopeLevel::Org,
68.         ScopeLevel::Federation,
69.         ScopeLevel::Commons,
70.     ];
71. 
72.     /// Return the next wider scope, or `None` if already at `Commons`.
73.     pub fn widen(&self) -> Option<ScopeLevel> {
74.         match self {
75.             ScopeLevel::Local => Some(ScopeLevel::Cell),
76.             ScopeLevel::Cell => Some(ScopeLevel::Org),
77.             ScopeLevel::Org => Some(ScopeLevel::Federation),
78.             ScopeLevel::Federation => Some(ScopeLevel::Commons),
79.             ScopeLevel::Commons => None,
80.         }
81.     }
82. 
83.     /// Return the next narrower scope, or `None` if already at `Local`.
84.     pub fn narrow(&self) -> Option<ScopeLevel> {
85.         match self {
86.             ScopeLevel::Local => None,
87.             ScopeLevel::Cell => Some(ScopeLevel::Local),
88.             ScopeLevel::Org => Some(ScopeLevel::Cell),
89.             ScopeLevel::Federation => Some(ScopeLevel::Org),
90.             ScopeLevel::Commons => Some(ScopeLevel::Federation),
91.         }
92.     }
93. 
94.     /// Check if this scope includes another scope.
95.     ///
96.     /// A wider scope includes all narrower scopes.
97.     /// e.g., `Org.includes(Cell)` is `true`, `Cell.includes(Org)` is `false`.
98.     pub fn includes(&self, other: ScopeLevel) -> bool {
99.         *self >= other
100.     }
