15. 
16. use crate::config::Config;
17. use crate::runtime::ShutdownTx;
18. 
19. use super::actors::{
20.     CoreActorHandles, EventSubscriptionHandles, GatewayActorHandles, ShutdownHandles,
21. };
22. 
23. /// Run the supervisor lifecycle
24. ///
25. /// This is the main entry point for supervisor operation. It:
26. /// 1. Initializes metrics and observability
27. /// 2. Spawns all actors (if identity bundle is available)
28. /// 3. Configures actor communication and bridging
29. /// 4. Spawns background tasks
30. /// 5. Waits for shutdown signal
31. /// 6. Performs graceful shutdown
32. ///
33. /// # Service Registry
34. ///
35. /// If `service_registry` is provided, services from it will be used instead of
36. /// creating internal implementations. This enables proper kernel/app separation
37. /// where the daemon constructs domain services from app crates.
38. pub async fn run_supervisor(
39.     config: Config,
40.     identity_bundle: Option<IdentityBundle>,
41.     shutdown_tx: ShutdownTx,
42.     service_registry: Option<ServiceRegistry>,
43.     bootstrap_handles: Option<super::BootstrapHandles>,
44. ) -> Result<()> {
45.     info!("Supervisor starting");
46. 
47.     // Log service registry status
48.     if let Some(ref registry) = service_registry {
49.         info!("Using daemon-provided service registry");
50.         if registry.trust().is_some() {
51.             info!("  - TrustService: provided");
52.         }
53.         if registry.governance().is_some() {
54.             info!("  - GovernanceService: provided");
55.         }
56.         if registry.ledger().is_some() {
57.             info!("  - LedgerService: provided");
58.         }
59.         if registry.security().is_some() {
60.             info!("  - SecurityService: provided");
61.         }
62.     } else {
63.         debug!("No service registry provided, using internal implementations");
64.     }
65. 
66.     // Initialize metrics
67.     icn_obs::init_metrics()?;
68. 
69.     // Set supervisor state to starting
70.     icn_obs::metrics::supervisor::state_set(1);
71. 
72.     // Start metrics server
73.     let metrics_port = config.observability.metrics_port;
74.     if let Err(e) = icn_obs::start_metrics_server(metrics_port).await {
75.         warn!("Failed to start metrics server: {}", e);
76.         icn_obs::metrics::supervisor::error_inc("metrics_server_start");
77.     }
78. 
79.     let mut shutdown_rx = shutdown_tx.subscribe();
80. 
81.     // Track spawned background tasks for graceful shutdown
82.     let mut background_tasks: JoinSet<()> = JoinSet::new();
83. 
84.     let mut gateway_handles = GatewayActorHandles::default();
85.     let mut event_subscriptions = EventSubscriptionHandles::default();
86.     let mut shutdown_handles = ShutdownHandles::default();
87. 
88.     // Spawn actors (requires identity bundle from unlocked keystore)
89.     let core_handles = if let Some(identity_bundle) = &identity_bundle {
90.         spawn_actors_with_identity(
91.             &config,
92.             identity_bundle,
93.             &shutdown_tx,
94.             &mut background_tasks,
95.             &mut gateway_handles,
96.             &mut event_subscriptions,
97.             &mut shutdown_handles,
98.             service_registry.as_ref(),
99.             bootstrap_handles,
100.         )

119. /// Trait for executing kernel-safe effects.
120. ///
121. /// This is the primary interface for the kernel to execute effects produced
122. /// by the governance app's payload-to-effect translation.
123. #[async_trait]
124. pub trait EffectExecutor: Send + Sync {
125.     /// Execute a kernel effect.
126.     ///
127.     /// # Arguments
128.     /// * `effect` - The kernel-safe effect to execute
129.     /// * `decision_receipt_id` - The receipt ID for audit linkage
130.     ///
131.     /// # Returns
132.     /// Result of the effect execution
133.     async fn execute_effect(
134.         &self,
135.         effect: KernelEffect,
136.         decision_receipt_id: &str,
137.     ) -> Result<EffectResult>;
138. 
139.     /// Execute a batch of effects atomically.
140.     ///
141.     /// Either all effects succeed or none are applied.
142.     async fn execute_effects_batch(
143.         &self,
144.         effects: Vec<KernelEffect>,
145.         decision_receipt_id: &str,
146.     ) -> Result<Vec<EffectResult>> {
147.         let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(effects.len());
148.         for effect in effects {
149.             results.push(self.execute_effect(effect, decision_receipt_id).await?);
150.         }
151.         Ok(results)
152.     }
153. }
154. 
155. /// Default effect executor that delegates to specialized executors.
156. pub struct DefaultEffectExecutor {
157.     treasury: std::sync::Arc<dyn TreasuryExecutor>,
158.     protocol: std::sync::Arc<dyn ProtocolExecutor>,
159. }
160. 
161. impl DefaultEffectExecutor {
162.     /// Create a new effect executor with the given specialized executors.
163.     pub fn new(
164.         treasury: std::sync::Arc<dyn TreasuryExecutor>,
165.         protocol: std::sync::Arc<dyn ProtocolExecutor>,
166.     ) -> Self {
167.         Self { treasury, protocol }
168.     }
169. }
170. 
171. #[async_trait]
172. impl EffectExecutor for DefaultEffectExecutor {
173.     async fn execute_effect(
174.         &self,
175.         effect: KernelEffect,
176.         decision_receipt_id: &str,
177.     ) -> Result<EffectResult> {
178.         let receipt_id = DecisionReceiptId::new(decision_receipt_id);
179. 
180.         match effect {
181.             KernelEffect::Treasury(treasury_effect) => {
182.                 // Convert TreasuryEffect to TreasuryOperation
183.                 let operation = treasury_effect_to_operation(&treasury_effect);
184.                 let outcome = self
185.                     .treasury
186.                     .execute_treasury_operation(&receipt_id, operation)
187.                     .await?;
188.                 Ok(execution_outcome_to_effect_result(
189.                     outcome,
190.                     decision_receipt_id,
191.                 ))
192.             }
193.             KernelEffect::Protocol(protocol_effect) => {
194.                 // Convert ProtocolEffect to ProtocolChange
195.                 if let Some(change) = protocol_effect_to_change(&protocol_effect) {
196.                     let outcome = self.protocol.apply_protocol_change(&receipt_id, change).await?;
197.                     Ok(execution_outcome_to_effect_result(
198.                         outcome,
199.                         decision_receipt_id,
200.                     ))
```

1. //! ICN Governance Actor
2. //!
3. //! This crate provides the [`GovernanceActor`] for distributed decision-making
4. //! across the ICN network. It manages governance state, proposal lifecycle,
5. //! voting, and outcome evaluation.
6. //!
7. //! ## Architecture
8. //!
9. //! The governance actor is a domain-specific application that sits above the
10. //! kernel layer. It depends on kernel-api traits (e.g., [`EventEmitter`],
11. //! [`ProtocolParameterStore`], [`GovernanceExecutor`]) rather than concrete
12. //! kernel implementations, maintaining clean separation between kernel
13. //! mechanisms and domain semantics.
14. //!
15. //! ## Handlers
16. //!
17. //! The [`handlers`] module provides the execution callback infrastructure for
18. //! processing accepted proposals. Each handler type (treasury, protocol,
19. //! federation) implements the [`handlers::ExecutionCallback`] trait.
20. //!
21. //! When kernel executors are configured via [`GovernanceHandle::with_executor`],
22. //! handlers can delegate execution to the kernel-provided executor traits:
23. //! - [`TreasuryExecutor`] for treasury operations
24. //! - [`ProtocolExecutor`] for protocol parameter changes
25. //!
26. //! [`EventEmitter`]: icn_kernel_api::events::EventEmitter
27. //! [`ProtocolParameterStore`]: icn_kernel_api::protocol_params::ProtocolParameterStore
28. //! [`GovernanceExecutor`]: icn_kernel_api::governance::GovernanceExecutor
29. //! [`TreasuryExecutor`]: icn_kernel_api::governance::TreasuryExecutor
30. //! [`ProtocolExecutor`]: icn_kernel_api::governance::ProtocolExecutor
31. 
32. pub mod actor;
33. pub mod executor;
34. pub mod handlers;
35. 
36. pub use actor::{GovernanceActor, GovernanceCommand, GovernanceConfigLite, GovernanceHandle};
37. pub use executor::{ExecutionCallback, GovernanceProposalExecutor};
38. pub use handlers::{
39.     translate_payload_to_effects, Allocation, AllocationReceipt, DisburseParams,
40.     ExecutionCallback as HandlerCallback, FederationHandler, ProposalExecutionContext,
41.     ProposalType, ProtocolHandler, TreasuryHandler,
42. };
43. 
44. // Re-export kernel effect types for kernel/app boundary
45. pub use icn_kernel_api::effects::{
46.     ControlEffect, EffectResult, FederationEffect, KernelEffect, MembershipEffect, ProtocolEffect,
47.     TreasuryEffect,
48. };
49. 
50. // Re-export kernel governance traits for convenience
51. pub use icn_kernel_api::governance::{
52.     DecisionReceiptId, ExecutionOutcome, GovernanceExecutor, ProtocolChange, ProtocolExecutor,
53.     TreasuryExecutor, TreasuryOperation, TreasuryOperationType,
54. };
55. 
56. // Re-export governance types needed by supervisor initialization.
57. // This allows icn-core to import from icn_governance_actor instead of
58. // icn_governance directly, reducing direct governance coupling.
59. pub use icn_governance::{MembershipResolver, StaticMembershipResolver};
60. 
61. /// Create a ProposalExecutor instance.
62. ///
63. /// This is the entry point for proposal execution. The executor requires
64. /// an execution callback that has access to icn-core internals.
65. ///
66. /// # Arguments
67. /// * `execution_callback` - Callback for executing proposals with domain logic
68. pub fn create_executor(
69.     execution_callback: executor::ExecutionCallback,
70. ) -> std::sync::Arc<dyn icn_kernel_api::services::ProposalExecutor> {
71.     std::sync::Arc::new(GovernanceProposalExecutor::new(execution_callback))
72. }

73.         ));
74.     }

1. //! System-wide event bus for inter-actor communication
2. //!
3. //! This module provides a simple event bus for coordinating actions across actors.
4. //! Key use case: Governance proposals triggering ledger transactions or contract execution.
5. //!
6. //! The [`SystemEvent`] enum and [`EventEmitter`] trait are defined in `icn-kernel-api`
7. //! and re-exported here. The [`EventBus`] implementation lives in icn-core.
8. 
9. use async_trait::async_trait;
10. use std::sync::Arc;
11. use tokio::sync::RwLock;
12. use tracing::{debug, warn};
13. 
14. // Re-export event types and trait from kernel-api
15. pub use icn_kernel_api::events::{EventCallback, EventEmitter, SystemEvent};
16. 
17. /// Subscription handle that automatically unsubscribes when dropped
18. ///
19. /// When this handle is dropped, the associated callback is removed from the event bus.
20. /// This prevents memory leaks when subscriptions are added dynamically.
21. pub struct SubscriptionHandle {
22.     id: usize,
23.     subscribers: Arc<RwLock<Vec<(usize, EventCallback)>>>,
24. }
25. 
26. impl Drop for SubscriptionHandle {
27.     fn drop(&mut self) {
28.         // Attempt to remove this subscription
29.         // Use try_write() to avoid panicking if the lock is held
30.         // (this can happen during async runtime shutdown)
31.         if let Ok(mut subs) = self.subscribers.try_write() {
32.             let initial_count = subs.len();
33.             subs.retain(|(id, _)| *id != self.id);
34.             let removed_count = initial_count - subs.len();
35.             if removed_count > 0 {
36.                 debug!(
37.                     "Event bus subscriber {} removed (remaining: {})",
38.                     self.id,
39.                     subs.len()
40.                 );
41.             }
42.         }
43.         // If we can't get the lock, silently skip cleanup
44.         // The subscription will remain in memory, but this is better than panicking
45.     }
46. }
47. 
48. /// Simple event bus for publishing and subscribing to system events
49. ///
50. /// This uses a synchronous broadcast pattern where all subscribers are called
51. /// immediately when an event is emitted. For high-throughput scenarios, consider
52. /// using an async channel-based approach.
53. ///
54. /// Subscriptions are tracked via SubscriptionHandle, which automatically unsubscribes
55. /// when dropped, preventing memory leaks.
56. #[derive(Clone)]
57. pub struct EventBus {
58.     subscribers: Arc<RwLock<Vec<(usize, EventCallback)>>>,
59.     next_id: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,
60. }
```

1. //! System-wide event types and emitter trait
2. //!
3. //! Provides the `SystemEvent` enum and `EventEmitter` trait for inter-actor
4. //! communication. The kernel treats events as opaque coordination primitives —
5. //! it routes them without interpreting their semantics.
6. 
7. use async_trait::async_trait;
8. use std::sync::Arc;
9. 
10. /// System-wide events that actors can emit and subscribe to.
11. ///
12. /// All fields use primitive or stringly-typed values so that kernel-api
13. /// remains free of domain crate dependencies.
14. #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
15. pub enum SystemEvent {
16.     /// A governance proposal was accepted
17.     ProposalAccepted {
18.         /// Unique identifier for the proposal
19.         proposal_id: String,
20.         /// Domain in which the proposal was made
21.         domain_id: String,
22.         /// Payload describing the proposal action (serialized)
23.         payload: serde_json::Value,
24.         /// Unix timestamp when the proposal was decided
25.         decided_at: u64,
26.     },
27. 
28.     /// A governance proposal was rejected or failed to reach quorum
29.     ProposalRejected {
30.         /// Unique identifier for the proposal
31.         proposal_id: String,
32.         /// Domain in which the proposal was made
33.         domain_id: String,
34.         /// Unix timestamp when the proposal was decided
35.         decided_at: u64,
36.     },
37. 
38.     /// A ledger transaction was executed
39.     TransactionExecuted {
40.         /// Hash of the ledger entry
41.         entry_hash: [u8; 32],
42.         /// Source DID (as string)
43.         from: String,
44.         /// Destination DID (as string)
45.         to: String,
46.         /// Transaction amount
47.         amount: i64,
48.         /// Currency identifier
49.         currency: String,
50.     },
51. 
52.     /// A contract was executed
53.     ContractExecuted {
54.         /// Contract identifier
55.         contract_id: String,
56.         /// Execution outcome as JSON
57.         outcome: serde_json::Value,
58.     },
59. 
60.     /// A proposal execution failed (proposal was accepted but could not be applied)
61.     ProposalExecutionFailed {
62.         /// Unique identifier for the proposal
63.         proposal_id: String,
64.         /// Type of the proposal (e.g., "protocol_change", "treasury")
65.         proposal_type: String,
66.         /// Human-readable error message
67.         error: String,
68.         /// Unix timestamp when the failure occurred
69.         failed_at: u64,
70.     },
71. 
72.     /// Protocol parameters were initialized (first run)
73.     ProtocolParametersInitialized {
74.         /// Number of parameters initialized
75.         count: usize,
76.         /// Unix timestamp when the initialization occurred
77.         initialized_at: u64,
78.     },
79. 
80.     /// Protocol parameter store was loaded (existing parameters)
81.     ProtocolParametersLoaded {
82.         /// Number of parameters loaded
83.         count: usize,
84.         /// Unix timestamp when the store was loaded
85.         loaded_at: u64,
86.     },
87. 
88.     /// A protocol parameter was changed (for audit logging)
89.     ProtocolParameterChanged {
90.         /// Parameter ID that was changed
91.         parameter_id: String,
92.         /// Old value (serialized as string for logging)
93.         old_value: String,
94.         /// New value (serialized as string for logging)
95.         new_value: String,
96.         /// Proposal ID that authorized the change (if any)
97.         proposal_id: Option<String>,
98.         /// DID of the actor who made the change
99.         changed_by: Option<String>,
100.         /// Unix timestamp when the change occurred
101.         changed_at: u64,
102.     },
103. }
104. 
105. /// Callback function for event subscribers
106. pub type EventCallback = Arc<dyn Fn(SystemEvent) + Send + Sync>;
107. 
108. /// Trait for emitting system events.
109. ///
110. /// Implementations handle the actual broadcast mechanism (e.g., in-memory
111. /// subscriber list, channel-based dispatch). The kernel provides a default
112. /// `EventBus` implementation.
113. #[async_trait]
114. pub trait EventEmitter: Send + Sync {

1. //! Protocol parameter types and storage trait
2. //!
3. //! These types define the kernel-level interface for governable protocol
4. //! parameters. Domain apps (like governance) implement the storage trait
5. //! and provide parameter defaults, while the kernel uses these types
6. //! without understanding governance semantics.
7. //!
8. //! # Meaning Firewall
9. //!
10. //! These types are deliberately "dumb" — they carry values and constraints
11. //! without interpreting them. The governance app decides what parameters
12. //! exist and what their values mean. The kernel just stores, retrieves,
13. //! and schedules changes.
14. 
15. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
16. use std::fmt;
17. 
18. /// Known parameter categories for validation
19. pub const KNOWN_PARAMETER_CATEGORIES: &[&str] = &[
20.     "gossip",
21.     "network",
22.     "ledger",
23.     "governance",
24.     "trust",
25.     "ratelimit",
26.     "compute",
27. ];
28. 
29. // ============================================================================
30. // ProtocolParameter
31. // ============================================================================
32. 
33. /// A governable protocol parameter
34. ///
35. /// Protocol parameters are configuration values that can be changed through
36. /// the governance process. Each parameter has:
37. /// - A unique identifier (e.g., "gossip.max_message_size")
38. /// - Constraints on valid values
39. /// - A scope determining where it applies
40. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
41. pub struct ProtocolParameter {
42.     /// Unique parameter identifier (e.g., "gossip.max_message_size")
43.     ///
44.     /// Format: `<category>.<name>` or `<category>.<subcategory>.<name>`
45.     pub id: String,
46. 
47.     /// Human-readable name
48.     pub name: String,
49. 
50.     /// Detailed description of what this parameter controls
51.     pub description: String,
52. 
53.     /// Current value
54.     pub value: ParameterValue,
55. 
56.     /// Constraints on valid values
57.     pub constraints: ParameterConstraints,
58. 
59.     /// Scope where this parameter applies
60.     pub scope: ParameterScope,
61. 
62.     /// When the parameter was last updated (Unix timestamp)
63.     pub updated_at: u64,
64. 
65.     /// Proposal ID that last changed this parameter (if any)
66.     pub updated_by: Option<String>,
67. 
68.     /// Version for optimistic locking
69.     ///
70.     /// Incremented on each update to detect concurrent modifications.
71.     #[serde(default)]
72.     pub version: u64,
73. }
74. 
75. impl ProtocolParameter {
76.     /// Validate that a parameter ID follows the required format.
77.     ///
78.     /// Valid formats:
79.     /// - `category.name` (e.g., "gossip.fanout")
80.     /// - `category.subcategory.name` (e.g., "network.peer.timeout")

810. /// Trait for protocol parameter storage operations

812. /// This is the kernel-level abstraction for parameter storage. Domain apps

814. pub trait ProtocolParameterStore: Send + Sync {

817.

### 💬 Copilot

## Summary

### What was wired

1. **New module `effect_dispatcher.rs`** in `icn-core/src/supervisor/`:
   - `EffectDispatcher` struct that coordinates payload → effect → execution
   - `execute_proposal()` method that calls `translate_payload_to_effects()` then `execute_effect()`
   - `create_effect_subscription()` factory function for event bus integration
   - 3 unit tests validating the path works

2. **Updated `mod.rs`** to export the new module and `EffectDispatcher` type

3. **Updated `lifecycle.rs`** (lines 624-638) to wire the parallel path:
   - Creates a `KernelGovernanceExecutor` with the protocol parameter store
   - Wraps it in an `EffectDispatcher`
   - Subscribes to `ProposalAccepted` events via `create_effect_subscription()`
   - Logs `"✓ Effect-based execution path wired (parallel to legacy handlers)"`

### Integration point

The integration happens in `lifecycle.rs` inside the governance event subscription setup block. The new path subscribes to the same events as the legacy `create_governance_subscription()` handler, so both execute for every accepted proposal.

### What needs to happen to test it

1. **Unit tests**: Already added and passing (3 tests in `effect_dispatcher::tests`)
2. **Manual verification**: Start icnd, submit a Treasury proposal through governance, observe logs showing both paths executing
3. **Comparison**: When a `ProposalAccepted` event fires, you'll see:
   - Legacy handler logs from `governance_handlers/`
   - New effect path logs: `"Executing N effects via new effect path"` and `"Effect-based execution complete"`
4. **Metrics comparison**: Future sprint can add metrics to compare outcomes between paths

194.                 // Convert ProtocolEffect to ProtocolChange
195.                 if let Some(change) = protocol_effect_to_change(&protocol_effect) {
196.                     let outcome = self.protocol.apply_protocol_change(&receipt_id, change).await?;
197.                     Ok(execution_outcome_to_effect_result(
198.                         outcome,
199.                         decision_receipt_id,
200.                     ))
201.                 } else {
202.                     Ok(EffectResult {
203.                         effect_id: decision_receipt_id.to_string(),
204.                         success: true,
205.                         message: "Protocol effect applied".to_string(),
206.                         state_change_hash: None,
207.                     })
208.                 }
209.             }
210.             KernelEffect::NoOp { reason } => Ok(EffectResult {
211.                 effect_id: decision_receipt_id.to_string(),
212.                 success: true,
213.                 message: format!("NoOp: {}", reason),
214.                 state_change_hash: None,
215.             }),
216.             // For other effect types, return success placeholder
217.             _ => Ok(EffectResult {
218.                 effect_id: decision_receipt_id.to_string(),
219.                 success: true,
220.                 message: "Effect type not yet implemented".to_string(),
221.                 state_change_hash: None,
222.             }),
223.         }
224.     }
225. }
226. 
227. /// Convert a TreasuryEffect to a TreasuryOperation
228. fn treasury_effect_to_operation(effect: &TreasuryEffect) -> TreasuryOperation {
229.     match effect {
230.         TreasuryEffect::Spend {
231.             treasury_did,
232.             recipient_did,
233.             amount,
234.             currency,
235.             memo,
236.             ..
237.         } => TreasuryOperation {
238.             treasury_id: treasury_did.clone(),
239.             operation_type: TreasuryOperationType::Spend,
240.             amount: *amount,
241.             currency: currency.clone(),
242.             recipient: Some(recipient_did.clone()),
243.             memo: memo.clone(),
244.         },
245.         TreasuryEffect::CreateBudget {
246.             treasury_did,
247.             budget_id,
248.             total_amount,
249.             currency,
250.             name,
251.             ..
252.         } => TreasuryOperation {
253.             treasury_id: treasury_did.clone(),
254.             operation_type: TreasuryOperationType::Allocate,
255.             amount: *total_amount,
256.             currency: currency.clone(),
257.             recipient: Some(budget_id.clone()),
258.             memo: name.clone(),
259.         },
260.         TreasuryEffect::Allocate {
261.             treasury_did,
262.             budget_id,
263.             amount,
264.             currency,
265.         } => TreasuryOperation {
266.             treasury_id: treasury_did.clone(),
267.             operation_type: TreasuryOperationType::Allocate,
268.             amount: *amount,
269.             currency: currency.clone(),
270.             recipient: Some(budget_id.clone()),
271.             memo: "Budget allocation".to_string(),
272.         },
273.         TreasuryEffect::Transfer {
274.             from_did,
275.             to_did,
276.             amount,
277.             currency,
278.             memo,
279.         } => TreasuryOperation {
280.             treasury_id: from_did.clone(),
281.             operation_type: TreasuryOperationType::Spend,
282.             amount: *amount,
283.             currency: currency.clone(),
284.             recipient: Some(to_did.clone()),
285.             memo: memo.clone(),
286.         },
287.         // Other treasury effects mapped to basic operations
288.         _ => TreasuryOperation {
289.             treasury_id: String::new(),
290.             operation_type: TreasuryOperationType::Reserve,
291.             amount: 0,
292.             currency: "UNKNOWN".to_string(),
293.             recipient: None,
294.             memo: "Unmapped treasury effect".to_string(),
295.         },
296.     }
297. }
298. 
299. /// Convert a ProtocolEffect to a ProtocolChange (if applicable)
300. fn protocol_effect_to_change(
301.     effect: &crate::effects::ProtocolEffect,
302. ) -> Option<ProtocolChange> {
303.     use crate::effects::ProtocolEffect;
304. 
305.     match effect {
306.         ProtocolEffect::SetParameter {
307.             parameter_name,
308.             old_value_hash,
309.             new_value_json,
310.             effective_at,
311.         } => Some(ProtocolChange {
312.             parameter_name: parameter_name.clone(),
313.             old_value: old_value_hash.clone(),
314.             new_value: new_value_json.clone(),
315.             effective_at: *effective_at,
316.         }),
317.         ProtocolEffect::SetGovernanceConfig {
318.             domain_id,
319.             config_json,
320.             ..
321.         } => Some(ProtocolChange {
322.             parameter_name: format!("governance.config.{}", domain_id),
323.             old_value: String::new(),
324.             new_value: config_json.clone(),
325.             effective_at: 0,
326.         }),
327.         _ => None,
328.     }
329. }
330. 
331. /// Convert an ExecutionOutcome to an EffectResult
332. fn execution_outcome_to_effect_result(outcome: ExecutionOutcome, effect_id: &str) -> EffectResult {
333.     match outcome {
334.         ExecutionOutcome::Success { effects, .. } => EffectResult {
335.             effect_id: effect_id.to_string(),
336.             success: true,
337.             message: effects.join("; "),
338.             state_change_hash: None,
339.         },
340.         ExecutionOutcome::Failed { reason, .. } => EffectResult {
341.             effect_id: effect_id.to_string(),
342.             success: false,
343.             message: reason,
344.             state_change_hash: None,
345.         },
346.         ExecutionOutcome::Deferred { reason, .. } => EffectResult {
347.             effect_id: effect_id.to_string(),
348.             success: true,
349.             message: format!("Deferred: {}", reason),
350.             state_change_hash: None,
351.         },
352.     }
353. }

1. //! Effect-based execution dispatcher for governance proposals.
2. //!
3. //! This module provides a parallel execution path that:
4. //! 1. Translates `ProposalPayload` to `KernelEffect`s via apps/governance
5. //! 2. Executes effects via `KernelGovernanceExecutor`
6. //!
7. //! This runs **parallel to** the legacy `governance_handlers` path.
8. //! Sprint 3+ will switch over and remove the old handlers.
9. //!
10. //! # Architecture
11. //!
12. //! ```text
13. //! ProposalPayload (icn-governance)
14. //!        |
15. //!        v
16. //! translate_payload_to_effects (apps/governance)
17. //!        |
18. //!        v
19. //! Vec<KernelEffect> (icn-kernel-api)
20. //!        |
21. //!        v
22. //! KernelGovernanceExecutor::execute_effect (icn-core)
23. //!        |
24. //!        v
25. //! EffectResult (kernel primitive types only)
26. //! ```
27. 
28. use std::sync::Arc;
29. 
30. use anyhow::Result;
31. use tracing::{debug, error, info, warn};
32. 
33. use icn_governance::ProposalPayload;
34. use icn_governance_actor::translate_payload_to_effects;
35. use icn_kernel_api::effects::{EffectResult, KernelEffect};
36. use icn_kernel_api::governance::EffectExecutor;
37. 
38. use super::governance_executor::KernelGovernanceExecutor;
39. 
40. /// Dispatcher that executes governance proposals via the effect system.
41. ///
42. /// This is the new execution path using kernel-safe effects.
43. pub struct EffectDispatcher {
44.     /// The kernel executor for effect processing
45.     executor: Arc<KernelGovernanceExecutor>,
46. }
47. 
48. impl EffectDispatcher {
49.     /// Create a new effect dispatcher.
50.     pub fn new(executor: Arc<KernelGovernanceExecutor>) -> Self {
51.         Self { executor }
52.     }
53. 
54.     /// Execute a governance proposal payload through the effect system.
55.     ///
56.     /// This is the primary entry point for the new execution path.
57.     ///
58.     /// # Arguments
59.     /// * `payload` - The governance proposal payload to execute
60.     /// * `decision_receipt_id` - The receipt ID for audit linkage
61.     ///
62.     /// # Returns
63.     /// Vector of effect results (one per translated effect)
64.     pub async fn execute_proposal(
65.         &self,
66.         payload: &ProposalPayload,
67.         decision_receipt_id: &str,
68.     ) -> Result<Vec<EffectResult>> {
69.         // Step 1: Translate payload to kernel-safe effects
70.         let effects = translate_payload_to_effects(payload, decision_receipt_id);
71. 
72.         if effects.is_empty() {
73.             debug!(
74.                 receipt_id = %decision_receipt_id,
75.                 "No effects generated from proposal payload"
76.             );
77.             return Ok(vec![]);
78.         }
79. 
80.         info!(
81.             receipt_id = %decision_receipt_id,
82.             effect_count = effects.len(),
83.             "Executing {} effects via new effect path",
84.             effects.len()
85.         );
86. 
87.         // Step 2: Execute each effect via the kernel executor
88.         let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(effects.len());
89.         for effect in effects {
90.             let effect_type = effect_type_label(&effect);
91.             match self
92.                 .executor
93.                 .execute_effect(effect, decision_receipt_id)
94.                 .await
95.             {
96.                 Ok(result) => {
97.                     if result.success {
98.                         debug!(
99.                             receipt_id = %decision_receipt_id,
100.                             effect_type = %effect_type,
101.                             "Effect executed successfully"
102.                         );
103.                     } else {
104.                         warn!(
105.                             receipt_id = %decision_receipt_id,
106.                             effect_type = %effect_type,
107.                             message = %result.message,
108.                             "Effect execution returned failure"
109.                         );
110.                     }
111.                     results.push(result);
112.                 }
113.                 Err(e) => {
114.                     error!(
115.                         receipt_id = %decision_receipt_id,
116.                         effect_type = %effect_type,
117.                         error = %e,
118.                         "Effect execution failed"
119.                     );
120.                     results.push(EffectResult {
121.                         effect_id: decision_receipt_id.to_string(),
122.                         success: false,
123.                         message: format!("Execution error: {}", e),
124.                         state_change_hash: None,
125.                     });
126.                 }
127.             }
128.         }
129. 
130.         Ok(results)
131.     }
132. 
133.     /// Execute a batch of effects atomically via the executor.
134.     ///
135.     /// This is a lower-level API for when effects are already translated.
136.     pub async fn execute_effects(
137.         &self,
138.         effects: Vec<KernelEffect>,
139.         decision_receipt_id: &str,
140.     ) -> Result<Vec<EffectResult>> {
141.         self.executor
142.             .execute_effects_batch(effects, decision_receipt_id)
143.             .await
144.     }
145. }
146. 
147. /// Get a label for an effect type (for logging/metrics).
148. fn effect_type_label(effect: &KernelEffect) -> &'static str {
149.     match effect {
150.         KernelEffect::Treasury(_) => "treasury",
151.         KernelEffect::Protocol(_) => "protocol",
152.         KernelEffect::Membership(_) => "membership",
153.         KernelEffect::Control(_) => "control",
154.         KernelEffect::Federation(_) => "federation",
155.         KernelEffect::NoOp { .. } => "noop",
156.     }
157. }
158. 
159. /// Create an event subscription callback that uses the effect dispatcher.
160. ///
161. /// This provides the same interface as `create_governance_subscription` but
162. /// executes through the new effect path.
163. ///
164. /// # Note
165. /// This is wired in **parallel** to the old subscription. The old path
166. /// is still the primary execution path until Sprint 3+ migration.
167. pub fn create_effect_subscription(
168.     dispatcher: Arc<EffectDispatcher>,
169. ) -> Arc<dyn Fn(crate::events::SystemEvent) + Send + Sync> {
170.     Arc::new(move |event| {
171.         use crate::events::SystemEvent;
172. 
173.         match &event {
174.             SystemEvent::ProposalAccepted {
175.                 proposal_id,
176.                 payload,
177.                 domain_id,
178.                 ..
179.             } => {
180.                 // Deserialize the payload
181.                 match serde_json::from_value::<ProposalPayload>(payload.clone()) {
182.                     Ok(proposal_payload) => {
183.                         // Generate receipt ID from proposal + domain for audit linkage
184.                         let receipt_id = format!("receipt-{}-{}", domain_id, proposal_id);
185. 
186.                         // Spawn async execution (we're in a sync callback)
187.                         let dispatcher = dispatcher.clone();
188.                         let proposal_id = proposal_id.clone();
189.                         let receipt_id_owned = receipt_id.clone();
190.                         tokio::spawn(async move {
191.                             match dispatcher
192.                                 .execute_proposal(&proposal_payload, &receipt_id_owned)
193.                                 .await
194.                             {
195.                                 Ok(results) => {
196.                                     let success_count = results.iter().filter(|r| r.success).count();
197.                                     info!(
198.                                         proposal_id = %proposal_id,
199.                                         receipt_id = %receipt_id_owned,
200.                                         total = results.len(),
201.                                         success = success_count,
202.                                         "Effect-based execution complete"
203.                                     );
204.                                 }
205.                                 Err(e) => {
206.                                     error!(
207.                                         proposal_id = %proposal_id,
208.                                         receipt_id = %receipt_id_owned,
209.                                         error = %e,
210.                                         "Effect-based execution failed"
211.                                     );
212.                                 }
213.                             }
214.                         });
215.                     }
216.                     Err(e) => {
217.                         error!(
218.                             proposal_id = %proposal_id,
219.                             error = %e,
220.                             "Failed to deserialize ProposalPayload for effect execution"
221.                         );
222.                     }
223.                 }
224.             }
225.             _ => {}
226.         }
227.     })
228. }

1. //! Supervisor lifecycle management
2. //!
3. //! This module contains the main supervisor startup and shutdown orchestration logic.
4. //! It coordinates actor initialization, background task spawning, and graceful shutdown.
5. 
6. use anyhow::Result;
7. use std::sync::Arc;
8. use tokio::select;
9. use tokio::sync::RwLock;
10. use tokio::task::JoinSet;
11. use tracing::{debug, info, warn};
12. 
13. use icn_identity::IdentityBundle;
14. use icn_kernel_api::services::ServiceRegistry;
15. 
16. use crate::config::Config;
17. use crate::runtime::ShutdownTx;
18. 
19. use super::actors::{
20.     CoreActorHandles, EventSubscriptionHandles, GatewayActorHandles, ShutdownHandles,
21. };
22. 
23. /// Run the supervisor lifecycle
24. ///
25. /// This is the main entry point for supervisor operation. It:
26. /// 1. Initializes metrics and observability
27. /// 2. Spawns all actors (if identity bundle is available)
28. /// 3. Configures actor communication and bridging
29. /// 4. Spawns background tasks
30. /// 5. Waits for shutdown signal
31. /// 6. Performs graceful shutdown
32. ///
33. /// # Service Registry
34. ///
35. /// If `service_registry` is provided, services from it will be used instead of
36. /// creating internal implementations. This enables proper kernel/app separation
37. /// where the daemon constructs domain services from app crates.
38. pub async fn run_supervisor(
39.     config: Config,
40.     identity_bundle: Option<IdentityBundle>,
41.     shutdown_tx: ShutdownTx,
42.     service_registry: Option<ServiceRegistry>,
43.     bootstrap_handles: Option<super::BootstrapHandles>,
44. ) -> Result<()> {
45.     info!("Supervisor starting");
46. 
47.     // Log service registry status
48.     if let Some(ref registry) = service_registry {
49.         info!("Using daemon-provided service registry");
50.         if registry.trust().is_some() {
51.             info!("  - TrustService: provided");
52.         }
53.         if registry.governance().is_some() {
54.             info!("  - GovernanceService: provided");
55.         }
56.         if registry.ledger().is_some() {
57.             info!("  - LedgerService: provided");
58.         }
59.         if registry.security().is_some() {
60.             info!("  - SecurityService: provided");
61.         }
62.     } else {
63.         debug!("No service registry provided, using internal implementations");
64.     }
65. 
66.     // Initialize metrics
67.     icn_obs::init_metrics()?;
68. 
69.     // Set supervisor state to starting
70.     icn_obs::metrics::supervisor::state_set(1);
71. 
72.     // Start metrics server
73.     let metrics_port = config.observability.metrics_port;
74.     if let Err(e) = icn_obs::start_metrics_server(metrics_port).await {
75.         warn!("Failed to start metrics server: {}", e);
76.         icn_obs::metrics::supervisor::error_inc("metrics_server_start");
77.     }
78. 
79.     let mut shutdown_rx = shutdown_tx.subscribe();
80. 
81.     // Track spawned background tasks for graceful shutdown
82.     let mut background_tasks: JoinSet<()> = JoinSet::new();
83. 
84.     let mut gateway_handles = GatewayActorHandles::default();
85.     let mut event_subscriptions = EventSubscriptionHandles::default();
86.     let mut shutdown_handles = ShutdownHandles::default();
87. 
88.     // Spawn actors (requires identity bundle from unlocked keystore)
89.     let core_handles = if let Some(identity_bundle) = &identity_bundle {
90.         spawn_actors_with_identity(
91.             &config,
92.             identity_bundle,
93.             &shutdown_tx,
94.             &mut background_tasks,
95.             &mut gateway_handles,
96.             &mut event_subscriptions,
97.             &mut shutdown_handles,
98.             service_registry.as_ref(),
99.             bootstrap_handles,
100.         )
```

1. //! Effect-based execution dispatcher for governance proposals.
2. //!
3. //! This module provides the kernel's effect execution layer. It receives
4. //! pre-translated `KernelEffect`s and executes them via `KernelGovernanceExecutor`.
5. //!
6. //! **IMPORTANT**: This is a kernel module. It must NOT import app/domain types
7. //! like `ProposalPayload`. Translation from domain types to effects happens
8. //! in the app layer (icn-governance-actor) BEFORE calling into the kernel.
9. //!
10. //! # Architecture
11. //!
12. //! ```text
13. //! [App Layer - icn-governance-actor]
14. //! ProposalPayload → translate_payload_to_effects() → Vec<KernelEffect>
15. //!                                                          |
16. //!                                                          v
17. //! [Kernel Layer - icn-core]
18. //! EffectDispatcher::execute_effects(effects) → Vec<EffectResult>
19. //! ```
20. //!
21. //! This runs **parallel to** the legacy `governance_handlers` path.
22. //! Sprint 3+ will switch over and remove the old handlers.
23. 
24. use std::sync::Arc;
25. 
26. use anyhow::Result;
27. use tracing::{debug, error, info, warn};
28. 
29. use icn_kernel_api::effects::{EffectResult, KernelEffect};
30. use icn_kernel_api::governance::EffectExecutor;
31. 
32. use super::governance_executor::KernelGovernanceExecutor;
33. 
34. /// Dispatcher that executes governance proposals via the effect system.
35. ///
36. /// This is the new execution path using kernel-safe effects.
37. pub struct EffectDispatcher {
38.     /// The kernel executor for effect processing
39.     executor: Arc<KernelGovernanceExecutor>,
40. }
41. 
42. impl EffectDispatcher {
43.     /// Create a new effect dispatcher.
44.     pub fn new(executor: Arc<KernelGovernanceExecutor>) -> Self {
45.         Self { executor }
46.     }
47. 
48.     /// Execute a batch of pre-translated kernel effects.
49.     ///
50.     /// This is the primary entry point for the effect execution path.
51.     /// The caller (app layer) is responsible for translating domain payloads
52.     /// to `KernelEffect`s before calling this method.
53.     ///
54.     /// # Arguments
55.     /// * `effects` - Pre-translated kernel effects to execute
56.     /// * `decision_receipt_id` - The receipt ID for audit linkage
57.     ///
58.     /// # Returns
59.     /// Vector of effect results (one per effect)
60.     pub async fn execute_effects(
61.         &self,
62.         effects: Vec<KernelEffect>,
63.         decision_receipt_id: &str,
64.     ) -> Result<Vec<EffectResult>> {
65.         if effects.is_empty() {
66.             debug!(
67.                 receipt_id = %decision_receipt_id,
68.                 "No effects to execute"
69.             );
70.             return Ok(vec![]);
71.         }
72. 
73.         info!(
74.             receipt_id = %decision_receipt_id,
75.             effect_count = effects.len(),
76.             "Executing {} effects via effect dispatcher",
77.             effects.len()
78.         );
79. 
80.         // Execute each effect via the kernel executor
````

Yes, pleasee

Alright. Here’s the exact migration order for those three proposal types, designed to keep the surface area tight and avoid “oops, now core imports governance again.”

I’m going to assume the current state is:

icn-kernel-api has KernelEffect + EffectExecutor (or equivalent).

apps/governance has an execution handler that can translate from ProposalPayload (domain) → KernelEffect.

icn-core has a KernelGovernanceExecutor that can execute effects via kernel services.

Legacy governance_handlers/* still exist and are still used by lifecycle in places.

Goal: migrate 3 representative paths end-to-end through the new effect route, with tests, then you’re safe to delete legacy.

Global Rule (Non-Negotiable)

Core never sees governance domain types.
No ProposalPayload, no TreasuryProposalOperation, no GovernanceProofV2, no ProposalId.

Core sees:

IDs (ReceiptId / Did / DomainId as opaque)

hashes

amounts

simple enums that live in icn-kernel-api

kernel services

If you violate this once, you’re back to “relocation.”

Step 0: Pick a Single “Switch” Point

You need one place where you decide:

“Use legacy handler” vs

“Use effect path”

Pick one of these as the switch:

the supervisor lifecycle where proposals are dispatched, or

the governance actor execution callback, or

the handler subscription wiring.

Prefer: a single dispatcher function in icn-core that can route to either path.
That gives you safe parallelism until you delete legacy.

Acceptance criteria:

For each proposal type you migrate, you can flip it to the effect path without touching other types.

Step 1: Treasury Spend (first)

Why first: it forces you to get settlement discipline right early.

1A) Define kernel-safe effect shape

In icn-kernel-api:

KernelEffect::Treasury(TreasuryEffect::Spend { ... })

Minimum fields:

treasury_did

to_did

amount

currency (or CurrencyId)

decision_receipt_id (or decision hash)

optional: memo_hash / purpose_hash

No governance types.

1B) Governance app translation

In apps/governance execution handler:

match the treasury spend proposal payload

convert to KernelEffect::Treasury(Spend {…})

call effect_executor.execute(effect).await

If translation needs additional data, fetch it inside the app, not core.

1C) Core executor implementation

In icn-core:

implement EffectExecutor::execute(KernelEffect)

handle TreasuryEffect::Spend by emitting SettlementIntent

or calling Treasury kernel service which emits intent internally

But do not write ledger directly if that’s your invariant.
You want:

Effect → SettlementIntent → LedgerOracle → LedgerEntry

1D) Tests (must exist)

Add an integration-ish test that proves:

governance payload produces effect

effect execution results in a ledger/tresury observable outcome

provenance links back to decision receipt id/hash

This is where you discover hidden coupling fast.

Exit criteria for Treasury Spend:

No new governance imports in core.

Test passes via effect path.

Legacy handler still exists but is no longer used for this proposal type.

Step 2: Protocol Change (second)

Why second: it proves you can mutate “system state” without letting governance types seep into kernel.

2A) Define Protocol effect

In icn-kernel-api:

KernelEffect::Protocol(ProtocolEffect::Upgrade { target_version, artifact_hash, decision_receipt_id })

Keep it minimal:

version / semver string

hash of the upgrade artifact/config bundle

decision receipt id/hash

2B) Governance translation

The governance app decides what “upgrade” means and produces the effect.

If you need validation rules, they live in:

kernel service (as policy)

or governance rules
…but not as governance domain types crossing boundary.

2C) Core executor

Core receives ProtocolEffect::Upgrade and calls a kernel service like:

ProtocolService::apply_upgrade(intent)

This should be a no-op in early phases except writing an auditable state transition.

2D) Tests

Test that:

decision → effect emitted

effect → protocol state record exists

audit/provenance chain references decision receipt

Exit criteria for Protocol Change:

effect path works end-to-end

protocol application is traceable, repeatable, and non-leaky

Step 3: Federation Proposal (third)

Why third: this is the nastiest one because it tries to pull identity/trust/membership into the same transaction.

You are not implementing federation routing. You’re proving effect grammar can represent it.

3A) Define Federation effect

In icn-kernel-api:

KernelEffect::Federation(FederationEffect::InviteMember { federation_id, subject_did, role, decision_receipt_id })

or:

join/leave

add/remove member

update policy hash

Everything must be IDs + hashes.

3B) Governance translation

Governance app interprets FederationProposal and emits one or more effects.

If a proposal requires multiple steps:

emit multiple effects in a deterministic order

all linked to the same decision receipt id/hash

(optional) add an “effect batch hash”

3C) Core executor

Core executes federation effects by calling:

membership service / federation service

writes state transitions (again traceable)

3D) Tests

Test that:

federation proposal emits correct effect(s)

executor applies membership/federation state

provenance links to decision receipt

Exit criteria for Federation:

effect batching (if needed) is deterministic

no governance types cross

the services called do not demand governance types

Final Step: Only after those 3 are green

Now you do the destructive cleanup:

Update lifecycle to route those proposal types to effect path by default

Remove corresponding legacy handler match arms

Delete legacy handler module only when all proposal types are migrated (or stub legacy out)

Remove icn-governance dependency from icn-core/Cargo.toml

Re-run firewall baseline

The One Trap to Avoid

Do not “solve it” by re-exporting domain types.
No hiding. No aliasing. No pretending.

If core needs a field you think only domain type has, that’s a signal:

either add it as a primitive field to the effect

or make the app fetch/derive it

or treat it as opaque hash/id

Micro-checklist you can paste into the plan

For each migrated proposal type:

 Translator exists in governance app

 Effect variant exists in kernel-api

 Executor handles the effect in core without domain imports

 Deterministic provenance linkage to decision receipt

 Test proving end-to-end path

 Legacy handler path disabled for this type

## Stage 2.1: Treasury Spend end-to-end (the first domino)

### Step 0 — Baseline reality check (5 minutes)

You want to know what already exists before you “implement” something twice.

Run:


**Stop condition:** if any of those are missing, you fill *that* gap only. No broad refactors.

---

## Stage 2.2: Make Treasury Spend provably “receipt-linked”

Right now you have effects, but the real win is **provenance**: the spend must link back to the decision receipt (and later allocation).

### 1) Extend the effect payload (if needed)

For Treasury Spend, the effect must carry only kernel-safe primitives *plus provenance pointers*:

* `treasury_did`
* `to_did`
* `amount`
* `currency`
* `decision_receipt_id` (or `receipt_id`)
* `decision_hash` (or canonical content hash)

If your effect currently lacks provenance fields, add them **to the effect struct**, not to kernel internals.

Where:

* `crates/icn-kernel-api/src/effects.rs` (Treasury effect payload)

**Rule:** no `ProposalPayload`, no `GovernanceProof*`, no domain enums.

### 2) Translator produces spend effect with provenance

In:

* `apps/governance/src/handlers/execution.rs`

Make the translator build the effect with provenance extracted from the decision receipt context (however you currently represent it).

**Stop condition:** if translator needs kernel types it doesn’t have, you move the minimal ID/hash into the effect itself, not vice versa.

### 3) Executor consumes spend effect and calls the right kernel services

In:

* `crates/icn-core/src/supervisor/governance_executor.rs`

Have the effect executor translate **effect -\> kernel operations** using existing services.

**Hard rule:** the executor never parses governance payloads.

---

## Stage 2.3: Add the integration test that proves the path (this is the real deliverable)

Add exactly one integration test that proves:

1. A treasury spend proposal exists (or synthetic decision receipt constructed)
2. Governance produces a **decision receipt**
3. Translator produces a **Treasury Spend effect**
4. Dispatcher routes it
5. Executor executes it
6. Ledger write (or treasury state change) exists **and references provenance**

Where to put it (pick the repo’s existing pattern, but don’t fight structure):

* If you already have tests near dispatcher/executor, add it there.
* Otherwise add a minimal integration test in `icn-core` test module for the dispatcher+executor.

**Acceptance criteria:**

* test asserts: “ledger entry has decision_hash OR receipt_id stored in metadata/provenance field”
* test asserts: “no governance domain types imported into icn-core new path files”

---

## Stage 2.4: Disable legacy treasury spend handler only (feature-gate)

Do **not** delete legacy handlers yet. Just stop them from handling Treasury Spend.

Two safe patterns:

* a runtime gate (config flag) like `use_effect_dispatcher_for_treasury_spend=true`
* a compile-time gate (feature flag) if that’s your existing style

You want to be able to flip back instantly if something subtle breaks.

**Stop condition:** if disabling legacy handler requires touching 10 unrelated places, don’t. Add a single routing if-statement at the seam where proposals dispatch.

---

# What I would deploy agents to do (if you’re actually using a fleet)

Yes: deploy them in the same order you listed, but make it “one agent per atomic artifact”:

1. **Agent A:** verify translator+executor for spend (compile + unit test)
2. **Agent B:** add integration test proving receipt → effect → execution → ledger provenance
3. **Agent C:** implement legacy spend handler disable gate (no deletion)

And *no one touches gateway* during this.

2.2 Decide where to store Decision Registry index

- GET /decisions?coop_id=...&meeting_id=...&tag=...&after=...&before=...
- GET /decisions/{decision_receipt_id} (returns receipt + metadata + provenance links)
- GET /decisions/{decision_receipt_id}/trace (parents chain, effects, ledger link if exists)

## 3) Red flags inside the transcript (things to distrust first)

Here’s what pings my “agent narrative” alarm:

* **“registry.rs (~600 lines)”**: agents love dropping huge files. Huge files often mean:

* explicit authorization/trust gating expectations,

---

## 4) Architectural “stop/go” checks for the Decision Registry

If the registry is meant to replace “Google Drive for summit decisions,” the risk is you accidentally create:

* a centralized “truth table”
* or an untrusted dumping ground
* or a gateway API that becomes the de facto authority

So enforce these invariants:

### Registry should store *canonical decision references*, not re-decide truth

* It should index decisions by **decision_hash**
* It should accept / display **DecisionReceipt** (or references to it)
* It should not treat gateway-local IDs as canonical identity across nodes

### Trust gating should be explicit

Even if pilot is “single node,” don’t bake in assumptions that will poison federation later.

### Provenance should be queryable end-to-end

A “trace view” endpoint is good *only if* it’s wired to the actual kernel-safe effect chain and ledger entry provenance, not a hand-built narrative.

```
1. //! Decision Registry API endpoints
2. //!
3. //! Provides REST API for managing governance meetings and decisions.
4. //! This is a "Google Drive replacement" for co-op meetings/decisions,
5. //! indexing over canonical receipts without touching kernel primitives.
6. //!
7. //! ## Endpoints
8. //!
9. //! ### Meetings
10. //! - `POST /v1/registry/meetings` - Create a meeting
11. //! - `GET /v1/registry/meetings?coop_id=...` - List meetings for a coop
12. //!
13. //! ### Decisions
14. //! - `POST /v1/registry/decisions` - Index a decision
15. //! - `GET /v1/registry/decisions?coop_id=...&meeting_id=...&tag=...` - List decisions
16. //! - `GET /v1/registry/decisions/{id}` - Get decision details
17. //! - `GET /v1/registry/decisions/{id}/trace` - Get decision trace/provenance
18. 
19. use actix_web::{get, post, web, HttpRequest, HttpResponse};
20. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
21. use std::collections::HashMap;
22. use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock};
23. 
24. use crate::error::{GatewayError, Result};
25. use crate::middleware::{get_claims, require_scope};
26. 
27. // ============================================================================
28. // Types (mirrors icn-governance-actor/src/registry/models.rs)
29. // ============================================================================
30. 
31. /// Status of a governance decision.
32. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
33. #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
34. pub enum DecisionStatus {
35.     /// Decision is pending (voting in progress).
36.     Pending,
37.     /// Decision was approved.
38.     Approved,
39.     /// Decision was rejected.
40.     Rejected,
41. }
42. 
43. impl Default for DecisionStatus {
44.     fn default() -> Self {
45.         Self::Pending
46.     }
47. }
48. 
49. /// A cooperative meeting record.
50. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
51. #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
52. pub struct Meeting {
53.     /// Unique meeting identifier, e.g., "mtg-2026-02-10-summit".
54.     pub meeting_id: String,
55.     /// Cooperative DID that owns this meeting.
56.     pub coop_id: String,
57.     /// Human-readable title, e.g., "Summit Planning 2026".
58.     pub title: String,
59.     /// Meeting start time as Unix timestamp.
60.     pub starts_at: u64,
61.     /// Optional meeting notes.
62.     #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
63.     pub notes: Option<String>,
64.     /// Creation timestamp.
65.     pub created_at: u64,
66. }
67. 
68. /// An index entry for a governance decision.
69. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
70. #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
71. pub struct DecisionIndexEntry {
72.     /// Primary key, links to canonical receipt.
73.     pub decision_receipt_id: String,
74.     /// Canonical hash (immutable anchor).
75.     pub decision_hash: String,
76.     /// Cooperative DID.
77.     pub coop_id: String,
78.     /// Optional meeting association.
79.     #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
80.     pub meeting_id: Option<String>,
81.     /// Human-readable summary.
82.     pub title: String,
83.     /// Searchable tags, e.g., ["budget", "approved"].
84.     pub tags: Vec<String>,
85.     /// Current status of the decision.
86.     pub status: DecisionStatus,
87.     /// Creation timestamp.
88.     pub created_at: u64,
89.     /// Type of proposal, e.g., "text", "treasury_spend".
90.     pub proposal_type: String,
91.     /// If this decision triggered a treasury action, the effect ID.
92.     #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
93.     pub treasury_effect_id: Option<String>,
94. }
95. 
96. /// Decision trace showing provenance and effects.
97. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
98. #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
99. pub struct DecisionTrace {
100.     /// The decision hash.
101.     pub decision_hash: String,
102.     /// Parent receipts (decisions this depends on).
103.     pub parent_receipts: Vec<String>,
104.     /// Effects triggered by this decision.
105.     pub effects: Vec<DecisionEffect>,
106.     /// If this decision triggered a ledger entry.
107.     #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
108.     pub ledger_entry_id: Option<String>,
109.     /// Provenance chain (ordered list of related decisions).
110.     pub provenance_chain: Vec<String>,
111. }
112. 
113. /// An effect triggered by a decision.
114. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
115. #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
116. pub struct DecisionEffect {
117.     /// Type of effect, e.g., "treasury_disbursement", "membership_change".
118.     #[serde(rename = "type")]
119.     pub effect_type: String,
120.     /// Details about the effect.
```

```
169.             }

172.     }
```

Make sure `/trace` isn’t just “joined from in-memory indexes.” It should follow canonical IDs:

```
3. //! These are APP-LAYER types for indexing governance decisions and meetings.
4. //! They provide a "Google Drive replacement" for co-op meetings/decisions,
5. //! indexing over canonical receipts without touching kernel primitives.
6. 
7. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
8. 
9. /// Status of a governance decision.
10. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
11. #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
12. pub enum DecisionStatus {
13.     /// Decision is pending (voting in progress).
14.     Pending,
15.     /// Decision was approved.
16.     Approved,
17.     /// Decision was rejected.
18.     Rejected,
19. }
20. 
21. impl Default for DecisionStatus {
22.     fn default() -> Self {
23.         Self::Pending
24.     }
25. }
26. 
27. /// A cooperative meeting record.
28. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
29. pub struct Meeting {
30.     /// Unique meeting identifier, e.g., "mtg-2026-02-10-summit".
31.     pub meeting_id: String,
32.     /// Cooperative DID that owns this meeting.
33.     pub coop_id: String,
34.     /// Human-readable title, e.g., "Summit Planning 2026".
35.     pub title: String,
36.     /// Meeting start time as Unix timestamp.
37.     pub starts_at: u64,
38.     /// Optional meeting notes.
39.     pub notes: Option<String>,
40.     /// Creation timestamp.
41.     pub created_at: u64,
42. }
43. 
44. /// An index entry for a governance decision.
45. ///
46. /// This is an APP-LAYER INDEX over canonical receipts. The `decision_receipt_id`
47. /// and `decision_hash` link back to the immutable canonical receipt, while the
48. /// other fields provide searchable metadata.
49. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
50. pub struct DecisionIndexEntry {
51.     /// Primary key, links to canonical receipt.
52.     pub decision_receipt_id: String,
53.     /// Canonical hash (immutable anchor).
54.     pub decision_hash: String,
55.     /// Cooperative DID.
56.     pub coop_id: String,
57.     /// Optional meeting association.
58.     pub meeting_id: Option<String>,
59.     /// Human-readable summary.
60.     pub title: String,
61.     /// Searchable tags, e.g., ["budget", "approved"].
62.     pub tags: Vec<String>,
63.     /// Current status of the decision.
64.     pub status: DecisionStatus,
65.     /// Creation timestamp.
66.     pub created_at: u64,
67.     /// Type of proposal, e.g., "text", "treasury_spend".
68.     pub proposal_type: String,
69.     /// If this decision triggered a treasury action, the effect ID.
70.     pub treasury_effect_id: Option<String>,
71. }
72. 
73. /// Filter criteria for querying decisions.
74. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
75. pub struct DecisionFilter {
76.     /// Filter by cooperative DID.
77.     pub coop_id: Option<String>,
78.     /// Filter by meeting ID.
79.     pub meeting_id: Option<String>,
80.     /// Filter by tag (any match).
81.     pub tag: Option<String>,
82.     /// Filter decisions created after this timestamp.
83.     pub after: Option<u64>,
84.     /// Filter decisions created before this timestamp.
85.     pub before: Option<u64>,
86.     /// Filter by proposal type.
87.     pub proposal_type: Option<String>,
88. }
89. 
90. impl DecisionFilter {
91.     /// Create an empty filter (matches all).
92.     pub fn new() -> Self {
93.         Self::default()
94.     }
95. 
96.     /// Filter by cooperative ID.
97.     pub fn with_coop_id(mut self, coop_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
98.         self.coop_id = Some(coop_id.into());
99.         self
100.     }
101. 
102.     /// Filter by meeting ID.
103.     pub fn with_meeting_id(mut self, meeting_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
104.         self.meeting_id = Some(meeting_id.into());
105.         self
106.     }
107. 
108.     /// Filter by tag.
109.     pub fn with_tag(mut self, tag: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
110.         self.tag = Some(tag.into());
111.         self
112.     }
113. 
114.     /// Filter by creation time range (after).
115.     pub fn after(mut self, timestamp: u64) -> Self {
116.         self.after = Some(timestamp);
117.         self
118.     }
119. 
120.     /// Filter by creation time range (before).
121.     pub fn before(mut self, timestamp: u64) -> Self {
122.         self.before = Some(timestamp);
123.         self
124.     }
125. 
126.     /// Filter by proposal type.
127.     pub fn with_proposal_type(mut self, proposal_type: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
128.         self.proposal_type = Some(proposal_type.into());
129.         self
130.     }
131. 
132.     /// Check if a decision entry matches this filter.
133.     pub fn matches(&self, entry: &DecisionIndexEntry) -> bool {
134.         if let Some(ref coop_id) = self.coop_id {
135.             if &entry.coop_id != coop_id {
136.                 return false;
137.             }
138.         }
139.         if let Some(ref meeting_id) = self.meeting_id {
140.             if entry.meeting_id.as_ref() != Some(meeting_id) {
141.                 return false;
142.             }
143.         }
144.         if let Some(ref tag) = self.tag {
145.             if !entry.tags.contains(tag) {
146.                 return false;
147.             }
148.         }
149.         if let Some(after) = self.after {
150.             if entry.created_at < after {
151.                 return false;
152.             }
153.         }
154.         if let Some(before) = self.before {
155.             if entry.created_at > before {
156.                 return false;
157.             }
158.         }
159.         if let Some(ref proposal_type) = self.proposal_type {
160.             if &entry.proposal_type != proposal_type {
161.                 return false;
162.             }
163.         }
164.         true
165.     }
166. }
167.
```

<sub>⏱️ 898m 20s</sub>

### 👤 User

Perfect — this is enough to do a real review.

And it surfaces two **critical correctness issues** plus one **pilot-risk** issue.

---

## 1) The provenance assertion you quoted is not the provenance invariant we want

You pasted:

```rust
assert_eq!(
    result.effect_id, decision_receipt_id,
    "effect_id must match decision_receipt_id for provenance tracking"
);
```

That’s… a *naming convention check*. Not provenance.

### Why it’s weak

* `effect_id == decision_receipt_id` proves you reused a string, not that the ledger entry is cryptographically or structurally linked to the canonical decision anchor.
* It can pass even if:

  * the ledger entry is never written,
  * the ledger entry is written without provenance,
  * or `decision_hash` is ignored entirely.

### What the invariant actually is (your own stated one)

From your Stage 2.1 notes (and your “hard STOP” philosophy):

* **Cross-node canonical equality anchor:** `decision_hash`
* **Node-local provenance:** receipt id, signatures, attestations, etc.
* Therefore: **the ledger entry must carry both**

  * `decision_receipt_id`
  * `decision_hash`

If either is missing, the pilot claim collapses.

So: keep the “effect_id == decision_receipt_id” if you like, but it’s not the proof.

---

## 2) You have a real drift hazard: snake_case vs camelCase mismatch

You said:

* Governance registry models are snake_case JSON keys.
* Gateway registry uses `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.

That means:

* identical Rust struct fields ≠ identical wire contract
* and clients will experience inconsistent API semantics depending on which service they hit.

### Pilot impact

If your summit demo script or any thin client consumes both gateway and governance endpoints (even indirectly), you’ll get “it works on my endpoint” behavior.

### Fix direction

Pick one of these, **now**, before it ossifies:

* **Option A (recommended):** Gateway and governance both emit **camelCase** for any public HTTP JSON.
* **Option B:** Both emit **snake_case**.
* **Option C:** Declare gateway as the only public API surface and ensure governance models never leak directly to clients.

Given your “gateway is the edge” architecture, Option C + A is the cleanest: the gateway contract is canonical.

---

## 3) Your “registry is index-only” claim is plausible, but not proven until storage/persistence & trace correctness are tested

Right now registry is described as:

* in-memory `RwLock\<HashMap\<...\>\>`
* handlers assemble trace chains

That is demoable. But the `/trace` endpoint can still be “storybook mode” if it isn’t forced to walk the actual canonical chain.

---

# What I’d change immediately (concrete, minimal, pilot-correct)

## A) Upgrade the golden-path test to assert ledger provenance

Add assertions like this (pseudocode-ish, but you’ll know the exact types):

```rust
// after executing TreasuryEffect::Spend
let ledger_entry = ledger.get_entry(result.ledger_entry_id).await?;

// hard pilot invariant:
assert_eq!(ledger_entry.provenance.decision_receipt_id, decision_receipt_id);
assert_eq!(ledger_entry.provenance.decision_hash, decision_hash);
```

If your ledger entry doesn’t currently store provenance, then that is the missing pilot-critical feature, not “nice to have.”

You already carried `decision_receipt_id + decision_hash` inside `TreasuryEffect::Spend`. The ledger write needs to persist it.

## B) Make `/trace` walk canonical IDs, not “whatever we cached”

Force trace to resolve:

* decision_hash → decision_receipt_id(s)
* decision_receipt_id → effect receipt / effect execution record
* effect execution → ledger entry id
* ledger entry → provenance fields

And add a test that fails if any step is mocked.

## C) Add a drift tripwire (cheap and effective)

Since you intentionally mirror types, you need an alarm when they diverge.

Easiest: snapshot the serialized field set (and casing!) for the gateway DTOs and governance models.

Example concept:

* Serialize empty/default instances (or derive schema using `schemars` if you already use it)
* Compare keys:

  * `gateway_keys == expected_keys`
  * `governance_keys == expected_keys`
  * plus casing match

If you don’t want a schema dependency, do a “JSON keys list” test.

---

# Quick read on the commit itself

`0d5031b2` adding `registry.rs` with ~717 LOC is not inherently bad, but it’s a smell. The danger isn’t “big file.” It’s:

* too much logic sitting at the edge with no persistence
* and contract drift (which you already hit via casing)

If the registry is going to exist, it should be:

* small API surface
* deterministic IDs
* persistence layer (even SQLite)
* and strict separation: index metadata + references only

---

# The one question I *don’t* need you to answer, but you should decide now

**Is the gateway registry the canonical public API contract?**

If yes, then:

* governance registry models should be internal
* and gateway’s casing/shape becomes “the contract”

If no, then you need to align casing across both immediately.

Either way, leaving them different guarantees pain.

<sub>⏱️ 899m 4s</sub>

Now I have the full picture. Let me summarize and create a fix plan:

---

## Critical Findings Summary

### Issue 1: Treasury Executor is a Placeholder
**Lines 142-165** of `governance_executor.rs`:
```rust
// TODO: Implement actual treasury operations via ledger
// For now, log and return success as a placeholder
```

The `KernelTreasuryExecutor::execute_treasury_operation` just logs and returns `Success`. **No ledger entry is created.**

### Issue 2: JournalEntry Lacks Provenance Fields
`JournalEntry` in `icn-ledger/src/types.rs` has:
- `id`, `timestamp`, `author`, `contract_ref`, `accounts`, `parents`, `signature`, `nonce`

**Missing**: `decision_receipt_id`, `decision_hash`

The `nonce` field can optionally be set to a receipt_id, but that's not structured provenance.

### Issue 3: Casing Drift
- Gateway: `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`
- Governance models: No `rename_all` (defaults to snake_case)

---

## Fix Plan

I'll implement the fixes in order of criticality:

1. **Add provenance fields to JournalEntry** (ledger-provenance)
2. **Wire treasury executor to create real ledger entries** 
3. **Fix casing drift** in governance models
4. **Add golden-path test** that asserts full chain

```
72.     pub fn build(self) -> Result<JournalEntry> {
73.         // Validate double-entry invariant: Σ debits == Σ credits per currency

75.

88.             accounts: self.accounts,
89.             parents: self.parents,
90.             signature: None, // Will be set by caller
91.             nonce: self.nonce,
92.         };
93.

96.

100. 
101. /// Validate double-entry bookkeeping invariant
102. /// For each currency, the sum of debits must equal the sum of credits
103. fn validate_double_entry(accounts: &[AccountDelta]) -> Result<()> {
104.     // Group by currency and sum debits/credits
105.     let mut currency_totals: HashMap<String, (i64, i64)> = HashMap::new();
106. 
107.     for delta in accounts {
108.         let (total_debits, total_credits) = currency_totals
109.             .entry(delta.currency.clone())
110.             .or_insert((0, 0));
111. 
112.         *total_debits += delta.debit.unwrap_or(0);
113.         *total_credits += delta.credit.unwrap_or(0);
114.     }
115. 
116.     // Check that debits == credits for each currency
117.     for (currency, (debits, credits)) in currency_totals.iter() {
118.         if debits != credits {
119.             bail!(
120.                 "Double-entry invariant violated for currency '{currency}': debits={debits}, credits={credits}"
121.             );
122.         }
123.     }
124. 
125.     Ok(())
126. }
127. 
128. /// Validate that all amounts are positive
129. fn validate_positive_amounts(accounts: &[AccountDelta]) -> Result<()> {
130.     for delta in accounts {
131.         if let Some(debit) = delta.debit {
132.             if debit < 0 {
133.                 bail!(
134.                     "Negative debit amount not allowed: {} for account {}",
135.                     debit,
136.                     delta.account_id
137.                 );
138.             }
139.         }
140. 
141.         if let Some(credit) = delta.credit {
142.             if credit < 0 {
143.                 bail!(
144.                     "Negative credit amount not allowed: {} for account {}",
145.                     credit,
146.                     delta.account_id
147.                 );
148.             }
149.         }
150.     }
151. 
152.     Ok(())
153. }
```

### 👤 User

Yeah — this is the right kind of diagnostic work, and it also confirms the exact problem I was worried about:

The pilot claim is still not true yet.

You’ve improved the schema (ledger can now carry provenance), but you still haven’t wired the Treasury executor → ledger write path, so the end-to-end chain is still broken.

And there are a couple of “agent-log tells” / contradictions in what you pasted that you should treat as not-yet-trusted until you eyeball the diff.

What’s genuinely good in what you found
✅ Critical finding was correct: Treasury executor is a placeholder

If KernelTreasuryExecutor::execute_treasury_operation logs and returns success, then:

no ledger entry is created

any test “passing” in treasury provenance is only proving effect plumbing, not economic execution

That’s exactly the failure mode.

✅ Adding decision_receipt_id + decision_hash to JournalEntry is the correct direction

That’s necessary groundwork. Optional fields for compatibility is also correct.

So far so good.

But: the “golden-path test” you added is not golden-path

What you described as “golden path” is:

a ledger unit test proving provenance survives serialization

That’s valuable, but it’s not the pilot proof.

The pilot proof is:

DecisionReceipt → TreasuryEffect::Spend → LedgerEntry (written) → LedgerEntry.provenance includes receipt_id + decision_hash

Until you actually write the entry in the treasury executor, you can’t prove that chain.

Right now you’ve proven: “ledger entries can store provenance if someone writes it.”

Cool. Someone still has to write it.

Two inconsistencies / red flags in the pasted log

It says it added a test named test_entry_with_decision_provenance, then it says “test wasn’t found,” then it says “the test passes.”
That’s classic “tool output compression” ambiguity. You need to confirm with:

cargo test -p icn-ledger --lib -- --list | rg decision_provenance


It claims a single commit 8a6588b1 contains both the ledger provenance additions and the casing drift fix and other changes.
That may be true, but it’s also a “bundle everything” pattern that makes review harder and increases the chance something got missed.

What you should do next (pilot-critical, minimal)
1) Wire treasury spend to produce a real ledger entry

This is the actual missing link.

Where it belongs: icn-core/src/supervisor/governance_executor.rs inside treasury execution path.

What it must do:

construct a JournalEntry (using builder)

set:

decision_receipt_id = Some(decision_receipt_id.clone())

decision_hash = Some(decision_hash.clone())

submit entry to ledger

return ledger_entry_id in result (or store it in effect result)

If you don’t currently have a ledger handle available in the executor, that’s the real integration task: thread it through cleanly (kernel-safe dependency injection style), don’t “just import ledger everywhere.”

2) Upgrade the end-to-end test to assert ledger provenance

Your earlier TODO comment is correct, but it cannot remain a TODO for pilot.

Add a test that actually executes the treasury effect path and then asserts:

ledger entry exists

ledger entry has the two provenance fields

decision_hash matches the canonical one from the receipt

3) Make casing consistent at the contract boundary

Adding #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] to two structs in governance is likely incomplete.

You need to decide your contract policy:

If gateway is the public API, then only the gateway’s casing matters externally, and governance models should not leak to clients at all.

If governance endpoints are public too, then you must apply casing consistently across all exported types (DecisionStatus, filters, trace DTOs, etc.).

Right now you’ve created a “partial fix” risk: some responses camelCase, some snake_case.

4) Add the drift tripwire (you still don’t have it)

You did not actually add a tripwire; you changed casing. Different problem.

A tripwire means: if governance model keys drift from gateway DTO keys, build fails.

Cheap version: a test that serializes default objects and compares key sets (and casing).

About /trace endpoint

You listed it as “not pilot-critical,” but: if your demo story includes trace, it’s pilot-critical.

The summit demo will live or die on:

“Show me the decision”

“Show me the spend”

“Show me the ledger entry”

“Show me the hash link”

If /trace is storybook mode (in-memory stitched), that’s a credibility trap.

Minimum safe behavior:

It can return partial traces, but it must clearly show which links are “resolved from canonical stores” vs “unresolved.”

What I want you to paste so I can review for real

Not another narrated agent log—actual diffs.

The exact diff of the ledger provenance commit:
