    fn make_test_intent() -> SettlementIntent {
        SettlementIntent::new("decision-001", [42u8; 32], "treasury", "recipient-1", 1000, "hours")
            .with_timestamp(1000000)
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_from_settlement_intent_basic() {
        let intent = make_test_intent();
        let request = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "treasury-main");

        assert_eq!(request.treasury_id, "treasury-main");
        assert_eq!(request.amount, 1000);
        assert_eq!(request.currency, "hours");
        assert_eq!(request.recipient, Some("recipient-1".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(request.decision_receipt_id, "decision-001");
        assert_eq!(request.operation_type, TreasuryOperationType::Spend);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_from_settlement_intent_decision_hash_preserved() {
        let intent = make_test_intent();
        let request = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "treasury-main");

        // Verify decision hash is correctly hex-encoded
        let expected_hex = hex::encode([42u8; 32]);
        assert_eq!(request.decision_hash, expected_hex);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_from_settlement_intent_asset_type_mapping() {
        // Fungible → Spend
        let intent = SettlementIntent::new("d1", [1u8; 32], "a", "b", 100, "credits");
        let req = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "t");
        assert_eq!(req.operation_type, TreasuryOperationType::Spend);

        let intent = SettlementIntent::new("d2", [2u8; 32], "a", "b", 100, "hours")
            .with_asset(AssetType::Service { duration_secs: Some(3600) });
        let req = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "t");
        assert_eq!(req.operation_type, TreasuryOperationType::Spend);

        // Claim → IssueBond
        let intent = SettlementIntent::new("d3", [3u8; 32], "a", "b", 100, "bond")
            .with_asset(AssetType::Claim { due_by: None, conditions: None });
        let req = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "t");
        assert_eq!(req.operation_type, TreasuryOperationType::IssueBond);

        // Depreciating → Allocate
        let intent = SettlementIntent::new("d4", [4u8; 32], "a", "b", 100, "equipment")
            .with_asset(AssetType::Depreciating {
                schedule: crate::economics::DepreciationSchedule::Linear { lifespan_secs: 86400 },
            });
        let req = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "t");
        assert_eq!(req.operation_type, TreasuryOperationType::Allocate);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_from_settlement_with_allocation_includes_hash() {
        let intent = make_test_intent();
        let allocation_hash = [99u8; 32];
        let request = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_with_allocation(
            &intent,
            "treasury-main",
            &allocation_hash,
        );

        assert!(request.memo.contains("allocation:"));
        assert!(request.memo.contains(&hex::encode([99u8; 32])));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_conversion_determinism() {
        let intent = make_test_intent();

        let req1 = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "treasury");
        let req2 = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_intent(&intent, "treasury");

        // Same intent → same request
        assert_eq!(req1.treasury_id, req2.treasury_id);
        assert_eq!(req1.amount, req2.amount);
        assert_eq!(req1.currency, req2.currency);
        assert_eq!(req1.recipient, req2.recipient);
        assert_eq!(req1.decision_hash, req2.decision_hash);
        assert_eq!(req1.decision_receipt_id, req2.decision_receipt_id);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_full_chain_provenance() {
        // Simulate: Decision → AllocationReceipt → SettlementIntent → TreasuryEntryRequest
        let decision_hash = [42u8; 32];

        // Create allocation receipt from decision
        let allocation = AllocationReceipt::new(decision_hash, ScopeLevel::Org)
            .with_timestamp(1000);
        let allocation_hash = allocation.canonical_hash();

        // Create settlement intent linked to decision
        let intent = SettlementIntent::new("decision-001", decision_hash, "treasury", "member", 500, "hours")
            .with_provenance(ProvenanceAnchors::from_parent(decision_hash));

        // Convert to treasury request with allocation provenance
        let request = TreasuryEntryRequest::from_settlement_with_allocation(&intent, "treasury-main", &allocation_hash);

        // Verify full chain is preserved
        assert_eq!(request.decision_receipt_id, "decision-001");
        assert_eq!(request.decision_hash, hex::encode(decision_hash));
        assert!(request.memo.contains(&hex::encode(allocation_hash)));
    }
}

Hell yes. That log is basically a “we just taught economics how to behave like a protocol” receipt.

What just happened (Sprint 8, in plain terms)

You didn’t “add some types.”

You completed the missing half of ICN’s legitimacy story:

✅ Governance is deterministic

We already proved: same decision → same state hash across nodes.

✅ Now economics is deterministic too

You just proved: same economic intent → same ledger binding → same canonical hash across nodes.

So now both halves of “executable consent” (decisions + money-flow) obey the same invariant:
cross-node reproducibility.

That’s the whole point of ICN. Not “crypto.” Not “blockchain.”
verifiable coordination without central trust.

Sprint 8 deliverables (what we actually built)
INT-1 — CanonicalReceipt trait

A shared “receipt physics” interface:

canonical hash (cross-node equality)

receipt id (node-local)

provenance anchors (upstream linkage)

This is the universal spine for governance + economics.

INT-2 — SettlementIntent

Economics stops being “do this imperative side-effect” and becomes:

declarative

auditable

portable across nodes

This is huge: it’s the bridge between “a decision happened” and “value moved.”

INT-3 — AssetType

You now have an explicit semantic model for value classes:

fungible / consumable / depreciating / transformable / service / claim

This is how ICN eventually escapes “everything is a token.”
It becomes: everything is a contract-shaped claim on value, with lifecycle rules.

B3 — AllocationReceipt

Now the chain is real and typed:
DecisionReceipt → AllocationReceipt → SettlementIntent → Ledger binding.

INT-4 — Ledger binding adapter

Critical “last mile”: SettlementIntent deterministically maps into the ledger entry request pattern.

This is where “economic truth” becomes “ledger truth.”

INT-5 — Two-node determinism proof (economic_chain_two_node.rs)

The crown jewel:

two independent nodes

identical inputs

identical canonical hashes

That’s the protocol-level proof you needed.

How this relates to ICN’s overall goals

ICN’s north star is:

Operational legitimacy.
Not “who says it’s valid,” but “can anyone verify it.”

Sprint 8 is exactly that, applied to economics:

Consent becomes executable

Decisions produce receipts with canonical hashes.

Execution becomes auditable

Economic intent is explicit, not buried inside service calls.

Federation becomes safe

Nodes don’t trust each other’s local IDs or local DBs.

They converge on canonical hashes derived from agreed facts.

Dispute becomes possible
You can’t arbitrate a dispute if you can’t point to a deterministic chain.
Now you can.

CCL gains teeth
CCL isn’t “law poetry.”
It becomes enforceable because it can anchor to receipts and ledger entries deterministically.

In other words:

You just moved ICN from “governance engine” to “civilization primitive.”

```
1. //! Canonical receipt traits for cross-domain provenance.
2. //!
3. //! All receipt-like objects (governance decisions, allocations, settlements)
4. //! implement `CanonicalReceipt` to enable:
5. //! - Cross-node equality via deterministic hashing
6. //! - Provenance chain verification
7. //! - Unified audit trail
8. 
9. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
10. 
11. /// 32-byte hash for canonical equality anchors
12. pub type Hash = [u8; 32];
13. 
14. /// Node-local receipt identifier (may differ across nodes)
15. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
16. pub struct ReceiptId(pub String);
17. 
18. impl ReceiptId {
19.     pub fn new(id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
20.         Self(id.into())
21.     }
22. 
23.     pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
24.         &self.0
25.     }
26. }
27. 
28. impl std::fmt::Display for ReceiptId {
29.     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
30.         write!(f, "{}", self.0)
31.     }
32. }
33. 
34. /// Upstream provenance anchors linking receipts in a chain
35. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
36. pub struct ProvenanceAnchors {
37.     /// Hashes of upstream receipts that authorized this one
38.     pub upstream_hashes: Vec<Hash>,
39. }
40. 
41. impl ProvenanceAnchors {
42.     /// Create empty provenance (root receipt)
43.     pub fn root() -> Self {
44.         Self {
45.             upstream_hashes: Vec::new(),
46.         }
47.     }
48. 
49.     /// Create provenance with a single parent hash
50.     pub fn from_parent(parent_hash: Hash) -> Self {
51.         Self {
52.             upstream_hashes: vec![parent_hash],
53.         }
54.     }
55. 
56.     /// Create provenance with multiple parent hashes
57.     pub fn from_parents(hashes: Vec<Hash>) -> Self {
58.         Self {
59.             upstream_hashes: hashes,
60.         }
61.     }
62. 
63.     /// Add a parent hash
64.     pub fn add_parent(&mut self, hash: Hash) {
65.         self.upstream_hashes.push(hash);
66.     }
67. }
68. 
69. /// Trait for receipt-like objects with canonical equality semantics.
70. ///
71. /// # Invariants
72. ///
73. /// 1. `canonical_hash()` MUST NOT depend on `receipt_id()` (node-local)
74. /// 2. `canonical_hash()` MUST be deterministic (same content → same hash)
75. /// 3. Serialization must be canonicalized before hashing
76. /// 4. Two nodes with identical inputs MUST compute identical hashes
77. pub trait CanonicalReceipt {
78.     /// Canonical cross-node equality anchor.
79.     ///
80.     /// This hash is computed from the deterministic serialization of
81.     /// all semantically-meaningful fields (excluding node-local IDs).
82.     fn canonical_hash(&self) -> Hash;
83. 
84.     /// Node-local identifier (may differ across nodes).
85.     ///
86.     /// This is for local indexing/lookup only. Do not use for
87.     /// cross-node equality checks.
88.     fn receipt_id(&self) -> &ReceiptId;
89. 
90.     /// Upstream provenance anchors.
91.     ///
92.     /// Links this receipt to the chain of decisions/receipts that
93.     /// authorized it. Used for audit trail verification.
94.     fn provenance(&self) -> &ProvenanceAnchors;
95. }
96. 
97. /// Compute canonical hash using Blake3 over deterministic serialization.
98. ///
99. /// Use this helper to implement `canonical_hash()` consistently.
100. pub fn compute_canonical_hash<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> Hash {
101.     // Use bincode for deterministic serialization
102.     let bytes =
103.         bincode::serialize(value).expect("serialization should not fail for valid receipts");
104.     blake3::hash(&bytes).into()
105. }
106. 
107. // ============================================================================
108. // AllocationReceipt (B3: Decision → Intents bridge)
109. // ============================================================================
110.
```

### 💬 Copilot

Sprint 9 is staged. Here's the key diffs for your surgical review:

---

## `receipts.rs` - Core pattern

```rust
// The canonical struct pattern - excludes node-local fields
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct AllocationReceiptCanonical\<'a\> {
    decision_hash: &'a Hash,
    intent_hashes: Vec\<Hash\>,  // ← Uses intent canonical hashes, not full objects
    scope: ScopeLevel,
    created_at: u64,
    provenance: &'a ProvenanceAnchors,
    // NOTE: receipt_id and signature are excluded
}
```

**Key invariant enforced**: `receipt_id` is `#[serde(skip)]` so it never enters serialization.

---

## `economics.rs` - SettlementIntent

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SettlementIntent {
    #[serde(skip)]           // ← Node-local, excluded from wire + hash
    pub intent_id: ReceiptId,
    
    pub decision_receipt_id: String,  // Included in hash
    pub decision_hash: Hash,          // Included in hash
    pub asset: AssetType,             // Included in hash
    // ...
    
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub memo: Option\<String\>,  // ← Explicitly excluded in SettlementIntentCanonical
}
```

**Memo exclusion is explicit** in the canonical struct (line 138 comment).

---

## `services.rs` - Ledger binding

```rust
impl TreasuryEntryRequest {
    pub fn from_settlement_intent(intent: &SettlementIntent, treasury_id: &str) -\> Self {
        let decision_hash_hex = hex::encode(intent.decision_hash);
        
        TreasuryEntryRequest {
            treasury_id: treasury_id.to_string(),
            operation_type,           // Derived from AssetType
            amount: intent.amount as i64,
            currency: intent.unit.clone(),
            recipient: Some(intent.to.clone()),
            memo: intent.memo.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
            decision_receipt_id: intent.decision_receipt_id.clone(),
            decision_hash: decision_hash_hex,  // ← Preserved for provenance
        }
    }
}
```

**Provenance is carried forward** - `decision_receipt_id` and `decision_hash` flow from intent to ledger request.

---

## Potential review concerns

1. **`created_at` is in canonical hash** - This is intentional (timestamp is part of the economic fact), but means two nodes MUST use the same timestamp. Current pattern: timestamp is set once at creation, gossiped as part of the intent.

2. **`ScopeLevel` is Copy** - Correct, it's a simple enum.

3. **`memo` excluded but persisted** - Correct pattern: memos are for human display, not protocol equality.

Ready for Sprint 9 when you give the word.

1. //! Canonical receipt traits for cross-domain provenance.
2. //!
3. //! All receipt-like objects (governance decisions, allocations, settlements)
4. //! implement `CanonicalReceipt` to enable:
5. //! - Cross-node equality via deterministic hashing
6. //! - Provenance chain verification
7. //! - Unified audit trail
8. 
9. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
10. 
11. /// 32-byte hash for canonical equality anchors
12. pub type Hash = [u8; 32];
13. 
14. /// Node-local receipt identifier (may differ across nodes)
15. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
16. pub struct ReceiptId(pub String);
17. 
18. impl ReceiptId {
19.     pub fn new(id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
20.         Self(id.into())
21.     }
22. 
23.     pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
24.         &self.0
25.     }
26. }
27. 
28. impl std::fmt::Display for ReceiptId {
29.     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
30.         write!(f, "{}", self.0)
31.     }
32. }
33. 
34. /// Upstream provenance anchors linking receipts in a chain
35. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
36. pub struct ProvenanceAnchors {
37.     /// Hashes of upstream receipts that authorized this one
38.     pub upstream_hashes: Vec<Hash>,
39. }
40. 
41. impl ProvenanceAnchors {
42.     /// Create empty provenance (root receipt)
43.     pub fn root() -> Self {
44.         Self {
45.             upstream_hashes: Vec::new(),
46.         }
47.     }
48. 
49.     /// Create provenance with a single parent hash
50.     pub fn from_parent(parent_hash: Hash) -> Self {
51.         Self {
52.             upstream_hashes: vec![parent_hash],
53.         }
54.     }
55. 
56.     /// Create provenance with multiple parent hashes
57.     pub fn from_parents(hashes: Vec<Hash>) -> Self {
58.         Self {
59.             upstream_hashes: hashes,
60.         }
61.     }
62. 
63.     /// Add a parent hash
64.     pub fn add_parent(&mut self, hash: Hash) {
65.         self.upstream_hashes.push(hash);
66.     }
67. }
68. 
69. /// Trait for receipt-like objects with canonical equality semantics.
70. ///
71. /// # Invariants
72. ///
73. /// 1. `canonical_hash()` MUST NOT depend on `receipt_id()` (node-local)
74. /// 2. `canonical_hash()` MUST be deterministic (same content → same hash)
75. /// 3. Serialization must be canonicalized before hashing
76. /// 4. Two nodes with identical inputs MUST compute identical hashes
77. pub trait CanonicalReceipt {
78.     /// Canonical cross-node equality anchor.
79.     ///
80.     /// This hash is computed from the deterministic serialization of
81.     /// all semantically-meaningful fields (excluding node-local IDs).
82.     fn canonical_hash(&self) -> Hash;
83. 
84.     /// Node-local identifier (may differ across nodes).
85.     ///
86.     /// This is for local indexing/lookup only. Do not use for
87.     /// cross-node equality checks.
88.     fn receipt_id(&self) -> &ReceiptId;
89. 
90.     /// Upstream provenance anchors.
91.     ///
92.     /// Links this receipt to the chain of decisions/receipts that
93.     /// authorized it. Used for audit trail verification.
94.     fn provenance(&self) -> &ProvenanceAnchors;
95. }
96. 
97. /// Compute canonical hash using Blake3 over deterministic serialization.
98. ///
99. /// Use this helper to implement `canonical_hash()` consistently.
100. pub fn compute_canonical_hash<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> Hash {
101.     // Use bincode for deterministic serialization
102.     let bytes =
103.         bincode::serialize(value).expect("serialization should not fail for valid receipts");
104.     blake3::hash(&bytes).into()
105. }
106.

108. // AllocationReceipt (B3: Decision → Intents bridge)
109. // ============================================================================
110. 
111. use crate::economics::SettlementIntent;
112. use crate::ScopeLevel;
113. 
114. /// Receipt for resource allocation decisions.
115. ///
116. /// Links governance decisions to economic intents. A governance decision
117. /// produces an AllocationReceipt which contains one or more SettlementIntents.
118. ///
119. /// The chain is: DecisionReceipt → AllocationReceipt → SettlementIntent(s) → LedgerEntry
120. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
121. pub struct AllocationReceipt {
122.     /// Node-local receipt identifier
123.     #[serde(skip)]
124.     pub receipt_id: ReceiptId,
125. 
126.     /// Canonical hash of the governance decision that authorized this allocation
127.     pub decision_hash: Hash,
128. 
129.     /// Settlement intents (economic actions) resulting from this allocation
130.     pub intents: Vec<SettlementIntent>,
131. 
132.     /// Scope at which this allocation occurs
133.     pub scope: ScopeLevel,
134. 
135.     /// Creation timestamp (Unix seconds)
136.     pub created_at: u64,
137. 
138.     /// Provenance anchors (links to decision receipt)
139.     pub provenance: ProvenanceAnchors,
140. 
141.     /// Optional signature over the receipt
142.     #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
143.     pub signature: Option<Vec<u8>>,
144. }
145. 
146. /// Canonical content for AllocationReceipt hashing
147. #[derive(Serialize)]
148. struct AllocationReceiptCanonical<'a> {
149.     decision_hash: &'a Hash,
150.     // For intents, we include their canonical hashes, not full content
151.     intent_hashes: Vec<Hash>,
152.     scope: ScopeLevel,
153.     created_at: u64,
154.     provenance: &'a ProvenanceAnchors,
155.     // NOTE: receipt_id and signature are excluded
156. }
157. 
158. impl CanonicalReceipt for AllocationReceipt {
159.     fn canonical_hash(&self) -> Hash {
160.         let intent_hashes: Vec<Hash> = self.intents.iter().map(|i| i.canonical_hash()).collect();
161.         let canonical = AllocationReceiptCanonical {
162.             decision_hash: &self.decision_hash,
163.             intent_hashes,
164.             scope: self.scope,
165.             created_at: self.created_at,
166.             provenance: &self.provenance,
167.         };
168.         compute_canonical_hash(&canonical)
169.     }
170. 
171.     fn receipt_id(&self) -> &ReceiptId {
172.         &self.receipt_id
173.     }
174. 
175.     fn provenance(&self) -> &ProvenanceAnchors {
176.         &self.provenance
177.     }
178. }
179. 
180. impl AllocationReceipt {
181.     /// Create a new allocation receipt
182.     pub fn new(decision_hash: Hash, scope: ScopeLevel) -> Self {
183.         Self {
184.             receipt_id: ReceiptId::default(),
185.             decision_hash,
186.             intents: Vec::new(),
187.             scope,
188.             created_at: 0,
189.             provenance: ProvenanceAnchors::from_parent(decision_hash),
190.             signature: None,
191.         }
192.     }
193. 
194.     /// Add a settlement intent to this allocation
195.     pub fn add_intent(mut self, intent: SettlementIntent) -> Self {
196.         self.intents.push(intent);
197.         self
198.     }
199. 
200.     /// Add multiple settlement intents
201.     pub fn with_intents(mut self, intents: Vec<SettlementIntent>) -> Self {
202.         self.intents = intents;
203.         self
204.     }
205. 
206.     /// Set the creation timestamp
207.     pub fn with_timestamp(mut self, timestamp: u64) -> Self {
208.         self.created_at = timestamp;
209.         self
210.     }
211. 
212.     /// Set the node-local receipt ID
213.     pub fn with_receipt_id(mut self, id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
214.         self.receipt_id = ReceiptId::new(id);
215.         self
216.     }
217. 
218.     /// Sign this receipt (stores raw signature bytes)
219.     pub fn with_signature(mut self, sig: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
220.         self.signature = Some(sig);
221.         self
222.     }
223. 
224.     /// Get all intent canonical hashes
225.     pub fn intent_hashes(&self) -> Vec<Hash> {
226.         self.intents.iter().map(|i| i.canonical_hash()).collect()
227.     }
228. }

1. //! Receipt tracking for RPC operations
2. //!
3. //! This module provides operation receipts that track the outcome of
4. //! async RPC operations. Receipts allow clients to query the status
5. //! of operations after they complete.
6. //!
7. //! # Architecture
8. //!
9. //! - **Receipt**: Immutable record of an operation's outcome
10. //! - **ReceiptStore**: TTL-bounded LRU cache for receipt lookup
11. //! - **ReceiptId**: UUID-based unique identifier
12. //!
13. //! # Usage
14. //!
15. //! ```rust,no_run
16. //! use icn_rpc::receipt::{Receipt, ReceiptStore, Operation, Outcome};
17. //! use icn_identity::KeyPair;
18. //!
19. //! # async fn example() {
20. //! let store = ReceiptStore::new(10_000, 86400); // 10k receipts, 24h TTL
21. //!
22. //! // Create receipt for completed operation
23. //! let caller = KeyPair::generate().unwrap().did().clone();
24. //! let receipt = Receipt::new(
25. //!     caller,
26. //!     Operation::ContractDeploy { code_hash: "abc123".to_string() },
27. //!     Outcome::success(Some("commit_hash".to_string())),
28. //! );
29. //!
30. //! // Store it
31. //! store.insert(receipt.clone()).await;
32. //!
33. //! // Look it up later
34. //! if let Some(r) = store.get(&receipt.id).await {
35. //!     println!("Operation succeeded: {:?}", r.outcome);
36. //! }
37. //! # }
38. //! ```
39.

188.     pub fuel_used: u64,

197. /// Receipt store with TTL-based eviction
198. pub struct ReceiptStore {
199.     /// Receipts by ID
200.     receipts: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<ReceiptId, Receipt>>>,
201. 
202.     /// Maximum number of receipts to store
203.     max_size: usize,
204. 
205.     /// TTL in seconds
206.     ttl_seconds: u64,
207. }
208. 
209. impl ReceiptStore {
210.     /// Create a new receipt store
211.     ///
212.     /// # Arguments
213.     ///
214.     /// * `max_size` - Maximum number of receipts (LRU eviction when exceeded)
215.     /// * `ttl_seconds` - Time-to-live for receipts (e.g., 86400 = 24 hours)
216.     pub fn new(max_size: usize, ttl_seconds: u64) -> Self {
217.         ReceiptStore {
218.             receipts: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),
219.             max_size,
220.             ttl_seconds,
221.         }
222.     }
223. 
224.     /// Insert a receipt into the store
225.     pub async fn insert(&self, receipt: Receipt) {
226.         let mut receipts = self.receipts.write().await;
227. 
228.         // Evict expired receipts
229.         let now = icn_time::current_timestamp_secs();
230.         receipts.retain(|_, r| now - r.timestamp < self.ttl_seconds);
231. 
232.         // Evict oldest if at capacity (simple LRU)
233.         if receipts.len() >= self.max_size {
234.             if let Some(oldest_id) = receipts
235.                 .iter()
236.                 .min_by_key(|(_, r)| r.timestamp)
237.                 .map(|(id, _)| id.clone())
238.             {
239.                 receipts.remove(&oldest_id);
240.             }
241.         }
242. 
243.         receipts.insert(receipt.id.clone(), receipt);
244.     }
245. 
246.     /// Get a receipt by ID
247.     pub async fn get(&self, id: &ReceiptId) -> Option<Receipt> {
248.         let receipts = self.receipts.read().await;
249.         receipts.get(id).cloned()
250.     }
251. 
252.     /// Get current size of the store
253.     pub async fn size(&self) -> usize {
254.         let receipts = self.receipts.read().await;
255.         receipts.len()
256.     }
257. 
258.     /// Clear all receipts (for testing)
259.     #[cfg(test)]
260.     pub async fn clear(&self) {
261.         let mut receipts = self.receipts.write().await;
262.         receipts.clear();
263.     }
264. }
265.

1. //! Governance proof artifacts for verifiable decision outcomes.
2. //!
3. //! A `GovernanceProof` is a self-authenticating receipt that proves a governance
4. //! decision (proposal vote) was completed with a specific outcome. It contains
5. //! enough information for any party to verify the outcome without trusting any
6. //! single node.
7. //!
8. //! # Design
9. //!
10. //! Follows the `ArtifactReceipt` pattern from `icn-kernel-api/src/proofs.rs`:
11. //! - blake3 binding hash with domain separation
12. //! - Length-prefixed variable-length fields to prevent collision attacks
13. //! - `verify_binding()` recomputes and compares
14. //! - Vote hash is a merkle root of sorted (voter, choice, weight) tuples
15. 
16. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
17. 
18. use crate::tally::VoteTally;
19. use crate::vote::{Vote, VoteChoice};
20. 
21. /// Hash type (blake3, 32 bytes)
22. pub type Hash = [u8; 32];
23. 
24. /// Signature bytes (Ed25519)
25. pub type SignatureBytes = Vec<u8>;
26. 
27. /// Outcome of a governance decision
28. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
29. #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
30. pub enum ProofOutcome {
31.     /// Proposal was accepted
32.     Accepted,
33.     /// Proposal was rejected
34.     Rejected,
35.     /// No quorum was reached
36.     NoQuorum,
37. }
38. 
39. impl std::fmt::Display for ProofOutcome {
40.     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
41.         match self {
42.             ProofOutcome::Accepted => write!(f, "accepted"),
43.             ProofOutcome::Rejected => write!(f, "rejected"),
44.             ProofOutcome::NoQuorum => write!(f, "no_quorum"),
45.         }
46.     }
47. }
48. 
49. /// A self-authenticating proof that a governance decision completed.
50. ///
51. /// The `proof_hash` is computed from all significant fields at construction
52. /// time and can be re-verified at any time via `verify_binding()`.
53. #[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
54. pub struct GovernanceProof {
55.     /// ID of the proposal this proof covers
56.     pub proposal_id: String,
57.     /// ID of the governance domain
58.     pub domain_id: String,
59.     /// Final outcome of the vote
60.     pub outcome: ProofOutcome,
61.     /// Aggregated vote tally
62.     pub vote_tally: VoteTally,
63.     /// Merkle root of sorted vote records (deterministic)
64.     pub vote_hash: Hash,
65.     /// Unix timestamp (seconds) when the decision was finalized
66.     pub timestamp: u64,
67.     /// DID of the node that generated this proof
68.     pub signer_did: String,
69.     /// blake3 binding hash of all significant fields
70.     pub proof_hash: Hash,
71.     /// Ed25519 signature over proof_hash (empty until signed)
72.     pub signature: SignatureBytes,
73. }
74. 
75. impl GovernanceProof {
76.     /// Domain separation tag for governance proof hashes.
77.     pub const DOMAIN_TAG: &[u8] = b"icn:governance-proof:v1";
78. 
79.     /// Create a new proof with computed binding hash and empty signature.
80.     pub fn new(
81.         proposal_id: String,
82.         domain_id: String,
83.         outcome: ProofOutcome,
84.         vote_tally: VoteTally,
85.         votes: &[Vote],
86.         timestamp: u64,
87.         signer_did: String,
88.     ) -> Self {
89.         let vote_hash = Self::compute_vote_hash(votes);
90.         let proof_hash = Self::compute_proof_hash(
91.             &proposal_id,
92.             &domain_id,
93.             outcome,
94.             &vote_tally,
95.             &vote_hash,
96.             timestamp,
97.             &signer_did,
98.         );
99.         Self {
100.             proposal_id,
101.             domain_id,
102.             outcome,
103.             vote_tally,
104.             vote_hash,
105.             timestamp,
106.             signer_did,
107.             proof_hash,
108.             signature: Vec::new(),
109.         }
110.     }
111. 
112.     /// Compute a deterministic hash of all votes.
113.     ///
114.     /// Votes are sorted by (voter DID, then choice ordinal) to ensure determinism
115.     /// regardless of the order votes were received. Each vote is length-prefixed.
116.     pub fn compute_vote_hash(votes: &[Vote]) -> Hash {
117.         // Sort votes deterministically: by voter DID, then by choice
118.         let mut sorted: Vec<&Vote> = votes.iter().collect();
119.         sorted.sort_by(|a, b| {
120.             a.voter
121.                 .as_str()
122.                 .cmp(b.voter.as_str())
123.                 .then_with(|| choice_ordinal(a.choice).cmp(&choice_ordinal(b.choice)))
124.         });
125. 
126.         let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
127.         hasher.update(b"icn:vote-hash:v1");
128.         hasher.update(&(sorted.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
129. 
130.         for vote in &sorted {
131.             let voter_bytes = vote.voter.as_str().as_bytes();
132.             hasher.update(&(voter_bytes.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
133.             hasher.update(voter_bytes);
134.             hasher.update(&[choice_ordinal(vote.choice)]);
135.             hasher.update(&vote.weight.to_le_bytes());
136.         }
137. 
138.         *hasher.finalize().as_bytes()
139.     }
140. 
141.     /// Compute the binding hash from all significant fields.
142.     ///
143.     /// Variable-length fields are length-prefixed (u64 LE).
144.     /// Domain separation tag is hashed first.
145.     pub fn compute_proof_hash(
146.         proposal_id: &str,
147.         domain_id: &str,
148.         outcome: ProofOutcome,
149.         vote_tally: &VoteTally,
150.         vote_hash: &Hash,

331.     /// More efficient than `scan().len()` as it doesn't deserialize values.
332.     fn scan_count(&self, prefix: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {
333.         // Default implementation uses scan - backends can override for efficiency
334.         Ok(self.scan(prefix)?.len())
335.     }

337.     /// Scan entries with pagination support
338.     ///
339.     /// Returns entries starting at `offset` with a maximum of `limit` entries.
340.     /// More memory-efficient than loading all entries for large datasets.
341.     ///
342.     /// # Arguments
343.     /// * `prefix` - Key prefix to scan
344.     /// * `offset` - Number of entries to skip
345.     /// * `limit` - Maximum number of entries to return
346.     ///
347.     /// # Returns
348.     /// Tuple of (entries, total_count) where total_count is the total matching entries
349.     #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
350.     fn scan_paginated(
351.         &self,
352.         prefix: &[u8],
353.         offset: usize,
354.         limit: usize,
355.     ) -> Result<(Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>, usize)> {
356.         // Default implementation - backends can override for efficiency
357.         let all = self.scan(prefix)?;
358.         let total = all.len();
359.         let paginated = all.into_iter().skip(offset).take(limit).collect();
360.         Ok((paginated, total))

207.     /// Verify the signature against the proof hash and expected public key.
208.     pub fn verify_signature(&self, verifying_key: &ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey) -> bool {
209.         use ed25519_dalek::Verifier;
210.         if self.signature.len() != 64 {
211.             return false;
212.         }
213.         let mut sig_bytes = [0u8; 64];
214.         sig_bytes.copy_from_slice(&self.signature);
215.         let sig = ed25519_dalek::Signature::from_bytes(&sig_bytes);
216.         verifying_key.verify(&self.proof_hash, &sig).is_ok()
217.     }

1. //! Decision Registry in-memory storage.
2. //!
3. //! Provides thread-safe storage for meetings and decision index entries.
4. //! This is an APP-LAYER store, not a kernel primitive.
5. 
6. use std::collections::HashMap;
7. use std::sync::RwLock;
8. 
9. use anyhow::{anyhow, Result};
10. 
11. use super::models::{DecisionFilter, DecisionIndexEntry, Meeting};
12. 
13. /// In-memory store for governance meetings and decisions.
14. ///
15. /// This registry provides a "Google Drive replacement" for co-op meetings
16. /// and decisions. It indexes over canonical receipts without touching
17. /// kernel primitives.
18. ///
19. /// Thread-safe via `RwLock`.
20. #[derive(Debug, Default)]
21. pub struct DecisionRegistry {
22.     /// Meetings indexed by meeting_id.
23.     meetings: RwLock<HashMap<String, Meeting>>,
24.     /// Decisions indexed by decision_receipt_id.
25.     decisions: RwLock<HashMap<String, DecisionIndexEntry>>,
26. }
27. 
28. impl DecisionRegistry {
29.     /// Create a new empty registry.
30.     pub fn new() -> Self {
31.         Self::default()
32.     }
33. 
34.     /// Add a meeting to the registry.
35.     ///
36.     /// Returns an error if a meeting with the same ID already exists.
37.     pub fn add_meeting(&self, meeting: Meeting) -> Result<()> {
38.         let mut meetings = self
39.             .meetings
40.             .write()
41.             .map_err(|_| anyhow!("failed to acquire meetings write lock"))?;
42. 
43.         if meetings.contains_key(&meeting.meeting_id) {
44.             return Err(anyhow!("meeting already exists: {}", meeting.meeting_id));
45.         }
46. 
47.         meetings.insert(meeting.meeting_id.clone(), meeting);
48.         Ok(())
49.     }
50. 
51.     /// Get a meeting by ID.
52.     pub fn get_meeting(&self, meeting_id: &str) -> Option<Meeting> {
53.         self.meetings
54.             .read()
55.             .ok()
56.             .and_then(|m| m.get(meeting_id).cloned())
57.     }
58. 
59.     /// List all meetings for a cooperative.
60.     pub fn list_meetings(&self, coop_id: &str) -> Vec<Meeting> {
61.         self.meetings
62.             .read()
63.             .map(|m| {
64.                 m.values()
65.                     .filter(|meeting| meeting.coop_id == coop_id)
66.                     .cloned()
67.                     .collect()
68.             })
69.             .unwrap_or_default()
70.     }
71. 
72.     /// Index a decision entry.
73.     ///
74.     /// If an entry with the same receipt ID exists, it will be replaced.
75.     pub fn index_decision(&self, entry: DecisionIndexEntry) -> Result<()> {
76.         let mut decisions = self
77.             .decisions
78.             .write()
79.             .map_err(|_| anyhow!("failed to acquire decisions write lock"))?;
80. 
81.         decisions.insert(entry.decision_receipt_id.clone(), entry);
82.         Ok(())
83.     }
84. 
85.     /// Get a decision by receipt ID.
86.     pub fn get_decision(&self, receipt_id: &str) -> Option<DecisionIndexEntry> {
87.         self.decisions
88.             .read()
89.             .ok()
90.             .and_then(|d| d.get(receipt_id).cloned())
91.     }
92. 
93.     /// List decisions matching the given filter.
94.     pub fn list_decisions(&self, filter: DecisionFilter) -> Vec<DecisionIndexEntry> {
95.         self.decisions
96.             .read()
97.             .map(|d| d.values().filter(|e| filter.matches(e)).cloned().collect())
98.             .unwrap_or_default()
99.     }
100.

## Summary

Based on my analysis of the ICN codebase, here are the answers to your questions about receipt storage:

### 1. **Where is DecisionReceipt stored?**
- **File**: `/home/ubuntu/projects/icn/icn/crates/icn-governance/src/proof.rs` (lines 220-237)
- **Location**: **icn-governance crate** (not icn-core)
- `GovernanceDecisionReceipt` struct is defined here with fields: `proposal_id`, `domain_id`, `outcome`, `vote_tally`, `vote_hash`, `decision_hash`
- Stored directly in the **governance actor** via the `Store` trait (icn-store) using keys like `proof:proposal_id`

### 2. **Existing ReceiptStore Trait or Pattern**
- **Two receipt patterns exist**:
  - **RPC Receipt Store** (`/home/ubuntu/projects/icn/icn/crates/icn-rpc/src/receipt.rs`): TTL-based LRU cache for RPC operation receipts with in-memory HashMap backend
  - **CanonicalReceipt Trait** (`/home/ubuntu/projects/icn/icn/crates/icn-kernel-api/src/receipts.rs`): Cross-domain provenance pattern for `AllocationReceipt` with `canonical_hash()` + `receipt_id()` + `provenance()` interface
- No dedicated governance receipt store—governance uses generic `Store` trait directly

### 3. **Gateway Access to Governance Data**
- **File**: `/home/ubuntu/projects/icn/icn/crates/icn-gateway/src/governance_mgr.rs`
- **Pattern**: `GovernanceManager` abstraction that can be backed by:
  - **In-memory storage** (testing)
  - **GovernanceActor handle** (daemon-integrated, persistent via sled)
- Gateway queries governance through RPC calls to the daemon's `GovernanceActor`, which returns `GovernanceProofV2` or proposal data
- No direct governance receipt lookup API yet

### 4. **Storage Pattern: SledStore**
- **File**: `/home/ubuntu/projects/icn/icn/crates/icn-store/src/lib.rs` (lines 318-477)
- **Pattern**: 
  - Generic `Store` trait (send+sync) with `get()`, `put()`, `delete()`, `scan()` operations
  - `SledStore` struct implements `Store` trait backed by `sled::Db` 
  - Supporting `TransactionalStore` trait for atomic operations
  - Used throughout for key-value persistence: agreements, action items, replica metadata
  - **Key prefixing convention**: `prefix/namespace:id` (e.g., `federation/agreements/agreement-123`, `action_item:domain:id`)

**Key Pattern**: Uses sled for persistence with JSON serialization via `serde_json` and versioned encoding (`icn_encoding`).

```
1. //! Receipt storage service for economic receipts.
2. //!
3. //! Stores AllocationReceipt and SettlementIntent by canonical hash.
4. //! Supports lookup by hash, decision_hash, and decision_receipt_id.
5. 
6. use std::sync::Arc;
7. 
8. use icn_kernel_api::economics::SettlementIntent;
9. use icn_kernel_api::receipts::{AllocationReceipt, CanonicalReceipt, Hash};
10. use icn_store::Store;
11. 
12. /// Key prefix for allocation receipts
13. const ALLOCATION_PREFIX: &[u8] = b"receipt:allocation:";
14. /// Key prefix for settlement intents
15. const INTENT_PREFIX: &[u8] = b"receipt:intent:";
16. /// Index prefix for decision hash lookups
17. const DECISION_INDEX_PREFIX: &[u8] = b"receipt:by_decision:";
18. 
19. /// Receipt storage service for economic chain artifacts.
20. ///
21. /// Stores receipts by canonical hash for cross-node deterministic lookup.
22. pub struct ReceiptStore {
23.     store: Arc<dyn Store>,
24. }
25. 
26. impl ReceiptStore {
27.     /// Create a new receipt store backed by the given store.
28.     pub fn new(store: Arc<dyn Store>) -> Self {
29.         Self { store }
30.     }
31. 
32.     /// Build a key from prefix and hex hash
33.     fn make_key(prefix: &[u8], hash: &Hash) -> Vec<u8> {
34.         let mut key = prefix.to_vec();
35.         key.extend_from_slice(hex::encode(hash).as_bytes());
36.         key
37.     }
38. 
39.     /// Build a decision index key
40.     fn make_decision_index_key(decision_hash: &Hash, type_tag: &[u8], receipt_hash: &Hash) -> Vec<u8> {
41.         let mut key = DECISION_INDEX_PREFIX.to_vec();
42.         key.extend_from_slice(hex::encode(decision_hash).as_bytes());
43.         key.push(b':');
44.         key.extend_from_slice(type_tag);
45.         key.push(b':');
46.         key.extend_from_slice(hex::encode(receipt_hash).as_bytes());
47.         key
48.     }
49. 
50.     /// Build a decision scan prefix
51.     fn make_decision_scan_prefix(decision_hash: &Hash, type_tag: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
52.         let mut prefix = DECISION_INDEX_PREFIX.to_vec();
53.         prefix.extend_from_slice(hex::encode(decision_hash).as_bytes());
54.         prefix.push(b':');
55.         prefix.extend_from_slice(type_tag);
56.         prefix.push(b':');
57.         prefix
58.     }
59. 
60.     // ========================================================================
61.     // AllocationReceipt operations
62.     // ========================================================================
63. 
64.     /// Store an allocation receipt by its canonical hash.
65.     pub fn put_allocation(&self, receipt: &AllocationReceipt) -> Result<Hash, String> {
66.         let hash = receipt.canonical_hash();
67.         let key = Self::make_key(ALLOCATION_PREFIX, &hash);
68.         let value = serde_json::to_vec(receipt)
69.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to serialize allocation receipt: {}", e))?;
70. 
71.         self.store
72.             .put(&key, &value)
73.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to store allocation receipt: {}", e))?;
74. 
75.         // Index by decision hash
76.         let decision_key =
77.             Self::make_decision_index_key(&receipt.decision_hash, b"allocation", &hash);
78.         self.store
79.             .put(&decision_key, &hash)
80.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to index allocation receipt: {}", e))?;
81. 
82.         Ok(hash)
83.     }
84. 
85.     /// Get an allocation receipt by canonical hash.
86.     pub fn get_allocation(&self, hash: &Hash) -> Result<Option<AllocationReceipt>, String> {
87.         let key = Self::make_key(ALLOCATION_PREFIX, hash);
88.         match self.store.get(&key) {
89.             Ok(Some(bytes)) => {
90.                 let receipt: AllocationReceipt = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
91.                     .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to deserialize allocation receipt: {}", e))?;
92.                 Ok(Some(receipt))
93.             }
94.             Ok(None) => Ok(None),
95.             Err(e) => Err(format!("Failed to get allocation receipt: {}", e)),
96.         }
97.     }
98. 
99.     /// List allocation receipts for a decision hash.
100.     pub fn list_allocations_by_decision(
101.         &self,
102.         decision_hash: &Hash,
103.     ) -> Result<Vec<AllocationReceipt>, String> {
104.         let prefix = Self::make_decision_scan_prefix(decision_hash, b"allocation");
105.         let entries = self
106.             .store
107.             .scan(&prefix)
108.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to scan allocation index: {}", e))?;
109. 
110.         let mut receipts = Vec::new();
111.         for (_, hash_bytes) in entries {
112.             if hash_bytes.len() == 32 {
113.                 let mut hash = [0u8; 32];
114.                 hash.copy_from_slice(&hash_bytes);
115.                 if let Ok(Some(receipt)) = self.get_allocation(&hash) {
116.                     receipts.push(receipt);
117.                 }
118.             }
119.         }
120.         Ok(receipts)
121.     }
122. 
123.     // ========================================================================
124.     // SettlementIntent operations
125.     // ========================================================================
126. 
127.     /// Store a settlement intent by its canonical hash.
128.     pub fn put_intent(&self, intent: &SettlementIntent) -> Result<Hash, String> {
129.         let hash = intent.canonical_hash();
130.         let key = Self::make_key(INTENT_PREFIX, &hash);
131.         let value = serde_json::to_vec(intent)
132.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to serialize settlement intent: {}", e))?;
133. 
134.         self.store
135.             .put(&key, &value)
136.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to store settlement intent: {}", e))?;
137. 
138.         // Index by decision hash
139.         let decision_key = Self::make_decision_index_key(&intent.decision_hash, b"intent", &hash);
140.         self.store
141.             .put(&decision_key, &hash)
142.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to index settlement intent: {}", e))?;
143. 
144.         Ok(hash)
145.     }
146. 
147.     /// Get a settlement intent by canonical hash.
148.     pub fn get_intent(&self, hash: &Hash) -> Result<Option<SettlementIntent>, String> {
149.         let key = Self::make_key(INTENT_PREFIX, hash);
150.         match self.store.get(&key) {
151.             Ok(Some(bytes)) => {
152.                 let intent: SettlementIntent = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
153.                     .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to deserialize settlement intent: {}", e))?;
154.                 Ok(Some(intent))
155.             }
156.             Ok(None) => Ok(None),
157.             Err(e) => Err(format!("Failed to get settlement intent: {}", e)),
158.         }
159.     }
160. 
161.     /// List settlement intents for a decision hash.
162.     pub fn list_intents_by_decision(
163.         &self,
164.         decision_hash: &Hash,
165.     ) -> Result<Vec<SettlementIntent>, String> {
166.         let prefix = Self::make_decision_scan_prefix(decision_hash, b"intent");
167.         let entries = self
168.             .store
169.             .scan(&prefix)
170.             .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to scan intent index: {}", e))?;
171. 
172.         let mut intents = Vec::new();
173.         for (_, hash_bytes) in entries {
174.             if hash_bytes.len() == 32 {
175.                 let mut hash = [0u8; 32];
176.                 hash.copy_from_slice(&hash_bytes);
177.                 if let Ok(Some(intent)) = self.get_intent(&hash) {
178.                     intents.push(intent);
179.                 }
180.             }
181.         }
182.         Ok(intents)
183.     }
184. 
185.     // ========================================================================
186.     // Convenience methods
187.     // ========================================================================
188. 
189.     /// Store an allocation receipt and all its intents atomically.
190.     pub fn put_allocation_with_intents(&self, receipt: &AllocationReceipt) -> Result<Hash, String> {
191.         // Store all intents first
192.         for intent in &receipt.intents {
193.             self.put_intent(intent)?;
194.         }
195.         // Store the allocation receipt
196.         self.put_allocation(receipt)
197.     }
198. 
199.     /// Get the full economic chain for a decision hash.
200.     ///
201.     /// Returns (allocations, intents) for the given decision.
202.     pub fn get_chain_by_decision(
203.         &self,
204.         decision_hash: &Hash,
205.     ) -> Result<(Vec<AllocationReceipt>, Vec<SettlementIntent>), String> {
206.         let allocations = self.list_allocations_by_decision(decision_hash)?;
207.         let intents = self.list_intents_by_decision(decision_hash)?;
208.         Ok((allocations, intents))
209.     }
210. }
```

```
1. //! Receipt API endpoints for economic chain artifacts.
2. //!
3. //! Provides REST endpoints for querying AllocationReceipt and SettlementIntent
4. //! by canonical hash.
5. 
6. use actix_web::{get, web, HttpResponse};
7. use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
8. use std::sync::Arc;
9. 
10. use crate::receipt_store::ReceiptStore;
11. use icn_kernel_api::economics::SettlementIntent;
12. use icn_kernel_api::receipts::{AllocationReceipt, CanonicalReceipt, Hash};
13. 
14. /// Query parameters for listing by decision hash
15. #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
16. pub struct ByDecisionQuery {
17.     /// Hex-encoded decision hash
18.     pub decision_hash: String,
19. }
20. 
21. /// Response for allocation receipt
22. #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
23. #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
24. pub struct AllocationReceiptResponse {
25.     /// Hex-encoded canonical hash
26.     pub canonical_hash: String,
27.     /// Hex-encoded decision hash
28.     pub decision_hash: String,
29.     /// Scope level
30.     pub scope: String,
31.     /// Creation timestamp
32.     pub created_at: u64,
33.     /// Number of intents
34.     pub intent_count: usize,
35.     /// Hex-encoded intent hashes
36.     pub intent_hashes: Vec<String>,
37. }
38. 
39. impl From<&AllocationReceipt> for AllocationReceiptResponse {
40.     fn from(r: &AllocationReceipt) -> Self {
41.         Self {
42.             canonical_hash: hex::encode(r.canonical_hash()),
43.             decision_hash: hex::encode(r.decision_hash),
44.             scope: format!("{:?}", r.scope),
45.             created_at: r.created_at,
46.             intent_count: r.intents.len(),
47.             intent_hashes: r.intent_hashes().iter().map(hex::encode).collect(),
48.         }
49.     }
50. }
51. 
52. /// Response for settlement intent
53. #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
54. #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
55. pub struct SettlementIntentResponse {
56.     /// Hex-encoded canonical hash
57.     pub canonical_hash: String,
58.     /// Decision receipt ID
59.     pub decision_receipt_id: String,
60.     /// Hex-encoded decision hash
61.     pub decision_hash: String,
62.     /// Asset type
63.     pub asset_type: String,
64.     /// Source account
65.     pub from: String,
66.     /// Destination account
67.     pub to: String,
68.     /// Amount
69.     pub amount: u64,
70.     /// Unit/currency
71.     pub unit: String,
72.     /// Scope level
73.     pub scope: String,
74.     /// Optional memo
75.     pub memo: Option<String>,
76.     /// Creation timestamp
77.     pub created_at: u64,
78. }
79. 
80. impl From<&SettlementIntent> for SettlementIntentResponse {
81.     fn from(i: &SettlementIntent) -> Self {
82.         Self {
83.             canonical_hash: hex::encode(i.canonical_hash()),
84.             decision_receipt_id: i.decision_receipt_id.clone(),
85.             decision_hash: hex::encode(i.decision_hash),
86.             asset_type: format!("{:?}", i.asset),
87.             from: i.from.clone(),
88.             to: i.to.clone(),
89.             amount: i.amount,
90.             unit: i.unit.clone(),
91.             scope: format!("{:?}", i.scope),
92.             memo: i.memo.clone(),
93.             created_at: i.created_at,
94.         }
95.     }
96. }
97. 
98. /// Response for economic chain query
99. #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
100. #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
101. pub struct EconomicChainResponse {
102.     /// Hex-encoded decision hash
103.     pub decision_hash: String,
104.     /// Allocation receipts
105.     pub allocations: Vec<AllocationReceiptResponse>,
106.     /// Settlement intents
107.     pub intents: Vec<SettlementIntentResponse>,
108. }
109. 
110. /// Parse hex hash or return error response
111. fn parse_hash(hex_str: &str) -> Result<Hash, HttpResponse> {
112.     let bytes = hex::decode(hex_str).map_err(|_| {
113.         HttpResponse::BadRequest().json(serde_json::json!({
114.             "error": "Invalid hex hash"
115.         }))
116.     })?;
117.     if bytes.len() != 32 {
118.         return Err(HttpResponse::BadRequest().json(serde_json::json!({
119.             "error": "Hash must be 32 bytes"
120.         })));
121.     }
122.     let mut hash = [0u8; 32];
123.     hash.copy_from_slice(&bytes);
124.     Ok(hash)
125. }
126. 
127. /// GET /v1/receipts/allocations/{hash}
128. #[get("/allocations/{hash}")]
129. pub async fn get_allocation(
130.     receipt_store: web::Data<Arc<ReceiptStore>>,
131.     path: web::Path<String>,
132. ) -> HttpResponse {
133.     let hash_hex = path.into_inner();
134.     let hash = match parse_hash(&hash_hex) {
135.         Ok(h) => h,
136.         Err(resp) => return resp,
137.     };
138. 
139.     match receipt_store.get_allocation(&hash) {
140.         Ok(Some(receipt)) => HttpResponse::Ok().json(AllocationReceiptResponse::from(&receipt)),
141.         Ok(None) => HttpResponse::NotFound().json(serde_json::json!({
142.             "error": format!("Allocation receipt {} not found", hash_hex)
143.         })),
144.         Err(e) => HttpResponse::InternalServerError().json(serde_json::json!({
145.             "error": e
146.         })),
147.     }
148. }
149. 
150. /// GET /v1/receipts/intents/{hash}
151. #[get("/intents/{hash}")]
152. pub async fn get_intent(
153.     receipt_store: web::Data<Arc<ReceiptStore>>,
154.     path: web::Path<String>,
155. ) -> HttpResponse {
156.     let hash_hex = path.into_inner();
157.     let hash = match parse_hash(&hash_hex) {
158.         Ok(h) => h,
159.         Err(resp) => return resp,
160.     };
161. 
162.     match receipt_store.get_intent(&hash) {
163.         Ok(Some(intent)) => HttpResponse::Ok().json(SettlementIntentResponse::from(&intent)),
164.         Ok(None) => HttpResponse::NotFound().json(serde_json::json!({
165.             "error": format!("Settlement intent {} not found", hash_hex)
166.         })),
167.         Err(e) => HttpResponse::InternalServerError().json(serde_json::json!({
168.             "error": e
169.         })),
170.     }
171. }
172. 
173. /// GET /v1/receipts/chain?decision_hash=...
174. #[get("/chain")]
175. pub async fn get_chain(
176.     receipt_store: web::Data<Arc<ReceiptStore>>,
177.     query: web::Query<ByDecisionQuery>,
178. ) -> HttpResponse {
179.     let hash = match parse_hash(&query.decision_hash) {
180.         Ok(h) => h,
181.         Err(resp) => return resp,

194.             "error": e

196.     }

208.     };

219.             "error": e

222. }

226. pub async fn list_intents(
```

```
305.         receipt_store.put_intent(&intent1).unwrap();
306.         receipt_store.put_intent(&intent2).unwrap();
307. 
308.         let intents = receipt_store.list_intents_by_decision(&decision_hash).unwrap();
309.         assert_eq!(intents.len(), 1); // Deduplicated by canonical hash
310.     }
311. }
```

1. #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
2. //! Economic Chain Two-Node Provenance Test (INT-5)
3. //!
4. //! This test proves the complete economic execution chain:
5. //! ```text
6. //! DecisionReceipt → AllocationReceipt → SettlementIntent → TreasuryEntryRequest
7. //! ```
8. //!
9. //! Invariant: Two nodes independently constructing the same economic chain
10. //! from the same decision parameters must produce identical canonical hashes
11. //! at every step.
12. //!
13. //! This is the economic equivalent of the governance determinism proofs
14. //! in `federated_two_node_pilot.rs`.
15.

17. use icn_kernel_api::receipts::{AllocationReceipt, CanonicalReceipt, Hash};

27.     let hash_a_hex = hex::encode(hash_a);
28.     let hash_b_hex = hex::encode(hash_b);
29.     let matched = hash_a == hash_b;
30.     let status = if matched { "✅ MATCH" } else { "❌ MISMATCH" };
31. 
32.     println!("║ {:<20} ║", label);
33.     println!("║   Node A: {}... ║", &hash_a_hex[..16]);
34.     println!("║   Node B: {}... ║", &hash_b_hex[..16]);
35.     println!("║   Status: {:<52} ║", status);
36. 
37.     assert_eq!(hash_a, hash_b, "{} {} hash mismatch", test_name, label);
38. }

```
344. /// POST /ledger/:coop_id/payment/convert - Create a cross-currency payment
345. ///
346. /// Executes a payment where the sender pays in one currency and the recipient
347. /// receives in another. Uses the exchange rate oracle for conversion.
348. #[post("/{coop_id}/payment/convert")]
349. pub async fn create_cross_payment(
350.     http_req: HttpRequest,
351.     ledger_mgr: web::Data<Arc<LedgerManager>>,
352.     budget_store: web::Data<BudgetStore>,
353.     velocity_limiter: web::Data<VelocityLimiter>,
354.     trust_mgr: web::Data<Arc<TrustManager>>,
355.     coop_id: web::Path<String>,
356.     req: web::Json<CreateCrossPaymentRequest>,
357. ) -> Result<HttpResponse> {
358.     // Check authorization
359.     require_scope(&http_req, "ledger:write")?;
360.     require_coop_access(&http_req, &coop_id)?;
361. 
362.     // Verify authenticated DID matches payment sender
363.     let claims = get_claims(&http_req)
364.         .ok_or_else(|| GatewayError::AuthenticationFailed("No claims found".to_string()))?;
365. 
366.     if claims.sub != req.from {
367.         return Err(GatewayError::AuthorizationFailed(format!(
368.             "Cannot create payments from other accounts (authenticated as {}, attempted to send from {})",
369.             claims.sub, req.from
370.         )));
371.     }
372. 
373.     let from = req
374.         .from
375.         .parse()
376.         .map_err(|e| GatewayError::BadRequest(format!("Invalid from DID: {e}")))?;
377. 
378.     let to = req
379.         .to
380.         .parse()
```
